claims.statement: A dwarf is a supernatural human-shaped being in Germanic folklore, commonly living in mountains or stones and a skilled craftsman.
claims.statement_id: Kurcaci adalah makhluk gaib berwujud manusia dalam cerita rakyat Jermanik (Germanic), umumnya tinggal di gunung atau batu dan perajin mahir.
claims.quote: is a type of supernatural human-shaped being in Germanic folklore. Accounts of dwarfs vary significantly throughout history. They are commonly, but not exclusively, presented as living in mountains or stones and being skilled craftsmen.

claims.statement: In early sources only males are called dwarfs, but they have sisters and daughters.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber awal hanya lelaki yang disebut kurcaci, tetapi mereka punya saudari dan anak perempuan.
claims.quote: In early literary sources, only males are explicitly referred to as dwarfs. However, they are described as having sisters and daughters, while male and female dwarfs feature in later saga literature and folklore.

claims.statement: English dwarf descends from Old English dweorg, cognate with Old Norse dvergr and Old High German twerg.
claims.statement_id: Kata Inggris (English) dwarf berasal dari dweorg (Old English), sekerabat dengan dvergr (Old Norse) dan twerg (Old High German).
claims.quote: The modern English noun dwarf descends from Old English: dweorg . It has a variety of cognates in other Germanic languages, including Old Norse dvergr, Old Frisian dwerch, Middle Dutch dwerch, Middle Low German dwerch, and Old High German twerg.

claims.statement: Prose Edda (Anderson): the dwarfs were first maggots in Ymer's flesh; the gods gave them understanding and human likeness, but they dwell in earth and rocks; Modsogner and Durin.
claims.statement_id: Edda Prosa (Anderson): kurcaci (dwarfs) mula-mula belatung (maggots) dalam daging Ymer; para dewa memberi akal dan rupa manusia, tetapi mereka tinggal di tanah dan batu (rocks); Modsogner dan Durin.
claims.quote: The dwarfs had first been created and had quickened in Ymer’s flesh, and were then maggots; but now, by the decision of the gods, they got the understanding and likeness of men, but still had to dwell in the earth and in rocks. Modsogner was one dwarf and Durin another.

claims.statement: In Eddic sources dwarfs craft Mjölnir, Sif's hair, Draupnir, Gullinbursti, Skíðblaðnir, Gleipnir, Gungnir, Brísingamen for Freyja, and the Mead of Poetry from Kvasir's blood.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber Edda (Eddic), kurcaci membuat Mjölnir, rambut Sif, Draupnir, Gullinbursti, Skíðblaðnir, Gleipnir, Gungnir, Brísingamen bagi Freyja, dan mead puisi (Mead of Poetry) dari darah Kvasir.
claims.quote: In Eddic sources dwarfs are attributed with creating magical treasures for the gods such as Mjölnir, Sif's hair, Draupnir, Gullinbursti, Skíðblaðnir, Gleipnir and Gungnir, while in Sörla þáttr they craft Brísingamen for Freyja. They further created the Mead of Poetry from the blood of Kvasir

claims.statement: The dwarf Alberich in the Nibelungenlied guards the Nibelung's treasure with the strength of twelve men.
claims.statement_id: Kurcaci Alberich dalam Nibelungenlied menjaga harta Nibelung dan sekuat dua belas lelaki.
claims.quote: The dwarf Alberich plays a vital role in the Nibelungenlied, where he guards the Nibelung's treasure and has the strength of twelve men.

claims.statement: In German literature many dwarfs turn invisible via a Tarnkappe and may be hostile or friendly to humans.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sastra Jerman (German), banyak kurcaci menjadi tak kasatmata dengan Tarnkappe dan bisa bermusuhan atau bersahabat dengan manusia.
claims.quote: In German literature, many dwarfs can make themselves invisible, typically via a "Tarnkappe" (cloak of invisibility), which has been suggested to be an ancient attribute of dwarfs. Depending on the story, they may be hostile or friendly to humans.

claims.statement: Early Old Norse sources do not call dwarfs small; legendary sagas and later folklore often describe them as short.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber Old Norse awal, kurcaci tidak disebut kecil; dalam saga legenda dan cerita rakyat kemudian mereka sering digambarkan pendek.
claims.quote: In the early Old Norse sources, dwarfs are typically described vaguely, with no reference to them being particularly small; in the legendary sagas and later folklore, however, they are often described as short.

claims.statement: Alvissmol (Bellows): the dwarf Alvis, wishing to marry Thor's daughter, is compelled to answer many questions.
claims.statement_id: Alvissmol (Bellows): kurcaci (dwarf) Alvis, yang ingin menikahi putri Thor, dipaksa menjawab banyak pertanyaan (questions).
claims.quote: the dwarf Alvis, desirous of marrying Thor's daughter, is compelled by the god to answer a number of questions to test his knowledge.

claims.statement: Alvissmol: Thor says the day has caught the dwarf as the sun shines in the hall.
claims.statement_id: Alvissmol: Thor berkata hari (day) telah menangkap sang kurcaci (dwarf) ketika matahari (sun) bersinar di aula (hall).
claims.quote: But with treacherous wiles must I now betray thee: The day has caught thee, dwarf! (Now the sun shines here in the hall.)

claims.statement: Völuspá (Voluspo, Bellows): Motsognir the mightiest of the dwarfs, Durin next; the dwarfs in the earth made many likenesses of men.
claims.statement_id: Völuspá (Voluspo, Bellows): Motsognir yang terkuat di antara kurcaci (dwarfs), Durin berikutnya; kurcaci di dalam bumi (earth) membuat banyak rupa manusia (men).
claims.quote: There was Motsognir the mightiest made Of all the dwarfs, and Durin next; Many a likeness of men they made, The dwarfs in the earth, as Durin said.

claims.statement: Scholars note the Svartálfar (black elves) seem the same as dwarfs, both living in Svartálfheimr in the Prose Edda.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana menilai Svartálfar (elf hitam) sama dengan kurcaci, karena keduanya tinggal di Svartálfheimr menurut Prose Edda.
claims.quote: Scholars have noted that the Svartálfar ('black elves') appear to be the same beings as dwarfs, given that both are described in the Prose Edda as the residents of Svartálfheimr.

claims.statement: Kurcaci (dwarf) are small people (manusia kerdil) in Norse (Nordik) mythology.
claims.statement_id: Kurcaci (dwarf) adalah manusia kerdil dalam mitologi Nordik.
claims.quote: Kurcaci (bahasa Inggris: dwarf ) adalah manusia kerdil dalam mitologi Nordik.

claims.statement: Dwarfs live in mountain caves or underground (gua, bawah tanah), see well in darkness (kegelapan), mine gold and silver (emas, perak), and are skilled smiths (tukang besi).
claims.statement_id: Kurcaci hidup di gua pegunungan atau bawah tanah, melihat baik dalam kegelapan, menambang emas, perak, besi, dan merupakan tukang besi yang mahir.
claims.quote: Mereka hidup di gua-gua di daerah pegunungan atau di bawah tanah. Mereka mampu beradaptasi di lingkungan bawah tanah dan mampu melihat dengan baik di dalam kegelapan. Di sana mereka menggali barang-barang tambang seperti emas, perak, besi, dan sebagainya. Mereka juga merupakan pembuat senjata dan tukang besi yang mahir.

claims.statement: The Codex Regius Völuspá has dwarfs come out of the earth; the Prose Edda has them form like maggots in Ymir's flesh.
claims.statement_id: Völuspá dalam Codex Regius mencatat kurcaci muncul dari tanah, sedangkan Prose Edda menyebut mereka terbentuk seperti belatung dalam daging Ymir.
claims.quote: The Codex Regius version of Völuspá records that dwarfs were produced out of the earth, while in the Prose Edda, they form like maggots in the flesh of Ymir, which became the earth.

claims.statement: In Norse (Nordik) mythology the dwarfs made the magic chain (rantai pusaka) that bound the wolf (serigala) Fenrir.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, kurcaci menciptakan rantai pusaka yang mengikat serigala Fenrir.
claims.quote: Dalam mitologi Nordik, mereka menciptakan rantai pusaka yang mampu mengikat serigala ganas, Fenrir.

claims.statement: The Simonside Dwarfs of Northumberland are said to use lights to lure people off paths, like a will-o'-the-wisp.
claims.statement_id: Simonside Dwarfs di Northumberland konon memakai cahaya untuk menyesatkan orang, seperti will-o'-the-wisp.
claims.quote: Dwarfs feature in the modern folklore of Germanic-speaking regions of Europe, such as the Simonside Dwarfs in Northumberland, who are sometimes believed to use lights to lure people off paths, akin to a will-o'-the-wisp.

claims.statement: Dwarfs feature in popular culture such as the works of J. R. R. Tolkien and Terry Pratchett.
claims.statement_id: Kurcaci tampil dalam budaya populer, seperti karya J. R. R. Tolkien dan Terry Pratchett.
claims.quote: Dwarfs continue to feature in modern popular culture, such as in the works of J. R. R. Tolkien and Terry Pratchett

claims.statement: In Snow White (Putih Salju) dwarfs are hard-working, simple and protective (pelindung); in The Lord of the Rings a race of Middle-earth (Dunia Tengah).
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng Putih Salju kurcaci pekerja keras, polos, dan pelindung; dalam The Lord of the Rings mereka ras Dunia Tengah.
claims.quote: Dalam kisah dongeng Putih Salju, kurcaci digambarkan sebagai bangsa pekerja keras, polos, sedikit serakah, penggerutu, tetapi juga pelindung. Dalam kisah-kisah The Lord of the Rings, kurcaci adalah salah satu ras yang menghuni Dunia Tengah.

claims.statement: Individual dwarfs can change shape and size; in Reginsmál the dwarf Andvari lived as a pike due to a Norn's curse.
claims.statement_id: Kurcaci dapat berubah bentuk dan ukuran; dalam Reginsmál kurcaci Andvari hidup sebagai ikan tombak (pike) karena kutukan Norn.
claims.quote: Diversity in appearance is not only seen between dwarfs throughout time and region but also with individual dwarfs, who can be capable of changing their shape and size, such as in Reginsmál, in which the dwarf Andvari lived as a pike in the water due to curse from a Norn

claims.statement: A leprechaun (Irish: leipreachán) is a diminutive supernatural being of Irish folklore, a solitary fairy, a little bearded man of mischief, and a shoemaker with a pot of gold at the rainbow's end.
claims.statement_id: Leprechaun (Irish: leipreachán) adalah makhluk gaib kecil cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore), peri penyendiri (solitary fairy), lelaki kecil berjanggut yang usil, dan pembuat sepatu dengan sepanci emas di ujung pelangi.
claims.quote: A leprechaun (Irish: lucharachán/leipreachán/luchorpán ) is a diminutive supernatural being in Irish folklore, classed by some as a type of solitary fairy. They are usually depicted as little bearded men, wearing a coat and hat, who partake in mischief. In later times, they have been depicted as shoe-makers who have a hidden pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.

claims.statement: The word leprechaun descends from Old Irish luchorpán or lupracán.
claims.statement_id: Kata leprechaun berasal dari bahasa Irlandia Kuno (Old Irish) luchorpán atau lupracán.
claims.quote: The Anglo-Irish (Hiberno-English) word leprechaun is descended from Old Irish luchorpán or lupracán

claims.statement: In Echtra Fergus mac Léti, Fergus mac Léti, King of Ulster, is dragged into the sea by three lúchorpáin who grant him three wishes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Echtra Fergus mac Léti, Fergus mac Léti, raja Ulster (King of Ulster), diseret ke laut oleh tiga lúchorpáin yang lalu memberinya tiga permintaan (three wishes).
claims.quote: The text contains an episode in which Fergus mac Léti, King of Ulster, falls asleep on the beach and wakes to find himself being dragged into the sea by three lúchorpáin. He captures his abductors, who grant him three wishes in exchange for release.

claims.statement: The leprechaun is a solitary creature whose main work is making and cobbling shoes and who enjoys practical jokes.
claims.statement_id: Leprechaun adalah makhluk penyendiri (solitary) yang pekerjaan utamanya membuat dan menambal sepatu (shoes) dan gemar bercanda.
claims.quote: The leprechaun is said to be a solitary creature, whose principal occupation is making and cobbling shoes, and who enjoys practical jokes.

claims.statement: Per McAnally, a human can capture the Leprechaun and refuse to release him until given supernatural wealth.
claims.statement_id: Menurut McAnally, manusia dapat menangkap Leprechaun dan menolak melepaskannya sampai diberi kekayaan gaib (supernatural wealth).
claims.quote: This is, he claims, the perfect opportunity for a human being to capture the Leprechaun, refusing to release him until the Leprechaun gives his captor supernatural wealth.

claims.statement: William Butler Yeats classed the leprechaun as a solitary fairy.
claims.statement_id: William Butler Yeats menggolongkan leprechaun sebagai peri penyendiri (solitary fairy).
claims.quote: The leprechaun has been classed as a "solitary fairy" by the writer and amateur folklorist William Butler Yeats.

claims.statement: According to William Butler Yeats, leprechauns' wealth comes from treasure-crocks buried in war-time.
claims.statement_id: Menurut William Butler Yeats, kekayaan leprechaun berasal dari guci harta (treasure-crocks) yang dikubur pada masa perang (war-time).
claims.quote: According to William Butler Yeats, the great wealth of the leprechauns comes from the "treasure-crocks, buried of old in war-time", which they have uncovered and appropriated.

claims.statement: Before the 20th century the leprechaun was generally held to wear red, not green.
claims.statement_id: Sebelum abad ke-20 leprechaun umumnya dianggap berpakaian merah (red), bukan hijau (green).
claims.quote: Before the 20th century, it was generally held that the leprechaun wore red, not green.

claims.statement: The Leprechaun (leipreachán) in Irish (Irlandia) mythology is a male fairy (peri jantan) dwelling in Ireland before the Celts (bangsa Kelt).
claims.statement_id: Leprechaun (leipreachán) dalam mitologi Irlandia adalah peri jantan yang mendiami Irlandia sebelum kedatangan bangsa Kelt.
claims.quote: Leprechaun (bahasa Irlandia: leipreachán) dalam mitologi Irlandia adalah sebangsa peri jantan yang mendiami daratan Irlandia. Bersama peri-peri lainnya, Leprechaun mendiami daratan Irlandia sebelum kedatangan bangsa Kelt.

claims.statement: By legend the leprechaun has a pot of gold (gentong emas) at the rainbow's end (ujung pelangi); its thief gets 3 wishes (permintaan) for its return.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, leprechaun punya gentong emas di ujung pelangi; pencurinya mendapat 3 permintaan sebagai ganti gentong itu.
claims.quote: Menurut legenda, leprechaun memiliki sebuah gentong yang berisi emas. Gentong tersebut dikatakan di letakkan di ujung pelangi. Dikatakan bahwa siapapun yang berhasil mencuri gentong emas tersebut, maka sang dewa muslihat tersebut harus mengabulkan 3 permintaan jika gentongnya ingin dikembalikan.

claims.statement: On Saint Patrick's Day (Santo Patrick), the leprechaun is said to visit people's homes.
claims.statement_id: Pada perayaan Hari Santo Patrick (Santo Patrick), leprechaun dikatakan datang ke rumah orang.
claims.quote: Pada saat perayaan Hari Hijau atau hari untuk mengingat Santo Patrick, dikatakan leprechaun akan datang kerumah seseorang.

claims.statement: The leprechaun is distinguished from the Aos Sí of the fairy mounds.
claims.statement_id: Leprechaun dibedakan dari Aos Sí penghuni gundukan peri (fairy mounds).
claims.quote: It is stressed that the leprechaun, though some may call it fairy, is clearly to be distinguished from the Aos Sí (or the 'good people') of the fairy mounds (sidhe) and raths.

claims.statement: A goblin is a small, grotesque, often malevolent humanoid of European folklore, mischievous or demonic, about 30 cm tall, furry, able to shapeshift.
claims.statement_id: Goblin adalah makhluk humanoid kecil, aneh, sering jahat dalam cerita rakyat Eropa (European folklore), usil atau iblis, kecil (sekitar 30 cm), berbulu, dan dapat berubah wujud.
claims.quote: A goblin is a diminutive, grotesque, and often malevolent humanoid creature prominent in European folklore, typically characterized by its mischievous or demonic nature, small stature (around 30 cm (12 in) in some traditions), furry or leathery appearance, and ability to shapeshift.

claims.statement: Goblins are believed to dwell underground or in households, doing anything from pranks to murder.
claims.statement_id: Goblin dipercaya tinggal di bawah tanah atau di rumah, berbuat dari lelucon hingga pembunuhan.
claims.quote: Goblins are believed to dwell in subterranean areas or households, where they engage in acts ranging from pranks to murder.

claims.statement: Gobelin was first attested in 1195 in L'Estoire de la guerre sainte by the Norman monk Ambroise; the French form goes back to Medieval Latin gobelinus, around 1140 in Orderic Vitalis's Historia ecclesiastica, for a demon expelled from a church in Évreux.
claims.statement_id: Gobelin pertama tercatat 1195 dalam L'Estoire de la guerre sainte karya rahib Norman (Norman) Ambroise; bentuk Latin (Medieval Latin) gobelinus muncul sekitar 1140 dalam Historia ecclesiastica Orderic Vitalis untuk iblis yang diusir dari gereja di Évreux (French). (Latin Abad Pertengahan, Pertengahannya)
claims.quote: which was first attested in 1195 in the chronicle L'Estoire de la guerre sainte by the Norman monk Ambroise, where it described a treacherous figure. This French form traces back to Medieval Latin gobelinus, appearing around 1140 in Orderic Vitalis's Historia ecclesiastica, referring to a demon expelled from a church in Évreux.

claims.statement: The Welsh coblyn, a knocker, derives from Old French gobelin via English goblin.
claims.statement_id: Kata Wales (Welsh) coblyn, sejenis knocker, berasal dari gobelin (Old French) melalui goblin (English).
claims.quote: The Welsh coblyn, a type of knocker, derives from the Old French gobelin via the English goblin.

claims.statement: In English and Scottish folklore goblins appear as brownies, household spirits doing night chores for an offering of porridge or milk.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris dan Skotlandia (English, Scottish), goblin muncul sebagai brownie, roh rumah yang mengerjakan tugas malam hari bila diberi bubur (porridge) atau susu (milk).
claims.quote: In English and Scottish folklore, goblins often appear as brownies, benevolent household spirits that perform domestic chores such as threshing grain, churning butter, or tending livestock during the night, provided they receive a small offering like porridge or milk left by the hearth.

claims.statement: In contrast, boggarts from Yorkshire are a more malevolent variant.
claims.statement_id: Sebaliknya, boggart dari Yorkshire adalah varian yang lebih jahat (malevolent).
claims.quote: In contrast, boggarts from Yorkshire traditions represent a more malevolent variant

claims.statement: Similar creatures include brownies, dwarves, duendes, gnomes, imps, leprechauns and kobolds; it is also a blanket term for all small fay creatures.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk serupa goblin: brownie, kurcaci, duende, gnome, imp, leprechaun, kobold; kata ini juga sebutan umum (blanket term) semua makhluk peri kecil.
claims.quote: Similar creatures include brownies, dwarves, duendes, gnomes, imps, leprechauns, and kobolds, but it is also commonly used as a blanket term for all small, fay creatures.

claims.statement: The term goblin entered English in the early 14th century from Old French gobelin.
claims.statement_id: Kata goblin masuk ke bahasa Inggris (English) awal abad ke-14 dari gobelin bahasa Prancis Kuno (Old French).
claims.quote: The term "goblin" entered English in the early 14th century, derived from the Anglo-Norman French gobelin or Old French gobelin

claims.statement: In European (Eropa) folklore Goblins are fairy folk (bangsa peri), small, sometimes unseen, little green beings with pointed ears (telinga runcing).
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa, Goblin bangsa peri, kecil, kadang tak terlihat, mungil berwarna hijau dan bertelinga runcing.
claims.quote: Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa, Goblin merupakan bangsa peri atau makhluk supranatural. Ukuran tubuh mereka kecil dan kadang kala tidak terlihat oleh mata manusia. Mereka dilukiskan sebagai makhluk mungil berwarna hijau dan bertelinga runcing.

claims.statement: Goblins are greedy and love gold (emas), are tied to fire (api), and in other versions are savage (buas), living in dark caves (gua-gua) or underground.
claims.statement_id: Goblin serakah dan cinta emas, terkait api (api), dan menurut versi lain buas serta tinggal di gua-gua gelap atau bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Mereka juga sangat serakah dan cinta emas atau jenis perhiasan. Goblin juga erat kaitannya dengan api dan memiliki kemahiran untuk menciptakannya. Menurut versi lain dalam beberapa dongeng dan kisah fantasi, Goblin merupakan bangsa makhluk yang buas dan ganas. Mereka tinggal di gua-gua yang gelap atau di bawah tanah.

claims.statement: Scholars link it to Ancient Greek kóbalos ("rogue") and to the Germanic household spirit kobold.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana mengaitkan goblin dengan kóbalos (Yunani Kuno, Ancient Greek, "rogue") dan dengan kobold, roh rumah Jermanik (Germanic).
claims.quote: Scholars propose possible etymological connections to earlier languages, including Ancient Greek kóbalos, meaning "rogue" or "mischievous sprite", which may have influenced post-classical Latin forms like cobalus denoting a demon. Additionally, links have been suggested to Germanic kobold, a household spirit

claims.statement: Goblins are sometimes classed as small pestering beings with various magical powers (kemampuan magis).
claims.statement_id: Goblin kadang diklasifikasikan sebagai makhluk kecil pengganggu dengan berbagai kemampuan magis (kemampuan magis).
claims.quote: Dalam beberapa kasus, Goblin telah diklasifikasikan sebagai makhluk kecil yang terus-menerus mengganggu dan memiliki berbagai kemampuan magis.

claims.statement: Vamana is the fifth avatar of the Hindu deity Vishnu, the first Dashavatara of the Treta Yuga after Narasimha, who in the Vedas and Puranas takes back the three worlds (Trailokya) from Mahabali with three steps.
claims.statement_id: Vamana adalah awatara kelima dewa Hindu Vishnu (Wisnu), Dashavatara pertama di Treta Yuga sesudah Narasimha, yang dalam Weda (Vedas) dan Purana merebut tiga dunia (Trailokya) dari Mahabali dengan tiga langkah (three steps).
claims.quote: is an avatar of the Hindu deity Vishnu. He is the fifth avatar of Vishnu and the first Dashavatara in the Treta Yuga, after Narasimha. First mentioned in the Vedas, Vamana is most commonly associated in the Hindu epics and Puranas with the story of taking back the three worlds (collectively referred to as the Trailokya) from the daitya-king Mahabali by taking three steps

claims.statement: Vāmana (Sanskrit वामन) means dwarf, small or short in stature.
claims.statement_id: Vāmana (Sanskerta, Sanskrit वामन) berarti kerdil (dwarf), kecil, atau pendek.
claims.quote: 'Vāmana' (Sanskrit वामन) means 'dwarf', 'small' or 'small or short in stature'.

claims.statement: He restores cosmic order and pushes Mahabali into the netherworld; he is the youngest of the adityas, sons of Aditi and the sage Kashyapa.
claims.statement_id: Ia memulihkan tatanan kosmos dan mendorong Mahabali ke dunia bawah; ia termuda di antara aditya, putra Aditi dan resi Kashyapa.
claims.quote: to restore the cosmic order and push Mahabali into the netherworld. He is the youngest among the adityas, the sons of Aditi and the sage Kashyapa.

claims.statement: Wamana is an avatar of the god Vishnu (Wisnu) in Hinduism, a dwarf priest (pendeta kerdil), son of Aditi and Kasyapa in the Tretayuga.
claims.statement_id: Wamana adalah awatara Dewa Wisnu dalam agama Hindu berwujud pendeta kerdil, putra Dewi Aditi dan Resi Kasyapa pada masa Tretayuga.
claims.quote: adalah salah satu awatara (penjelmaan) Dewa Wisnu dalam agama Hindu, yang berwujud pendeta kerdil, lahir pada masa Tretayuga sebagai putra Dewi Aditi dan Resi Kasyapa.

claims.statement: Wamana is shown as a brahmin (brahmana) in a child's body with a kamandalu and umbrella (payung), also called Upendra.
claims.statement_id: Wamana dilukiskan sebagai brahmana berraga anak kecil membawa kamandalu dan payung, juga disebut Upendra.
claims.quote: Wamana dilukiskan sebagai brahmana dengan raga anak kecil yang membawa kamandalu dan payung. Wamana kadang-kadang dikenal juga dengan sebutan Upendra

claims.statement: Wamana's story in the Bhagawatapurana, Brahmapurana, Padmapurana, Wamanapurana and other Mahapuranas: he came to King Bali's (Raja Bali) palace when Bali invited brahmins for gifts, though Sukracarya had warned Bali.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Wamana dalam Bhagawatapurana, Brahmapurana, Padmapurana, Wamanapurana, dan Mahapurana lain: ia datang ke istana Raja Bali yang mengundang brahmana untuk diberi hadiah, meski Bali dinasihati Sukracarya (Guru Sukra).
claims.quote: Kisah Wamana dimuat dalam kitab Bhagawatapurana, Brahmapurana, Padmapurana, Wamanapurana, dan berbagai kitab Mahapurana lainnya. Menurut cerita dalam kitab, Wamana sebagai brahmana cilik datang ke istana Raja Bali karena pada saat itu Raja Bali mengundang seluruh brahmana untuk diberikan hadiah. Ia sudah dinasihati oleh Sukracarya (Guru Sukra)

claims.statement: The little brahmin asked for land of three strides; King Bali (Raja Bali) granted it, and the brahmin grew until he strode over heaven (surga) and earth (bumi) at once.
claims.statement_id: Brahmana kecil meminta tanah tiga langkah; Raja Bali mengabulkan, lalu brahmana itu membesar hingga melangkah di surga dan bumi sekaligus.
claims.quote: brahmana kecil itu meminta tanah seluas tiga jengkal yang diukur dengan langkah kakinya. Raja Bali pun takabur dan melupakan nasihat Sukracarya, dan menyuruh brahmana kecil itu melangkah. Pada waktu itu juga, brahmana tersebut membesar dan terus membesar. Dengan ukurannya yang sangat besar, ia mampu melangkah di surga dan bumi sekaligus.

claims.statement: His first step trod swarga, the second the earth (bumi), and for the third Bali offered his head (kepalanya).
claims.statement_id: Langkah pertama menginjak swarga, kedua bumi, dan untuk langkah ketiga Bali menyerahkan kepalanya.
claims.quote: Pada langkah yang pertama, ia menginjak swarga. Pada langkah yang kedua, ia menginjak bumi. Pada langkah yang ketiga, karena tidak ada lahan untuknya berpijak, maka Bali menyerahkan kepalanya.

claims.statement: Impressed by Bali's generosity, Wamana titled him Mahabali and promised he would be Indra in the next Manwantara.
claims.statement_id: Terkesan kedermawanan Bali, Wamana memberi gelar Mahabali dan menjanjikan jabatan Indra pada Manwantara berikutnya.
claims.quote: Karena terkesan dengan kedermawanan Bali, Wamana memberinya gelar "Mahabali". Ia juga berjanji bahwa kelak Bali akan menjabat sebagai Indra (pemimpin para dewa) pada Manwantara berikutnya.

claims.statement: The epithet Trivikrama means three steps, referring to Vishnu's three strides in the Rigveda.
claims.statement_id: Julukan Trivikrama berarti tiga langkah (three steps), merujuk tiga langkah Wisnu (Vishnu) dalam Rigveda.
claims.quote: 'Trivikrama' त्रिविक्रम 'three steps' or 'three strides' (tri 'three' + vikrama 'step' or 'stride'). This epithet refers to the three steps or strides of Vishnu in the Rigveda.

claims.statement: The tale of Wamana Awatara and King Bali (Raja Bali) is marked yearly at Onam in Kerala (India); Wamana temples include Kerala and Kanchipuram near the Kamakshi temple.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Wamana Awatara dan Raja Bali diperingati setiap tahun dalam Onam di Kerala (India); kuil Wamana ada di Kerala dan Kanchipuram, dekat kuil Kamakshi.
claims.quote: Kisah Wamana Awatara dan Raja Bali diperingati setiap tahun pada perayaan Onam di Kerala (India). Di sana juga terdapat kuil yang khusus memuja dia (Wamana). Selain di sana, beberapa kuil Wamana tersebar di India, salah satunya di Kanchipuram, dekat kuil Kamakshi.

claims.statement: Morgan le Fay is a powerful, ambiguous enchantress of the King Arthur legend, a fairy or human, good or harmful, Arthur's sister or no kin.
claims.statement_id: Morgan le Fay adalah penyihir perempuan yang kuat dan ambigu dalam legenda King Arthur, peri atau manusia, baik atau jahat, saudari atau tak berkerabat dengan Arthur.
claims.quote: is a powerful and ambiguous enchantress from the legend of King Arthur, in which most often she and he are siblings. According to the different authors, she is a fairy or a human; beneficial or harmful; either a sister, half-sister, or unrelated to Arthur.

claims.statement: Her character may originate from Welsh mythology and other ancient and medieval myths.
claims.statement_id: Tokohnya mungkin berasal dari mitologi Wales (Welsh) serta mitos kuno dan abad pertengahan lainnya.
claims.quote: Her character may have originated from Welsh mythology as well as from other ancient and medieval myths and historical figures.

claims.statement: Geoffrey of Monmouth's Vita Merlini (c. 1150) links Morgan to the Isle of Apples (Avalon), where Arthur was carried after the Battle of Camlann, as leader of nine magical sisters.
claims.statement_id: Vita Merlini karya Geoffrey of Monmouth (sekitar 1150) mengaitkan Morgan dengan Isle of Apples (Avalon), tempat Arthur dibawa setelah Battle of Camlann, sebagai pemimpin sembilan saudari sakti.
claims.quote: The earliest documented account, by Geoffrey of Monmouth in Vita Merlini (written c. 1150) refers to Morgan in association with the Isle of Apples (Avalon), to which Arthur was carried after having been fatally wounded at the Battle of Camlann, as the leader of the nine magical sisters unrelated to Arthur.

claims.statement: Late 12th-century romance authors made Morgan Arthur's supernatural elder sister.
claims.statement_id: Pengarang roman akhir abad ke-12 menjadikan Morgan kakak perempuan Arthur yang gaib.
claims.quote: Romance authors of the late 12th century established Morgan as Arthur's supernatural elder sister.

claims.statement: In the 13th-century prose cycles and Le Morte d'Arthur she is Igraine's youngest daughter; Arthur, son of Igraine and Uther Pendragon, is her half-brother.
claims.statement_id: Dalam siklus prosa abad ke-13 dan Le Morte d'Arthur ia putri bungsu Igraine; Arthur, putra Igraine dan Uther Pendragon, adalah saudara tirinya.
claims.quote: In the 13th-century prose cycles – and the later works based on them, including the influential Le Morte d'Arthur – she is usually described as the youngest daughter of Arthur's mother Igraine and her first husband. Arthur, son of Igraine and Uther Pendragon, is thus Morgan's half-brother

claims.statement: In some variants, including Malory's, Morgan is Arthur's greatest enemy, yet she reconciles and takes him to Avalon.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi, termasuk karya Malory, Morgan musuh terbesar Arthur, tetapi akhirnya berdamai dan membawanya ke Avalon.
claims.quote: In some variants, including in the popular retelling by Malory, Morgan is the greatest enemy of Arthur, scheming to usurp his throne and indirectly becoming an instrument of his death. However, she eventually reconciles with Arthur, retaining her original role of taking him on his final journey to Avalon.

claims.statement: Medieval and Renaissance tales after Camlann show Morgan as the immortal queen of Avalon.
claims.statement_id: Kisah abad pertengahan dan Renaisans (Renaissance) sesudah Camlann menampilkan Morgan sebagai ratu Avalon yang abadi.
claims.quote: Medieval and Renaissance tales feature continuations from the aftermath of Camlann where Morgan appears as the immortal queen of Avalon

claims.statement: Morgan le Fay is Morgen in Welsh and Cornish and Fée Morgane in Modern French.
claims.statement_id: Nama Morgan le Fay dalam bahasa Wales dan Kornwall (Welsh, Cornish) adalah Morgen, dalam bahasa Prancis modern (Modern French) Fée Morgane.
claims.quote: Morgan le Fay (/ˈmɔːr.ɡən lə ˈfeɪ/; Welsh and Cornish: Morgen; Modern French: Fée Morgane)

claims.statement: Morgan le Fay, also Morgana or Feimorgan (Mittelhochdeutschen), is an important female figure (weibliche Figur) of the King Arthur (König Artus) legend.
claims.statement_id: Morgan le Fay, juga Morgana atau Feimorgan (Mittelhochdeutschen), adalah tokoh perempuan penting (weibliche Figur) dalam mitologi Raja Arthur (König Artus).
claims.quote: Morgan le Fay, auch bekannt als Morgaine, Morgain (la Fée) oder Morgana und unter weiteren Namen, zum Beispiel im Mittelhochdeutschen: Feimorgan, Feimurgân oder Famurgan/Fâmurgân, ist eine wichtige weibliche Figur in der Mythologie um König Artus, der Artussage.

claims.statement: Geoffrey of Monmouth (Geoffrey von Monmouth) portrays her as a healer (Heilerin) who could change shape (Gestalten verwandeln).
claims.statement_id: Geoffrey (Geoffrey von Monmouth) menggambarkannya sebagai penyembuh (Heilerin) dan yang dapat berubah wujud (Gestalten verwandeln).
claims.quote: Von Geoffrey von Monmouth wird sie sowohl als Heilerin dargestellt wie auch als jemand, der sich in unterschiedliche Gestalten verwandeln konnte.

claims.statement: Her modern character is often conflated with her sister the Queen of Orkney, making Morgan the mother of Mordred.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh modernnya sering dirancukan dengan saudarinya, Queen of Orkney (Ratu Orkney), sehingga Morgan menjadi ibu Mordred.
claims.quote: Notably, her modern character is frequently being conflated with that of her sister, the Queen of Orkney, thus making Morgan the mother of Arthur's son and nemesis Mordred.

claims.statement: Morgan marries Urien, has a son Yvain, becomes Merlin's apprentice, opposes knights of the Round Table and hates Guinevere.
claims.statement_id: Morgan menikah dengan Urien, beranak Yvain, menjadi murid Merlin, memusuhi kesatria Round Table (Meja Bundar), dan membenci Guinevere.
claims.quote: The young Morgan unhappily marries Urien, with whom she has a son, Yvain. She becomes an apprentice of Merlin, and a capricious and vindictive adversary of some knights of the Round Table, all the while harbouring a special hatred for Arthur's wife Guinevere.

claims.statement: A key aspect of many versions of Morgan is the unpredictable duality of her nature, capable of good and evil.
claims.statement_id: Ciri penting banyak versi Morgan adalah sifat mendua (duality) yang tak terduga, bisa baik (good) dan jahat (evil).
claims.quote: A significant aspect in many of Morgan's medieval and later iterations is the unpredictable duality of her nature, with potential for both good and evil.

claims.statement: In Vita Merlini and Chrétien de Troyes's early romances Morgan's chief role is a great healer.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Vita Merlini dan roman awal Chrétien de Troyes, peran utama Morgan adalah penyembuh agung (great healer).
claims.quote: Therein, and in the early chivalric romances by Chrétien de Troyes and others, Morgan's chief role is that of a great healer.

claims.statement: In Gallo-Roman religion Epona was goddess of horses and ponies, a fertility and mother goddess, shown riding or enthroned with foals.
claims.statement_id: Dalam agama Galia-Romawi (Gallo-Roman), Epona adalah dewi kuda dan kuda poni, dewi kesuburan dan ibu, digambarkan menunggang kuda atau duduk bersama anak kuda.
claims.quote: In Gallo-Roman religion, Epona was the goddess of horses and ponies. She was also a fertility and mother goddess, and was frequently depicted in art and sculptures either mounted on a horse, etc., (usually in sidesaddle position) or sitting on a throne with foals, or standing beside a foal.

claims.statement: She holds a patera, cornucopia, fruit or bread; she may also have been a death goddess escorting souls with her horses to the afterlife.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa patera, tanduk kelimpahan, buah, atau roti; mungkin juga dewi kematian yang bersama kudanya mengantar jiwa ke alam baka.
claims.quote: She is typically depicted holding a patera, cornucopia, fruit, bread, (wheat, grain); or accompanied by a foal or foals. She may have had a death goddess's aspect, and it is speculated that She (and her horses) might have been regarded as escorting souls to the world of the afterlife.

claims.statement: Scholars compare Epona to the Welsh legendary figure Rhiannon, also tied to horses.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana membandingkan Epona dengan tokoh legenda Wales (Welsh) Rhiannon yang juga terkait kuda.
claims.quote: Various scholars also point to the parallel between Epona and the Welsh legendary figure Rhiannon (also closely associated with horses)

claims.statement: Epona's worship as cavalry patroness spread through the Roman Empire in the 1st–3rd centuries; she was the sole Celtic deity worshipped in Rome.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan Epona sebagai pelindung kavaleri tersebar di Kekaisaran Romawi (Roman Empire) abad ke-1 hingga ke-3; ia satu-satunya dewa Kelt (Celtic) yang dipuja di Roma (Rome).
claims.quote: Epona's worship as the patroness of cavalry was widespread in the Roman Empire between the 1st and 3rd centuries AD. While adopted Celtic deities were usually only associated with specific localities, Epona was "the sole Celtic divinity ultimately worshipped in Rome itself."

claims.statement: The name Epona (Great Mare) comes from Gaulish epos (horse), from the Proto-Indo-European word for horse.
claims.statement_id: Nama Epona (Great Mare) berasal dari bahasa Galia (Gaulish), dari epos (kuda), berakar pada kata Proto-Indo-Eropa (Proto-Indo-European) untuk kuda.
claims.quote: The name Epona ('Great Mare') originates from Gaulish, an extinct Celtic language. It is derived from the reconstructed Proto-Indo-European word for horse: *éḱwos, which appeared in the reconstructed Proto-Celtic language as *ekʷos ('horse'), and later became the Celtic Gaulish epos ('horse').

claims.statement: Epona (also Epana) is a Celtic fertility goddess (keltische Göttin der Fruchtbarkeit) and the Roman goddess of horses (Göttin der Pferde).
claims.statement_id: Epona (juga Epana) adalah dewi kesuburan Kelt (keltische Göttin der Fruchtbarkeit) dan dewi kuda Romawi (römische Göttin der Pferde).
claims.quote: Epona, seltener auch Epana genannt, ist eine keltische Göttin der Fruchtbarkeit sowie die römische Göttin der Pferde.

claims.statement: Roman troops (römischen Truppen) adopted Epona as goddess of horses and cavalry (Kavallerie); in late antiquity (Spätantike) her feast was held near Mantua on 18 December (Dezember).
claims.statement_id: Pasukan Romawi (römischen Truppen) menjadikan Epona dewi kuda dan pasukan berkuda (Kavallerie); pada akhir zaman kuno (Spätantike) pestanya di Mantua pada 18 Desember (Dezember).
claims.quote: Die römischen Truppen übernahmen Epona als Göttin der Pferde und der Reiterei, wobei sie nicht nur als Schutzgöttin der Kavallerie, sondern auch der Wagenführer verehrt wurde. In der Spätantike wurde das Fest der Epona in der Umgebung von Mantua am 18. Dezember begangen.

claims.statement: According to Juvenal and Apuleius, images of the goddess (Figuren der Göttin) were worshipped in small shrines (Schreinen) by stables (Pferdeställen).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Juvenal dan Apuleius, patung dewi (Figuren der Göttin) dipuja di kuil kecil (Schreinen) dekat kandang kuda (Pferdeställen).
claims.quote: Nach Angaben bei Juvenal (Satiren 8,155–157) und Apuleius (Metamorphosen 3,27,2) wurden Figuren der Göttin in kleinen Schreinen bei Pferdeställen verehrt.

claims.statement: Epona's worship spread across the Celtic world (Celticum), attested by about 60 dedicatory inscriptions (Weiheinschriften).
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan Epona tersebar di seluruh wilayah Kelt (Celticum), dibuktikan sekitar 60 prasasti persembahan (Weiheinschriften).
claims.quote: Die Verehrung Eponas war zu Zeiten der Kelten und Gallo-Römer in der Antike bis Spätantike im gesamten keltischen Raum (Celticum) verbreitet, was durch rund 60 Weiheinschriften bezeugt ist.

claims.statement: Cernunnos is a Celtic god whose name is clearly attested only on the 1st-century CE Pillar of the Boatmen from Paris, with an aged, antlered figure wearing torcs.
claims.statement_id: Cernunnos adalah dewa Kelt (Celtic) yang namanya hanya jelas tercatat pada Pillar of the Boatmen dari Paris abad ke-1 M, dengan gambar sosok tua bertanduk rusa bertorc.
claims.quote: Cernunnos is a Celtic god whose name is only clearly attested once, on the 1st-century CE Pillar of the Boatmen from Paris, where it is identified with an image of an aged, antlered figure with torcs around his horns.

claims.statement: The name Cernunnos is applied to images of an antlered, cross-legged god with torcs, ram-horned serpents, fertility symbols and wild beasts.
claims.statement_id: Nama Cernunnos dipakai untuk gambar dewa bertanduk rusa yang duduk bersila, dengan torc, ular bertanduk domba, lambang kesuburan, dan hewan liar.
claims.quote: the name "Cernunnos" has been applied to the members of an iconographic cluster, consisting of depictions of an antlered god (often aged and with crossed legs) associated with torcs, ram-horned (or ram-headed) serpents, symbols of fertility, and wild beasts (especially deer).

claims.statement: As many as 25 Cernunnos-type images are known, mostly in north-eastern Gaul, as far as Italy (Val Camonica) and Denmark (Gundestrup).
claims.statement_id: Sebanyak 25 gambar tipe Cernunnos dikenali, terutama di Galia (Gaul) timur laut, hingga Italia (Italy, Val Camonica) dan Denmark (Gundestrup).
claims.quote: As many as 25 depictions of the Cernunnos-type have been identified. Though this iconographic group is best attested in north-eastern Gaul, depictions of the god have been identified as far off as Italy (Val Camonica) and Denmark (Gundestrup).

claims.statement: Cernunnos is read as a god of fertility, the underworld and bi-directionality; his cult from the 4th century BCE was largely unaffected by the Roman conquest of Gaul.
claims.statement_id: Cernunnos ditafsirkan sebagai dewa kesuburan, dunia bawah, dan dwiarah; pemujaannya sejak abad ke-4 SM tak banyak terpengaruh penaklukan Romawi (Roman) atas Galia (Gaul).
claims.quote: Cernunnos has been variously interpreted as a god of fertility, of the underworld, and of bi-directionality. His cult, attested iconographically as early as the 4th century BCE, seems to have been largely unaffected by the Roman conquest of Gaul

claims.statement: The Gallo-Roman Pillar of the Boatmen was discovered in 1711 under Notre-Dame de Paris.
claims.statement_id: Pillar of the Boatmen Galia-Romawi (Gallo-Roman) ditemukan pada 1711 di bawah Notre-Dame de Paris.
claims.quote: The Gallo-Roman Pillar of the Boatmen was discovered in 1711 under the choir of Notre-Dame de Paris.

claims.statement: Joseph Vendryes and Whatmough argue it read Cernennos.
claims.statement_id: Joseph Vendryes dan Whatmough berpendapat tulisannya berbunyi Cernennos.
claims.quote: Joseph Vendryes and Whatmough argue (following the Dacia inscription) that it read "Cernennos".

claims.statement: In Celtic (keltik) mythology Cernunnos is a horned god (dewa bertanduk) ruling wild places and a god of vegetation (tumbuh-tumbuhan).
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitologi Kelt (keltik), Cernunnos adalah dewa bertanduk penguasa tempat-tempat liar dan dewa tumbuh-tumbuhan.
claims.quote: Cernunnos menurut kepercayaan mitologi keltik merujuk pada dewa bertanduk yang menguasai tempat-tempat liar. Ia juga disebutkan sebagai dewa tumbuh-tumbuhan.

claims.statement: Cernunnos is nicknamed Lord of the wild things.
claims.statement_id: Cernunnos dijuluki Lord of the wild things, penguasa hal-hal liar.
claims.quote: Cernunnos juga dijuluki dengan sebutan Lord of the wild things atau penguasa hal-hal liar.

claims.statement: In the Middle Ages the Christian church (gereja kristen) used Cernunnos as a symbol of the antichrist (antikristus).
claims.statement_id: Pada abad pertengahan gereja Kristen (kristen) memakai Cernunnos sebagai simbol antikristus.
claims.quote: Pada abad pertengahan Cernunnos digunakan sebagai simbol antikristus oleh gereja kristen.

claims.statement: Cernunnos has been tentatively linked with Conall Cernach, a hero of medieval Irish mythology.
claims.statement_id: Cernunnos secara tentatif dikaitkan dengan Conall Cernach, pahlawan mitologi Irlandia (Irish).
claims.quote: Cernunnos has been tentatively linked with Conall Cernach, a hero of medieval Irish mythology

claims.statement: Lugh is a figure of Irish mythology, one of the Tuatha Dé Danann, a warrior, king, master craftsman and saviour skilled in many arts.
claims.statement_id: Lugh adalah tokoh mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology), anggota Tuatha Dé Danann, pejuang, raja, perajin ulung, dan penyelamat yang mahir dalam banyak keahlian.
claims.quote: is a figure in Irish mythology. A member of the Tuatha Dé Danann, a group of supernatural beings, Lugh is portrayed as a warrior, a king, a master craftsman and a saviour. He is associated with skill and mastery in multiple disciplines, including the arts.

claims.statement: Lugh is tied to oaths, truth, law and rightful kingship, and to the harvest festival of Lughnasadh named after him.
claims.statement_id: Lugh terkait sumpah, kebenaran, hukum, dan kerajaan yang sah, serta perayaan panen Lughnasadh yang menyandang namanya.
claims.quote: Lugh also has associations with oaths, truth, and the law, and therefore with rightful kingship. He is also associated with intelligence. Lugh is linked with the harvest festival of Lughnasadh, which bears his name.

claims.statement: His epithets are Lámfada (Modern Irish: Lámhfhada, long hand) and Samildánach.
claims.statement_id: Julukannya Lámfada (Modern Irish: Lámhfhada, tangan panjang) dan Samildánach.
claims.quote: His most common epithets are Lámfada (Modern Irish: Lámhfhada [ˈl̪ˠaːw ad̪ˠə] ; "long hand" or "long arm", possibly for his skill with a spear or his ability as a ruler) and Samildánach

claims.statement: Lugh is son of Cian and Ethniu, grandson of the Fomorian tyrant Balor whom he kills at the Battle of Mag Tuired; his son is the hero Cú Chulainn.
claims.statement_id: Lugh putra Cian dan Ethniu, cucu tiran Fomoria (Fomorian) Balor yang ia bunuh dalam Battle of Mag Tuired; putranya pahlawan Cú Chulainn.
claims.quote: In mythology, Lugh is the son of Cian and Ethniu (or Ethliu). He is the maternal grandson of the Fomorian tyrant Balor, whom Lugh kills in the Battle of Mag Tuired. Lugh's son is the hero Cú Chulainn, who is believed to be an incarnation of Lugh.

claims.statement: Lugh has an unstoppable fiery spear, a sling stone, a hound named Failinis, and invented fidchell, ball games and horse racing.
claims.statement_id: Lugh memiliki tombak berapi tak terhentikan, batu umban, anjing Failinis, dan menciptakan fidchell, permainan bola, dan pacuan kuda.
claims.quote: He wields an unstoppable fiery spear and a sling stone and owns a hound named Failinis. He is said to have invented fidchell, ball games, and horse racing.

claims.statement: Lugh is the Irish form of the pan-Celtic god Lugus; his Welsh counterpart is Lleu Llaw Gyffes; he corresponds to Mercury.
claims.statement_id: Lugh wujud Irlandia (Irish) dewa pan-Kelt (pan-Celtic) Lugus; padanan Wales (Welsh) Lleu Llaw Gyffes; disamakan dengan Mercury. (Wales)
claims.quote: He is the Irish manifestation of the pan-Celtic god Lugus, and his Welsh counterpart is Lleu Llaw Gyffes. The interpretatio romana has Lug correspond to the Romans god Mercury.

claims.statement: In Celtic myth Lugh is the chief god of the ancient Celts (Bangsa Celtic) and king of the Tuatha Dé Danann; Julius Caesar paired him with Mercury (Romawi).
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitos Kelt (celtic), Lugh dewa utama Bangsa Celtic kuno dan raja Tuatha Dé Danann; Julius Caesar menyandingkannya dengan Mercury (Romawi).
claims.quote: menurut mitos celtic adalah dewa utama bagi Bangsa Celtic kuno, raja penguasa Tuatha Dé Danann. Dalam beberapa catatan oleh Julius Caesar, ia disandingkan dengan Mercury, dewa utama dalam mitologi Romawi

claims.statement: Lugus is often called Lugh or Lug.
claims.statement_id: Lugus sering disebut Lugh atau Lug.
claims.quote: Lugus, sering disebut sebagai Lugh atau Lug

claims.statement: Lugh dwells at Tara in County Meath and at Moytura in County Sligo.
claims.statement_id: Lugh bertempat tinggal di Tara di County Meath dan di Moytura di County Sligo.
claims.quote: Ia mempunyai dua tempat tinggal yang berada di Tara di County Meath dan di Moytura, di County Sligo.

claims.statement: The ancient Celts (Bangsa Celtic) marked 1 August (Agustus) as Lughnasa, a holy day for the god (Dewa) Lugh.
claims.statement_id: Bangsa Celtic kuno memperingati 1 Agustus sebagai Lughnasa, hari suci bagi Dewa Lugh (Laugh).
claims.quote: Bangsa Celtic kuno memperingati setiap tanggal 1 Agustus yang disebut dengan Lughnasa, yang diyakini mereka sebagai hari suci untuk Dewa Laugh.

claims.statement: Some scholars derive the name from a Proto-Indo-European root meaning to bind by oath.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian ahli menurunkan namanya dari akar Proto-Indo-Eropa (Proto-Indo-European) "mengikat dengan sumpah" (to bind by oath).
claims.quote: Some scholars propose that it derives from a suggested Proto-Indo-European root *(h₂)lewgʰ- meaning "to bind by oath"

claims.statement: In war Lugh wields the lightning spear (tombak petir) Assal or Assail.
claims.statement_id: Dalam perang Lugh memakai tombak petir (tombak petir) Assal atau Assail.
claims.quote: Dalam peperangan Lugh dilengkapi dengan senjata tombak petir Assal atau Assail

claims.statement: Belenus is an ancient Celtic healing god centred at Aquileia in north-eastern Italy, tied to Noricum, attested from Italy to the British Isles, Gaul, Aquitania and Britain.
claims.statement_id: Belenus adalah dewa penyembuh Kelt (Celtic) kuno, berpusat di Aquileia, Italia (Italy) timur laut, terkait Noricum, dan disebut dari Italia sampai Kepulauan Britania (British Isles), Galia (Gaul), Aquitania, dan Britania (Britain).
claims.quote: is an ancient Celtic healing god whose cult is attested across much of the Celtic-speaking world. While his principal centre of worship lay at Aquileia in northeastern Italy, and the deity is primarily associated with the Noricum region, mentions extend from the Italian peninsula to the British Isles, including Gaul, Aquitania, and Britain.

claims.statement: In Roman sources Belenus was identified with Apollo, especially for healing and therapeutic springs.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber Romawi (Roman), Belenus disamakan dengan Apollo, terutama terkait penyembuhan dan mata air berkhasiat.
claims.quote: In Roman sources and inscriptions, Belenus was commonly identified with Apollo through interpretatio romana, especially in contexts associated with healing and therapeutic springs.

claims.statement: Tertullian and Herodian call him a protective civic deity, notably at Aquileia; his cult tied to medicinal waters, sanctuaries and oracles.
claims.statement_id: Tertullian dan Herodian menyebutnya dewa pelindung kota, terutama di Aquileia; pemujaannya terkait air berkhasiat, tempat suci, dan orakel.
claims.quote: Ancient authors such as Tertullian and Herodian describe him as a prominent protective and civic deity, notably at Aquileia, where he was regarded as the city's patron god. Archaeological and epigraphic evidence further indicate that his cult was closely connected with medicinal waters, sanctuaries, and, in some regions, oracular functions.

claims.statement: Belenus, the Latin form of Gaulish Belenos, appears in some 51 inscriptions, mostly at Aquileia (Friuli, Italy).
claims.statement_id: Nama Belenus, bentuk Latin dari Belenos (Gaulish, Galia), muncul dalam sekitar 51 prasasti, kebanyakan di Aquileia (Friuli, Italia).
claims.quote: which is a latinised form of the Gaulish Belenos (or Belinos), appears in some 51 inscriptions. Although most of them are located in Aquileia (Friuli, Italy), the main centre of his cult

claims.statement: Traditionally the name is read as 'bright one' or 'shining one'.
claims.statement_id: Secara tradisional namanya diartikan "yang cerah" atau "yang bersinar" (shining one).
claims.quote: Traditionally, the name has been interpreted as meaning 'bright one' or the 'shining one'

claims.statement: Belenus (Belenos, Belinos) was a Celtic god (keltischer Gott) equated with the Roman (römischen) Apollon; after Epona he is the Celtic deity most named by ancient authors (antiken Autoren).
claims.statement_id: Belenus (Belenos, Belinos) adalah dewa Kelt (keltischer Gott) yang disamakan dengan Apollon Romawi (römischen); sesudah Epona ia dewa Kelt yang paling banyak disebut penulis kuno (antiken Autoren).
claims.quote: Belenus, latinisierte Form von Belenos, Belinos, war ein keltischer Gott, der nach der Interpretatio Romana mit dem römischen Apollon gleichgesetzt wurde. Nach Epona ist er die von antiken Autoren am meisten genannte keltische Gottheit.

claims.statement: The etymology as a spring god (Quellgott) supports reading Belenus as a healing deity (Heilgottheit).
claims.statement_id: Etimologi sebagai dewa mata air (Quellgott) mendukung tafsiran Belenus sebagai dewa penyembuh (Heilgottheit).
claims.quote: Für die Deutung von Belenus als Heilgottheit spricht die Etymologie als „Quellgott“

claims.statement: In Scottish folklore the kelpie is a shape-shifting spirit of Scotland's lochs, also in Yorkshire; tales of these water-horses spread across the British Isles.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), kelpie adalah roh berubah wujud penghuni loch di Skotlandia (Scotland), juga di Yorkshire; legenda kuda air ini tersebar di Kepulauan Britania (British Isles).
claims.quote: In Scottish folklore, a kelpie, or water kelpie (Scottish Gaelic: each-uisge), is a mythical shape-shifting spirit inhabiting lochs in Scotland. They also inhabit meres and streams in Yorkshire (Jórvik) mythology. Legends of these shape-shifting water-horses, under various names, spread across the British Isles

claims.statement: The kelpie is a grey or white horse-like creature that can take human form, keeping its hooves, tied to Satan by Robert Burns in Address to the Devil (1786).
claims.statement_id: Kelpie digambarkan seperti kuda kelabu atau putih yang dapat berwujud manusia, tetap berkuku, sehingga dikaitkan dengan Setan (Satan) oleh Robert Burns dalam Address to the Devil (1786).
claims.quote: It is usually described as a grey or white horse-like creature, able to adopt human form. Some accounts state that the kelpie retains its hooves when appearing as a human, leading to its association with the Christian idea of Satan as alluded to by Robert Burns in his 1786 poem "Address to the Devil".

claims.statement: Almost every water in Scotland has a kelpie tale, most at Loch Ness; counterparts include the Germanic nixie, the wihwin of Central America and the Australian bunyip.
claims.statement_id: Hampir setiap perairan di Skotlandia (Scotland) punya kisah kelpie, terbanyak di Loch Ness; padanannya nixie Jermanik (Germanic), wihwin Amerika Tengah (Central America), dan bunyip Australia (Australian).
claims.quote: Almost every sizeable body of water in Scotland has an associated kelpie story, but the most extensively reported is that of Loch Ness. The kelpie has counterparts across the world, such as the Germanic nixie, the wihwin of Central America and the Australian bunyip.

claims.statement: Kelpie tales served to keep children from dangerous water and warn young women of handsome strangers.
claims.statement_id: Kisah kelpie berguna menjauhkan anak dari perairan berbahaya dan memperingatkan perempuan muda terhadap orang asing tampan.
claims.quote: but the practical purposes of keeping children away from dangerous stretches of water and warning young women to be wary of handsome strangers has been noted in secondary literature.

claims.statement: The Scots word kelpie may come from Gaelic calpa or cailpeach; the spelling kaelpie first appears in an ode by William Collins before 1759.
claims.statement_id: Asal kata Skots (Scots) kelpie tak pasti, mungkin dari Gaelik (Gaelic) calpa atau cailpeach; ejaan kaelpie pertama tercatat dalam ode William Collins sebelum 1759.
claims.quote: The etymology of the Scots word kelpie is uncertain, but it may be derived from the Gaelic calpa or cailpeach, meaning "heifer" or "colt". The first recorded use of the term to describe a mythological creature, then spelled kaelpie, appears in the manuscript of an ode by William Collins, composed some time before 1759

claims.statement: The kelpie has counterparts across the world.
claims.statement_id: Kelpie punya padanan di seluruh dunia.
claims.quote: The kelpie has counterparts across the world

claims.statement: The kelpie is the most common water spirit in Scottish folklore.
claims.statement_id: Kelpie adalah roh air paling umum dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore).
claims.quote: The kelpie is the most common water spirit in Scottish folklore

claims.statement: Kelpies appear in art and literature, including two steel sculptures at Falkirk, The Kelpies, finished in October (Oktober) 2013.
claims.statement_id: Kelpi digambarkan dalam seni dan sastra, termasuk dua patung baja di Falkirk, The Kelpies, yang rampung Oktober 2013.
claims.quote: Kelpi telah digambarkan dalam berbagai bentuknya dalam seni dan sastra, termasuk dua patung baja setinggi 30-meter-high (100 ft) di Falkirk, The Kelpies, yang rampung pada bulan Oktober 2013.

claims.statement: Some folklorists, like John Gregorson Campbell of Tiree, distinguish river-dwelling kelpies from the Celtic loch-dwelling each-uisge.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian folklorist, seperti John Gregorson Campbell dari Tiree, membedakan kelpie penghuni sungai dari kuda air Kelt (Celtic) penghuni loch, each-uisge.
claims.quote: Folklorists who define kelpies as spirits living beside rivers, as distinguished from the Celtic lochside-dwelling water horse (each-uisge), include 19th-century minister of Tiree John Gregorson Campbell

claims.statement: A changeling (auf or oaf) is a human-like creature of European folklore, a substitute left by a supernatural being when kidnapping a human.
claims.statement_id: Changeling (auf atau oaf) adalah makhluk mirip manusia dalam cerita rakyat Eropa (European folklore), pengganti yang ditinggalkan makhluk gaib saat menculik manusia. Dulu disebut dalam bahasa Inggris (English) dan dikenal di Eropa (Europe).
claims.quote: A changeling, also historically referred to as an auf or oaf, is a human-like creature found throughout much of European folklore. According to folklore, a changeling was a substitute left by a supernatural being when kidnapping a human being.

claims.statement: Sometimes the changeling was a stock of wood, more often a supernatural being magically made to look like the victim.
claims.statement_id: Kadang changeling sepotong kayu (stock) yang disihir, lebih sering makhluk gaib yang disihir menyerupai korban.
claims.quote: Although sometimes it was a "stock" (a piece of wood made magically to resemble the kidnapped human), more often the changeling was a supernatural being made magically to look like the kidnapped human.

claims.statement: Kidnappers included fairies, demons, trolls and nereids; victims were usually children, but adults too in Scandinavia and Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Penculiknya peri, iblis, troll, nereid; korbannya biasanya anak, tetapi di Skandinavia (Scandinavia) dan Irlandia (Ireland) orang dewasa juga.
claims.quote: Supernatural beings blamed for stealing children included fairies, demons, trolls, nereids and many others. Usually, the kidnapped human was a child; but there were cases, particularly in Scandinavia and Ireland, where adults were taken.

claims.statement: In Irish legend a fairy child looks sickly, does not grow, may have a beard or long teeth, and is clever beyond its years.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Irlandia (Irish), anak peri tampak sakit, tak tumbuh, berjanggut atau bergigi panjang, dan cerdas melampaui usianya.
claims.quote: In Irish legend, a fairy child may appear sickly and will not grow in size like a normal child, and may have notable physical characteristics such as a beard or long teeth. They may also display intelligence far beyond their apparent years and possess uncanny insight.

claims.statement: An inverted coat or open iron scissors where the child sleeps were thought to ward them off.
claims.statement_id: Mantel terbalik atau gunting besi terbuka di dekat anak tidur dipercaya menangkalnya.
claims.quote: Simple charms such as an inverted coat or open iron scissors left where the child sleeps were thought to ward them off

claims.statement: Some modern scholars argue these stories began as folk explanations for autism or other developmental conditions.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sarjana modern berpendapat kisah ini berasal dari penjelasan rakyat atas autisme atau kondisi perkembangan lain.
claims.quote: Some modern scholars have argued these stories of replaced children originated as folklore explanations for autism or other developmental conditions.

claims.statement: Bridget Cleary, an adult thought a changeling, was killed by her husband trying to force the fairies to return his real wife.
claims.statement_id: Bridget Cleary, dewasa yang dianggap changeling, dibunuh suaminya yang ingin memaksa peri mengembalikan istrinya yang asli.
claims.quote: Bridget Cleary is one of the most well-known cases of an adult thought to be a changeling by her family: her husband killed her, attempting to force the fairies to return his 'real' wife.

claims.statement: In medieval European superstition (Aberglauben) the Wechselbalg was an infant (Säugling) swapped by a demonic being (dämonisches Wesen) to harass and harm people (Menschen).
claims.statement_id: Dalam takhayul (Aberglauben) Eropa abad pertengahan, Wechselbalg adalah bayi (Säugling) yang ditukar makhluk iblis (dämonisches Wesen) untuk mengganggu dan merugikan manusia (Menschen).
claims.quote: Der Wechselbalg war im Aberglauben des europäischen Mittelalters ein Säugling (veraltet „Balg“), der einer Wöchnerin durch ein dämonisches Wesen im Austausch gegen ihr eigenes Kind mit der Absicht untergeschoben wurde, die Menschen zu belästigen und ihnen zu schaden.

claims.statement: In non-Christian (nichtchristlichen) belief the Wechselbalg was fathered by Druden, dwarfs (Zwergen) or elves (Elfen).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan non-Kristen (nichtchristlichen), Wechselbalg dilahirkan Druden, kurcaci (Zwergen), atau elf (Elfen).
claims.quote: In nichtchristlichen Glaubensvorstellungen wurde der Wechselbalg von Druden, Zwergen oder Elfen gezeugt und untergeschoben.

claims.statement: In Christian (christlichen) belief the Wechselbalg was a child of witches (Hexen) or the Devil (Teufels), who sought unbaptized children (ungetaufte Kinder).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan Kristen (christlichen), Wechselbalg anak penyihir (Hexen) atau Iblis (Teufels), yang mengincar anak belum dibaptis (ungetaufte Kinder).
claims.quote: Der Wechselbalg im christlichen Volksglauben war ein Kind von Hexen oder sogar des Teufels. Der Teufel interessierte sich besonders für ungetaufte Kinder

claims.statement: The term (Begriff) Wechselbalg first appears in the early 11th century (11. Jahrhunderts).
claims.statement_id: Istilah (Begriff) Wechselbalg pertama muncul awal abad ke-11 (11. Jahrhunderts).
claims.quote: Der für das Böse und Unheimliche stehende Begriff Wechselbalg taucht Anfang des 11. Jahrhunderts erstmals auf.

claims.statement: The frightened mother (Mutter) saw baptism (Taufe) as the best protection (besten Schutz) from a Wechselbalg.
claims.statement_id: Ibu (Mutter) yang takut menganggap baptisan (Taufe) pelindung terbaik (besten Schutz) dari Wechselbalg.
claims.quote: Die verängstigte Mutter betrachtete wiederum die Taufe als den besten Schutz vor einem Wechselbalg.

claims.statement: Taranis (Taranus, Tanarus) is a Celtic thunder god; the Roman poet Lucan's Pharsalia names Taranis, Esus and Teutates as gods given human sacrifice by the Gauls.
claims.statement_id: Taranis (Taranus, Tanarus) adalah dewa guntur Kelt (Celtic); Pharsalia karya Lucan (Roman) menyebut Taranis, Esus, dan Teutates sebagai dewa yang diberi kurban manusia oleh orang Galia (Gauls).
claims.quote: Taranis (sometimes Taranus or Tanarus) is a Celtic thunder god attested in literary and epigraphic sources. The Roman poet Lucan's epic Pharsalia mentions Taranis, Esus, and Teutates as gods to whom the Gauls sacrificed humans.

claims.statement: Victims of Taranis were burned in a hollow wooden container, compared with the wicker man described by Caesar.
claims.statement_id: Korban Taranis dibakar dalam wadah kayu berongga, dibandingkan dengan wicker man yang digambarkan Caesar.
claims.quote: in particular, that the victims of Taranis were burned in a hollow wooden container. This sacrifice has been compared with the wicker man described by Caesar.

claims.statement: The scholia say the Romans equated Taranis with Dis Pater or Jupiter; scholars prefer Jupiter, as inscriptions agree.
claims.statement_id: Scholia (scholia) menyebut orang Romawi (Romans) menyamakan Taranis dengan Dis Pater atau Jupiter; sarjana lebih menyukai Jupiter karena prasasti juga demikian.
claims.quote: These scholia also tell us that Taranis was perhaps either equated by the Romans with Dis Pater, Roman god of the underworld, or Jupiter, Roman god of weather. Scholars have preferred the latter equation to the former, as Taranis is also equated with Jupiter in inscriptions.

claims.statement: The Celtic wheel god is shown with a spoked wheel and Jupiter's attributes, including a thunderbolt.
claims.statement_id: Dewa roda (wheel god) Kelt digambarkan dengan roda berjari-jari dan atribut Jupiter, termasuk petir (thunderbolt).
claims.quote: This god, known only from iconographic sources, is depicted with a spoked wheel and the attributes of Jupiter (including a thunderbolt).

claims.statement: Inscriptions to Taranis date from the 4th century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
claims.statement_id: Prasasti pemujaan Taranis berasal dari abad ke-4 SM hingga abad ke-3 M.
claims.quote: Various inscriptions attest to Taranis's worship, dating between the 4th century BCE and the 3rd century CE.

claims.statement: A dedication to Iovi Tanaro (Jupiter Tanaris) in Dalmatia confirms the form Tanaris; so does the Chester altar (154 AD).
claims.statement_id: Persembahan kepada Iovi Tanaro (Jupiter Tanaris) di Dalmatia (Dalmatia) membuktikan bentuk Tanaris; altar Chester (154 M) juga.
claims.quote: The issue was settled by the discovery of a dedication to Iovi Tanaro ('Jupiter Tanaris') in Dalmatia, which confirms that this form did exist.

claims.statement: Taranis is a Celtic god (keltischer Gott) of sky (Himmels), weather (Wetters) and thunder (Donners); in Lucan he stood with Teutates and Esus atop the Celtic pantheon.
claims.statement_id: Taranis adalah dewa Kelt (keltischer Gott) langit (Himmels), cuaca (Wetters), dan guntur (Donners); menurut Lucan ia di puncak dunia dewa Kelt bersama Teutates dan Esus.
claims.quote: Taranis ist ein keltischer Gott des Himmels, des Wetters und des Donners. Dem römischen Dichter Lucan zufolge stand er mit Teutates und Esus an der Spitze der keltischen Götterwelt.

claims.statement: The name Taranis comes from proto-Celtic *torano- (thunder), cognate with Old Irish torann and Middle Welsh taran.
claims.statement_id: Nama Taranis dari Proto-Kelt (proto-Celtic) *torano- (guntur, thunder), sekerabat dengan torann (Old Irish, Irlandia Kuno) dan taran (Middle Welsh, Wales).
claims.quote: The name Taranis derives from proto-Celtic *torano- ("thunder"), which in turn derives from the proto-Indo-European root *(s)tenh₂- ("to thunder"). Through this proto-Celtic etymon, the theonym is cognate with words for thunder in Old Irish (torann ), Old Breton (taran ), Middle Welsh (taran )

claims.statement: Taranis's name corresponds etymologically to the Germanic god Donar (Thor).
claims.statement_id: Nama Taranis sepadan secara etimologis dengan dewa Jermanik (Germanic) Donar (Thor).
claims.quote: Taranis's name corresponds etymologically to that of the Germanic god Donar (i.e., Thor).

claims.statement: Brigid is a goddess of pre-Christian Ireland, one of the Tuatha Dé Danann, daughter of the Dagda, wife of Bres, mother of Ruadán, tied to wisdom, poetry, healing, protection and smithing.
claims.statement_id: Brigid adalah dewi Irlandia (Ireland) pra-Kristen, anggota Tuatha Dé Danann, putri Dagda, istri Bres, ibu Ruadán, terkait kebijaksanaan, puisi, penyembuhan, perlindungan, dan pandai besi.
claims.quote: is a goddess of pre-Christian Ireland. She appears in Irish mythology as a member of the Tuatha Dé Danann, the daughter of the Dagda and wife of Bres, with whom she had a son named Ruadán. She is associated with wisdom, poetry, healing, protection, smithing and domesticated animals.

claims.statement: Cormac's Glossary of the 9th century calls Brigid the goddess poets adored, with sisters Brigid the healer and Brigid the smith; perhaps a triple deity.
claims.statement_id: Cormac's Glossary abad ke-9 menyebut Brigid dewi pujaan penyair dan saudarinya Brigid penyembuh dan Brigid pandai besi; mungkin dewi tiga rupa (triple deity).
claims.quote: Cormac's Glossary, written in the 9th century by Christian monks, says that Brigid was "the goddess whom poets adored" and that she had two sisters: Brigid the healer and Brigid the smith. This suggests she may have been a triple deity.

claims.statement: Saint Brigid shares the goddess's attributes; her 1 February feast was originally Imbolc, so the saint may be a Christianization of the goddess.
claims.statement_id: Santa Brigid (Saint Brigid) berbagi atribut sang dewi; hari rayanya 1 Februari (February) semula Imbolc, sehingga sang santa dianggap kristenisasi sang dewi.
claims.quote: Saint Brigid shares many of the goddess's attributes and her feast day, 1 February, was originally a festival called Imbolc. It has thus been argued that the saint is a Christianization of the goddess

claims.statement: The name comes from Proto-Celtic *Brigantī, "the high one", cognate with the ancient British goddess Brigantia.
claims.statement_id: Nama Brigid dari Proto-Kelt (Proto-Celtic) *Brigantī, "yang tinggi", sekerabat dengan dewi Britania (British) Brigantia.
claims.quote: The name comes from Proto-Celtic *Brigantī and means "the high one" or "the exalted one". It is cognate with the name of the ancient British goddess Brigantia

claims.statement: Middle Irish Brigit became Brighid and, after the 1948 spelling reform, Bríd.
claims.statement_id: Brigit (Middle Irish) menjadi Brighid, dan sejak reformasi ejaan 1948 dibakukan menjadi Bríd.
claims.quote: Middle Irish Brigit [ˈbʲɾʲiʝidʲ] evolved into early modern Irish Brighid [bʲɾʲiːdʲ] and, after a spelling reform in 1948, the spelling was standardised as Bríd

claims.statement: Her sanctuary (Heiligtum) was at Kildare (Irland) where her sacred fire (heiliges Feuer) was kept; her Welsh name (walisischer Name) is Ffraid.
claims.statement_id: Tempat sucinya (Heiligtum) di Kildare (Irland, Irlandia), tempat api sucinya (heiliges Feuer) dijaga; nama Wales (walisischer Name) Ffraid. (Wales)
claims.quote: Ihr Heiligtum war in Kildare (Irland), wo ihr heiliges Feuer gehütet wurde. Ihr walisischer Name lautet Ffraid

claims.statement: Brigid personifies poetry (Dichtkunst), protects poets (Poeten), is worshipped in threefold form (dreifacher Gestalt), and is patron of lawgivers (Gesetzgeber), healing (Heilkunst), fertility and smiths (Schmiede).
claims.statement_id: Brigid personifikasi puisi (Dichtkunst), pelindung penyair (Poeten), dipuja dalam tiga wujud (dreifacher Gestalt), dan pelindung pembuat hukum (Gesetzgeber), penyembuhan (Heilkunst), kesuburan, dan pandai besi (Schmiede).
claims.quote: Sie soll eine Personifikation der Dichtkunst und Beschützerin der Poeten gewesen sein und wurde in dreifacher Gestalt verehrt, weshalb manchmal von den „drei Brigids“ die Rede ist. Zusammen mit ihren beiden „Schwestern“ wird sie noch dazu als Schutzgöttin der Gesetzgeber, der Heilkunst, der Fruchtbarkeit und der Schmiede gesehen.

claims.statement: The Morrígan (Mórrígan, Morrígu, Mór-ríoghan) is a figure of Irish mythology, "great queen" or "phantom queen", tied to war and fate, foretelling doom, death or victory, often as a crow, the badb.
claims.statement_id: Morrígan (Mórrígan, Morrígu, Mór-ríoghan) adalah tokoh mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology), "ratu agung" atau "ratu hantu", terkait perang dan takdir, meramalkan malapetaka, kematian, atau kemenangan, sering sebagai gagak (crow), badb.
claims.quote: The Morrígan or Mórrígan, also known as Morrígu, is a figure from Irish mythology. The name is Mór-ríoghan in modern Irish before the spelling reform, and it has been translated as "great queen" or "phantom queen". The Morrígan is mainly associated with war and fate, especially with foretelling doom, death, or victory in battle. In this role she often appears as a crow, the badb.

claims.statement: The Morrígan spurs warriors to brave deeds, frightens their foes and washes the bloodstained clothes of those fated to die.
claims.statement_id: Morrígan mendorong pejuang berani, menakuti musuh, dan mencuci pakaian berlumur darah milik yang ditakdirkan mati.
claims.quote: The Morrígan encourages warriors to do brave deeds, strikes fear into their enemies, and is portrayed washing the bloodstained clothes of those fated to die.

claims.statement: She is seen as a goddess of battle and war, and as a form of the earth and sovereignty goddess, guardian of land and people.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipandang sebagai dewi pertempuran dan perang, juga wujud dewi bumi dan kedaulatan, penjaga wilayah dan rakyat.
claims.quote: She is most frequently seen as a goddess of battle and war and has also been seen as a manifestation of the earth- and sovereignty-goddess, chiefly representing the goddess's role as guardian of the territory and its people.

claims.statement: The Morrígan is often three sisters, the three Morrígna: Badb, Macha and the Morrigan, who may be named Anu, perhaps names of one goddess.
claims.statement_id: Morrígan sering digambarkan sebagai tiga bersaudari (three Morrígna): Badb, Macha, dan Morrigan yang mungkin bernama Anu, mungkin nama dewi yang sama.
claims.quote: The Morrígan is often described as a trio of individuals, all sisters, called "the three Morrígna". In mythology membership of the triad is given as Badb, Macha, and the Morrigan, who may be named Anu. It is believed that these were all names for the same goddess.

claims.statement: The Morrígan is described as the envious wife of The Dagda and a shape-shifting goddess.
claims.statement_id: Morrígan digambarkan sebagai istri Dagda (The Dagda) yang pencemburu dan dewi yang berubah wujud.
claims.quote: The Morrígan is described as the envious wife of The Dagda and a shape-shifting goddess

claims.statement: She is associated with the banshee of later folklore.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan banshee dalam cerita rakyat kemudian.
claims.quote: She is associated with the banshee of later folklore.

claims.statement: The Morrigan can become a fair maiden, war leader, old woman, crow or vulture (burung bangkai).
claims.statement_id: Morrigan dapat menjelma gadis rupawan, pemimpin pasukan, nenek tua, burung gagak, atau burung bangkai (hering).
claims.quote: Ia dapat mengubah wujudnya menjadi seorang gadis rupawan, pemimpin pasukan, nenek tua, dan burung gagak maupun burung bangkai (hering).

claims.statement: As a black crow (gagak hitam) she flies over the battlefield (medan perang) shrieking and foretells the outcome (hasil peperangan).
claims.statement_id: Sebagai gagak hitam ia terbang di atas medan perang sambil melengking dan meramalkan hasil peperangan.
claims.quote: Citra gagak hitam sering muncul dalam suatu peperangan yang mana ia terbang diatas medan perang sambil mengeluarkan lengkingannya dan mampu meramalkan hasil peperangan tersebut.

claims.statement: Mor may come from an Indo-European root of terror, akin to Old English maere (in nightmare) and Scandinavian mara.
claims.statement_id: Unsur Mor mungkin dari akar Indo-Eropa (Indo-European) bermakna teror, sekerabat dengan maere (Old English, Inggris Kuno) dalam kata nightmare dan mara Skandinavia (Scandinavian).
claims.quote: Mor may derive from an Indo-European root connoting terror, monstrousness, cognate with the Old English maere (which survives in the modern English word "nightmare") and the Scandinavian mara

claims.statement: The earliest sources are glosses in Latin manuscripts; the 8th-century O'Mulconry's Glossary names Macha one of the three morrígna.
claims.statement_id: Sumber tertua adalah glos dalam naskah Latin (Latin); O'Mulconry's Glossary abad ke-8 menyebut Macha salah satu tiga morrígna.
claims.quote: The earliest sources for the Morrígan are glosses in Latin manuscripts and glossaries (collections of glosses). The 8th century O'Mulconry's Glossary says that Macha is one of the three morrígna.

claims.statement: Rígan means queen; Morrígan is read as Phantom Queen, the derivation now favoured.
claims.statement_id: Rígan berarti ratu (queen); Morrígan diartikan Ratu Hantu (Phantom Queen), tafsiran yang paling diterima kini.
claims.quote: while rígan translates as "queen". This etymological sequence can be reconstructed in the Proto-Celtic language as *Moro-rīganī-s. Accordingly, Morrígan is often translated as "Phantom Queen". This is the derivation generally favoured in current scholarship.

claims.statement: Danu is presumed a goddess of Irish mythology, attested only in the name Tuatha Dé Danann; Victorian folklorists gave her traits of motherhood and prosperity.
claims.statement_id: Danu diduga dewi mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology), hanya tercatat dalam nama Tuatha Dé Danann; folkloris era Victoria (Victorian) memberinya sifat keibuan dan kemakmuran.
claims.quote: is presumed to have been a goddess in Irish mythology, whose sole attestation is in the name of the Tuatha Dé Danann, which is usually translated 'the folk of the goddess Danu'. Despite the complete absence of any such figure from the primary texts, some later Victorian folklorists attempted to ascribe certain attributes to Danu, such as association with motherhood or agricultural prosperity.

claims.statement: The form *Danu is not in any medieval Irish text but is reconstructed from the genitive Danann.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk *Danu tak ditemukan dalam teks Irlandia (Irish) abad pertengahan, melainkan rekonstruksi dari genitif Danann.
claims.quote: The hypothetical nominative form of the name, *Danu, is not found in any medieval Irish text, but is rather a reconstruction by modern scholars based on the genitive Danann (also spelled Donand or Danand), which is the only form attested in the primary sources

claims.statement: In Irish mythology Anu is a goddess, distinct or another name for Danu.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish), Anu adalah dewi tersendiri atau nama lain Danu.
claims.quote: In Irish mythology, Anu (sometimes declined as Anann or Anand) is a goddess. She may be a distinct goddess in her own right or an alternative name for Danu

claims.statement: Cormac's Glossary, older than the Lebor Gabala Erenn, names Anu mother of the gods; some scholars merge Danu with Anu.
claims.statement_id: Cormac's Glossary, lebih tua dari Lebor Gabala Erenn, menyebut Anu ibu para dewa; sebagian sarjana menyamakan Danu dengan Anu.
