claims.quote: Cormac's Glossary, a text that predates the Lebor Gabala Erenn, names the goddess Anu as the mother of the gods. Some scholars suggest that Danu was a conflation of Anu and is the same goddess.

claims.statement: No myths or legends about Danu survive in medieval Irish texts.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada mitos atau legenda tentang Danu dalam teks Irlandia (Irish) abad pertengahan.
claims.quote: Danu has no surviving myths or legends associated with her in any of the medieval Irish texts.

claims.statement: Early scholars linked it to the Vedic water goddess Danu from a Proto-Indo-European root to flow, perhaps behind the river name Danube.
claims.statement_id: Sarjana awal mengaitkannya dengan dewi air Weda (Vedic) Danu dari akar Proto-Indo-Eropa (Proto-Indo-European) "mengalir", mungkin juga asal nama sungai Danube.
claims.quote: with some earlier scholars favoring a link with the Vedic water goddess Danu, whose name is derived from the Proto-Indo-European root *dʰenh₂- "to run, to flow", which may also lie behind the ancient name for the river Danube

claims.statement: The name (Name) Danu never appears in Old Irish mythology (altirischen Mythologie) but is inferred from Túatha Dé Danann and Tri Dée Dána.
claims.statement_id: Nama (Name) Danu tak pernah muncul dalam mitologi Irlandia Kuno (altirischen Mythologie), tetapi disimpulkan dari Túatha Dé Danann dan Tri Dée Dána.
claims.quote: Der Name Danu selbst taucht in der altirischen Mythologie als solcher niemals auf, wird aber aus den tradierten Begriffen Túatha Dé Danann („Die Stämme der Göttin Danu“) und Tri Dée Dána („Die drei Götter von Dána“) abgeleitet.

claims.statement: Danu may parallel the Welsh legendary figure Dôn of the Mabinogion, seen as a mother goddess.
claims.statement_id: Danu mungkin sepadan dengan tokoh legenda Wales (Welsh) Dôn dalam Mabinogion, yang dianggap dewi ibu.
claims.quote: She has possible parallels with the Welsh legendary figure Dôn in the medieval tales of the Mabinogion, whom most modern scholars consider to be a mythological mother goddess.

claims.statement: This may also link Danu to The Morrígan, which some scholars call an epithet of Anu.
claims.statement_id: Hal ini mungkin juga menghubungkan Danu dengan The Morrígan, yang oleh sebagian sarjana dianggap julukan Anu.
claims.quote: This may also connect Danu to The Morrígan, which some scholars say is an epithet for Anu.

claims.statement: The Dagda is the great god of Irish mythology, chief god of the Tuatha Dé Danann, a father-figure, king and druid.
claims.statement_id: Dagda dianggap dewa agung mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology), dewa utama Tuatha Dé Danann, sosok bapak, raja, dan druid.
claims.quote: is considered the great god of Irish mythology. He is the chief god of the Tuatha Dé Danann, with the Dagda portrayed as a father-figure, king, and druid.

claims.statement: The Dagda is tied to fertility, agriculture, strength, magic, druidry, wisdom; controls life and death, weather, crops, time, seasons; a big bearded man or giant in a hooded cloak.
claims.statement_id: Dagda terkait kesuburan, pertanian, kekuatan, sihir, kedruidan, kebijaksanaan; menguasai hidup-mati, cuaca, panen, waktu, musim; lelaki besar berjanggut atau raksasa berjubah berkerudung.
claims.quote: He is associated with fertility, agriculture, masculinity and strength, as well as magic, druidry and wisdom. He can control life and death (cf. his staff), the weather and crops, as well as time and the seasons. He is often described as a large bearded man or giant wearing a hooded cloak.

claims.statement: He owns a magic staff (lorc) that kills and revives, a cauldron (coire ansic) never empty, and a magic harp.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki tongkat sakti (lorc) yang membunuh dan menghidupkan, kuali (coire ansic) yang tak pernah kosong, dan harpa sakti.
claims.quote: He owns a magic staff (lorc ) of dual nature: it kills with one end and brings to life with the other. He also owns a cauldron (the coire ansic) which never runs empty, and a magic harp

claims.statement: He is said to dwell in Brú na Bóinne (Newgrange).
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan tinggal di Brú na Bóinne (Newgrange).
claims.quote: He is said to dwell in Brú na Bóinne (Newgrange).

claims.statement: The Dagda's name means the good god or great god; other names include Eochu or Eochaid Ollathair and Ruad Rofhessa.
claims.statement_id: Nama Dagda berarti dewa yang baik atau dewa agung; nama lainnya Eochu atau Eochaid Ollathair dan Ruad Rofhessa.
claims.quote: The Dagda's name is thought to mean "the good god" or "the great god". His other names include Eochu or Eochaid Ollathair ("horseman, great father"), and Ruad Rofhessa ("mighty one/lord of great knowledge").

claims.statement: The Dagda is husband of the Morrígan and lover of Boann; his children include Aengus, Brigit, Bodb Derg, Cermait, Aed and Midir.
claims.statement_id: Dagda suami Morrígan dan kekasih Boann; anaknya Aengus, Brigit, Bodb Derg, Cermait, Aed, dan Midir.
claims.quote: The Dagda is said to be the husband of the Morrígan and lover of Boann. His children include Aengus, Brigit, Bodb Derg, Cermait, Aed, and Midir.

claims.statement: The Dagda is likened to the Germanic Odin, the Gaulish Sucellos and the Roman Dīs Pater or Jupiter.
claims.statement_id: Dagda dibandingkan dengan dewa Jermanik (Germanic) Odin, dewa Galia (Gaulish) Sucellos, dan Dīs Pater atau Jupiter (Roman).
claims.quote: The Dagda has been likened to the Germanic god Odin, the Gaulish god Sucellos, and the Roman god Dīs Pater or Jupiter.

claims.statement: The Dagda is a leader (Anführer) of the Túatha Dé Danann, the Allvater over law (Gesetz) and order (Ordnung), ugly (hässlich) and pot-bellied (Schmerbauch), with hood (Kapuze) and tunic (Tunika).
claims.statement_id: Dagda pemimpin (Anführer) Túatha Dé Danann, Allvater yang mengurus hukum (Gesetz) dan ketertiban (Ordnung), buruk rupa (hässlich) berperut buncit (Schmerbauch), berkerudung (Kapuze) dan bertunik (Tunika).
claims.quote: Dagda ist ein Anführer der mythischen Túatha Dé Danann. Er ist der Allvater und zuständig für Recht, Gesetz und Ordnung. Er wird als hässlich mit einem Schmerbauch beschrieben. Er trägt eine Kapuze, mit der er sein Gesicht verhüllt, und eine Tunika.

claims.statement: His attributes (Attribute) are the magic cauldron (magische Kessel), harp (Harfe) and club (Keule).
claims.statement_id: Atributnya (Attribute) kuali sakti (magische Kessel), harpa sakti (magische Harfe), dan gada sakti (magische Keule).
claims.quote: Seine Attribute sind der „magische Kessel“, die „magische Harfe“ und die „magische Keule“.

claims.statement: The Old Irish name Dagda stems from Proto-Celtic *Dago-dēwos.
claims.statement_id: Nama Dagda (Old Irish) berasal dari Proto-Kelt (Proto-Celtic) *Dago-dēwos.
claims.quote: The Old Irish name Dagda is generally believed to stem from Proto-Celtic: *Dago-dēwos , meaning "the good god" or "the great god".

claims.statement: The Fomorians (Fomori; Old Irish Fomóire, Modern Irish Fomhóraigh) are a hostile, monstrous supernatural race of Irish mythology.
claims.statement_id: Fomoria (Fomori; Old Irish Fomóire, Modern Irish Fomhóraigh) adalah bangsa gaib mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology), bermusuhan dan mengerikan.
claims.quote: The Fomorians or Fomori (Old Irish: Fomóire , Modern Irish: Fomhóraigh / Fomóraigh ) are a supernatural race in Irish mythology, who are often portrayed as hostile and monstrous beings.

claims.statement: At first from under the sea or earth; later sea raiders and giants.
claims.statement_id: Awalnya dari bawah laut atau bumi; kemudian perompak laut dan raksasa.
claims.quote: Originally they were said to come from under the sea or the earth. Later, they were portrayed as sea raiders and giants.

claims.statement: The Fomorians are foes of Ireland's first settlers and the Tuatha Dé Danann, who defeat them at the Battle of Mag Tuired.
claims.statement_id: Fomoria musuh pemukim pertama Irlandia (Ireland) dan lawan Tuatha Dé Danann, yang mengalahkan mereka dalam Battle of Mag Tuired.
claims.quote: They are enemies of Ireland's first settlers and opponents of the Tuatha Dé Danann, the other supernatural race in Irish mythology; although some members of the two races have offspring. The Tuatha Dé Danann defeat the Fomorians in the Battle of Mag Tuired.

claims.statement: One theory: the Fomorians represent nature's wild, destructive powers; chaos, darkness, death, blight and drought.
claims.statement_id: Satu teori: Fomoria mewakili kekuatan alam yang liar atau merusak; kekacauan, kegelapan, kematian, hama, kekeringan.
claims.quote: One theory is that the Fomorians were supernatural beings representing the wild or destructive powers of nature; personifications of chaos, darkness, death, blight and drought.

claims.statement: The first part of the name is Old Irish fo, under.
claims.statement_id: Unsur pertama nama mereka adalah fo (Old Irish), di bawah.
claims.quote: The first part is generally agreed to be the Old Irish fo, meaning under, below, lower, beneath, nether, etc.

claims.statement: A probably 7th-century elegy for Mess-Telmann says they dwell under the worlds of men.
claims.statement_id: Ratapan abad ke-7 untuk Mess-Telmann menyebut mereka tinggal di bawah dunia manusia.
claims.quote: In one of the earliest references to them, a probably 7th-century elegy for Mess-Telmann, they are said to dwell "under the worlds of men".

claims.statement: Per the 11th-century Lebor na hUidre, they have a man's body and goat's head, or one eye, arm and leg.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Lebor na hUidre abad ke-11, mereka bertubuh manusia berkepala kambing, atau bermata, berlengan, dan berkaki satu.
claims.quote: Sometimes they are said to have the body of a man and the head of a goat, according to an 11th-century text in Lebor na hUidre (the Book of the Dun Cow), or to have had one eye, one arm and one leg.

claims.statement: In Scotland (Schottland) they are called Foawr; demonic giants (dämonische Riesen) with one arm (Arm) and leg (Bein), some with animal heads (Tierköpfe).
claims.statement_id: Di Skotlandia (Schottland) mereka disebut Foawr; raksasa iblis (dämonische Riesen) berlengan (Arm) dan berkaki (Bein) satu, sebagian berkepala hewan (Tierköpfe).
claims.quote: In Schottland sind sie als „Foawr“ bekannt. Sie erscheinen als dämonische Riesen mit nur einem Arm und einem Bein und einige Angehörige ihres Volkes haben Tierköpfe (Ziegen-, Hirsch- oder Stier-), sind gehörnt oder reptilienartig.

claims.statement: The Tuatha de Danann took Ireland (Irland) from the Firbolg at the first battle of Magh Tuireadh and beat the Fomorii at the second (zweiten Schlacht).
claims.statement_id: Tuatha de Danann merebut Irlandia (Irland) dari Firbolg pada pertempuran pertama Magh Tuireadh dan mengalahkan Fomorii pada pertempuran kedua (zweiten Schlacht).
claims.quote: Die Tuatha de Danann entrissen den Firbolg bei der ersten Schlacht von Magh Tuireadh die Herrschaft über Irland und mussten dann bei der zweiten Schlacht von Magh Tuireadh die Fomorii schlagen, um die Eroberung zu sichern.

claims.statement: This is likened to other myths of a war between gods, such as the Æsir–Vanir War and the Titanomachy.
claims.statement_id: Pertempuran ini dibandingkan dengan mitos perang para dewa lainnya, seperti perang Æsir dan Vanir dan Titanomachy.
claims.quote: This has been likened to other Indo-European myths of a war between gods, such as the Æsir and Vanir War in Norse mythology, the Titanomachy (Olympian-Titan War) in Greek mythology, and the Devas and Asuras in Indian mythology.

claims.statement: Aos sí is the Irish name for a supernatural race of Gaelic folklore, similar to elves, descended from the Tuatha Dé Danann or Irish gods.
claims.statement_id: Aos sí adalah nama Irlandia (Irish) untuk ras gaib dalam cerita rakyat Gaelik (Gaelic folklore), mirip elf, keturunan Tuatha Dé Danann atau dewa mitologi Irlandia.
claims.quote: is the Irish name for a supernatural race in Gaelic folklore, similar to elves. They are said to descend from the Tuatha Dé Danann or the gods of Irish mythology.

claims.statement: Aos sí means folk of the sí, mounds that are portals to an Otherworld, in English fairy mounds or hollow hills; they are called ancestors, nature spirits, or gods.
claims.statement_id: Aos sí berarti bangsa sí, gundukan gerbang ke Dunia Lain (Otherworld), dalam bahasa Inggris (English) fairy mounds atau hollow hills; mereka disebut leluhur, roh alam, atau dewa-dewi.
claims.quote: The term aos sí means "folk of the sí"; these are the mounds in which they are said to dwell, which are seen as portals to an Otherworld. Such abodes are referred to in English as "shees", "fairy mounds", "elf mounds" or "hollow hills". The aos sí interact with humans and the human world. They are variously said to be the ancestors, the spirits of nature, or goddesses and gods.

claims.statement: Another name is daoine sí, people of the fairy mound; in English "the Sidhe".
claims.statement_id: Nama lain aos sí adalah daoine sí, orang gundukan peri; dalam bahasa Inggris "the Sidhe".
claims.quote: Another name for the aos sí is daoine sí , which likewise means "people of the fairy mound".

claims.statement: The 7th-century Irish bishop Tírechán called the sídh folk earthly gods (dei terreni); the 8th-century Fiacc's Hymn says they were adored before Saint Patrick.
claims.statement_id: Uskup Irlandia (Irish) Tírechán abad ke-7 menyebut kaum sídh dewa bumi (dei terreni, Latin); Fiacc's Hymn abad ke-8 menyebut mereka dipuja sebelum Saint Patrick (Santo Patrick).
claims.quote: Writing in the 7th century, the Irish bishop Tírechán described the sídh folk as "earthly gods" (Latin: dei terreni ). The 8th century Fiacc's Hymn says that the Irish adored the sídh folk before the coming of Saint Patrick.

claims.statement: Fairies could be fallen angels or descendants of the Tuatha Dé Danann, equivalent to the aos sí.
claims.statement_id: Peri bisa malaikat yang jatuh atau keturunan Tuatha Dé Danann, yang sama dengan aos sí.
claims.quote: The fairies could either be fallen angels or the descendants of the Tuatha Dé Danann; in the latter case, this is equivalent with aos sí.

claims.statement: In folk belief the aos sí are appeased with offerings and care is taken not to anger them.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat, aos sí ditenangkan dengan persembahan dan orang menghindari membuat mereka marah.
claims.quote: In folk belief and practice, the aos sí are often appeased with offerings and care is taken to avoid angering or insulting them.

claims.statement: The aos sí are a supernatural race of Irish and Scottish (Irlandia, Skotlandia) mythology like fairies or elves, living underground or in a world beside ours, a parallel universe in the Lebor Gabála Érenn.
claims.statement_id: Aos sí ras supranatural mitologi Irlandia dan Skotlandia mirip peri atau elf, tinggal di bawah tanah atau dunia lain di samping dunia manusia, yang dalam Lebor Gabála Érenn adalah alam semesta paralel.
claims.quote: adalah istilah yang mengacu kepada ras supranatural dalam mitologi Irlandia dan Skotlandia yang mirip dengan peri atau elf. Konon mereka tinggal di bawah tanah atau di dunia kasatmata yang ada bersamaan dengan dunia manusia. Dunia ini dijelaskan di dalam Lebor Gabála Érenn sebagai alam semesta paralel

claims.statement: In Scottish (Skotlandia) mythology they are called daoine sìth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Skotlandia mereka dinamai daoine sìth.
claims.quote: sementara dalam mitologi Skotlandia mereka dinamai daoine sìth.

claims.statement: Some sources call them survivors of the Tuatha Dé Danann who retreated into the Otherworld from the Sons of Míl Espáine.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sumber menyebut mereka sisa Tuatha Dé Danann yang mundur ke Dunia Lain (Otherworld) saat lari dari putra-putra Míl Espáine (kaum Milesia).
claims.quote: Some sources describe them as the survivors of the Tuatha Dé Danann who retreated into the Otherworld when fleeing the mortal Sons of Míl Espáine

claims.statement: In European folklore, familiars (familiar spirits) were supernatural beings protecting or helping witches and cunning folk in magic and divination.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa (European folklore), familiar (familiar spirits) adalah makhluk gaib yang melindungi atau membantu penyihir dan cunning folk dalam sihir dan ramalan.
claims.quote: were believed to be supernatural entities, interdimensional beings, or spiritual guardians that would protect or assist witches and cunning folk in their practice of magic, divination, and spiritual insight.

claims.statement: Familiars could appear in many forms, usually an animal, sometimes a human.
claims.statement_id: Familiar dapat muncul dalam banyak wujud, biasanya hewan, kadang manusia.
claims.quote: those alleging to have had contact with familiar spirits reported that they could manifest as numerous forms, usually as an animal, but sometimes as a human or humanoid figure

claims.statement: Witches' familiars were thought malevolent and classed as demons; cunning folk's were benevolent and called fairies.
claims.statement_id: Familiar penyihir dianggap jahat dan digolongkan iblis; familiar cunning folk dianggap baik dan disebut peri.
claims.quote: When they served witches, they were often thought to be malevolent, but when working for cunning folk, they were often considered benevolent (although there was some ambiguity in both cases). The former were often categorized as demons, while the latter were more commonly thought of and described as fairies.

claims.statement: The main purpose of familiars was to serve and protect the witch.
claims.statement_id: Tujuan utama familiar melayani dan melindungi penyihir.
claims.quote: The main purpose of familiars was to serve the witch, providing protection for them as they came into their new powers.

claims.statement: Since the 20th century practitioners, including Wiccans, use familiars, with pets or invisible familiars as aides.
claims.statement_id: Sejak abad ke-20 praktisi sihir, termasuk penganut Wicca, memakai konsep familiar dengan hewan peliharaan atau familiar tak kasatmata.
claims.quote: Since the 20th century some magical practitioners, including adherents of the neopagan religion of Wicca, use the concept of familiars, due to their association with older forms of magic. These contemporary practitioners use pets or wildlife, or believe that invisible versions of familiars act as magical aides.

claims.statement: The Familiar or Hexentier (spiritus familiaris) is a small animal-shaped (tierischer Gestalt) supernatural being of Celtic (keltischen) and Anglo-Saxon (angelsächsischen) folklore aiding witches (Hexen) and healers (Heilerinnen).
claims.statement_id: Familiar atau Hexentier (spiritus familiaris) adalah makhluk gaib kecil berwujud hewan (tierischer Gestalt) dalam cerita rakyat Kelt (keltischen) dan Anglo-Saxon (angelsächsischen) yang membantu penyihir (Hexen) dan penyembuh (Heilerinnen).
claims.quote: Als Familiar (englisch für Vertraute/r) oder Hexentier – mitunter auch lateinisch spiritus familiaris – werden besonders in der keltischen und angelsächsischen Folklore kleine übernatürliche Wesen mit tierischer Gestalt bezeichnet, die oftmals Hexen und Heilerinnen zur Seite stehen und diese unterstützen sollen.

claims.statement: Familiars are not bound to a house (Haus) and can travel (reisen) with their owner (Besitzerin).
claims.statement_id: Familiar tidak terikat pada rumah (Haus) dan dapat bepergian (reisen) bersama pemiliknya (Besitzerin).
claims.quote: Sie sind nicht an ein Haus und Grundstück gebunden und können mit ihrer Besitzerin reisen.

claims.statement: Some witch-hunters (Hexenjäger) saw Familiars as proof and as an earthly form of a demon (Dämons) or the Devil (Teufels).
claims.statement_id: Sebagian pemburu penyihir (Hexenjäger) melihat Familiars sebagai bukti dan wujud iblis (Dämons) atau Setan (Teufels).
claims.quote: Manche Hexenjäger sahen in den Familiars nicht nur einen Beweis für die Wahrheit ihrer Theorie, dass eine beschuldigte Person eine Hexe war, sondern in den Familiars eine irdische Gestalt eines Dämons oder des Teufels selbst.

claims.statement: Fionn mac Cumhaill (Finn McCool) is a hero of Irish mythology and Scottish and Manx folklore, leader of the Fianna, seer and poet with a magic thumb, hunting with hounds Bran and Sceólang.
claims.statement_id: Fionn mac Cumhaill (Finn McCool) adalah pahlawan mitologi Irlandia (Irish) dan cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish) dan Man (Manx), pemimpin Fianna, peramal dan penyair, beribu jari ajaib, berburu dengan anjing Bran dan Sceólang.
claims.quote: is a hero in Irish mythology, as well as in later Scottish and Manx folklore. He is the leader of the Fianna bands of young roving hunter-warriors, as well as being a seer and poet. He is said to have a magic thumb that bestows him with great wisdom. He is often depicted hunting with his hounds Bran and Sceólang, and fighting with his spear and sword.

claims.statement: Fionn's tales form the Fianna or Fenian Cycle, much narrated by his son, the poet Oisín.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Fionn membentuk Siklus Fianna (Fenian Cycle), banyak dituturkan putranya, penyair Oisín.
claims.quote: The tales of Fionn and his fiann form the Fianna Cycle or Fenian Cycle (an Fhiannaíocht ), much of it narrated by Fionn's son, the poet Oisín

claims.statement: In Old Irish finn means white, bright, fair.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Irlandia Kuno (Old Irish), finn berarti putih, terang, elok.
claims.quote: In Old Irish, finn/find means "white, bright, lustrous; fair, light-hued (of complexion, hair, etc.)

claims.statement: Fionn was the posthumous son of Cumhall, leader of the Fianna, and Muirne.
claims.statement_id: Fionn putra anumerta Cumhall, pemimpin Fianna, dan Muirne.
claims.quote: Fionn was the posthumous son of Cumhall, leader of the Fianna, by Muirne.

claims.statement: At the Battle of Cnucha Cumhall was killed by Goll mac Morna, who took over the Fianna.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Battle of Cnucha, Cumhall dibunuh Goll mac Morna, yang lalu memimpin Fianna.
claims.quote: The Battle of Cnucha was fought between Conn and Cumhall, and Cumhall was killed by Goll mac Morna, who took over leadership of the Fianna.

claims.statement: Fionn (Finn, Find Mac Cumail, MacCool) is an Irish hero (irischer Held) of medieval epic (mittelalterlichen Epik), namesake of the Finn-Zyklus.
claims.statement_id: Fionn (Finn, Find Mac Cumail, MacCool) adalah pahlawan Irlandia (irischer Held) epos abad pertengahan (mittelalterlichen Epik), tokoh utama Finn-Zyklus.
claims.quote: auch Finn oder Find Mac Cumail (auch Mac Umaill, MacCool), ist ein irischer Held aus der mittelalterlichen Epik. Er ist die namensgebende Hauptperson im Finn-Zyklus.

claims.statement: Fionn has healing hands (heilende Hände); whoever he gives water (Wasser) recovers; he learns combat from his aunt (Tante) Los Lurgann and gets the sword (Schwert) Mac an Luinn from his mother Muirne.
claims.statement_id: Fionn bertangan penyembuh (heilende Hände); yang diberinya air (Wasser) sembuh; belajar bertarung dari bibinya (Tante) Los Lurgann dan menerima pedang (Schwert) Mac an Luinn dari ibunya Muirne.
claims.quote: Er hat „heilende Hände“ – wem er Wasser reicht, der wird wieder gesund. Er lernt Kampfkunststücke bei seiner Tante Los Lurgann („Schnellfuß“) und erhält sein Schwert Mac an Luinn von seiner Mutter Muirne.

claims.statement: In later tales Fionn is a good warrior (Krieger) and seer (Seher), late in life envious (neidisch) and vengeful (rachsüchtig) in Diarmuid und Gráinne.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah kemudian Fionn pejuang (Krieger) dan peramal (Seher) yang baik, menjelang akhir hidupnya iri (neidisch) dan pendendam (rachsüchtig) dalam Diarmuid und Gráinne.
claims.quote: In den jüngeren Berichten ist Fionn ein positiv gezeichneten Krieger und Seher, gegen Ende seines Lebens wird er als neidisch und rachsüchtig dargestellt (Diarmuid und Gráinne).

claims.statement: Manannán (Manann, Manannán mac Lir, son of the Sea) is a sea god, warrior and otherworld king of Gaelic (Irish, Manx, Scottish) myth, one of the Tuatha Dé Danann.
claims.statement_id: Manannán (Manann, Manannán mac Lir, son of the Sea) adalah dewa laut, pejuang, dan raja dunia lain mitologi Gaelik (Gaelic: Irish, Manx, Scottish), salah satu Tuatha Dé Danann.
claims.quote: Manannán or Manann , also known as Manannán mac Lir ('son of the Sea'), is a sea god, warrior and king of the otherworld in Gaelic (Irish, Manx and Scottish) mythology who is one of the Tuatha Dé Danann .

claims.statement: He rules and guards the otherworld: Emain Ablach (Isle of Apple Trees), Mag Mell (Plain of Delights), Tír Tairngire (Land of Promise).
claims.statement_id: Ia penguasa dan penjaga dunia lain: Emain Ablach (Pulau Pohon Apel, Isle of Apple Trees), Mag Mell (Dataran Kebahagiaan), Tír Tairngire (Negeri Perjanjian).
claims.quote: He is seen as a ruler and guardian of the otherworld and his dominion is referred by such names as Emain Ablach (or Emhain Abhlach , 'Isle of Apple Trees'), Mag Mell ('Plain of Delights'), or Tír Tairngire ('Land of Promise').

claims.statement: He owns the boat Sguaba Tuinne (Wave-sweeper), the horse Aonbharr that runs over water and land, and the sword Fragarach.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki perahu Sguaba Tuinne (Wave-sweeper, Penyapu Ombak), kuda Aonbharr yang berlari di air dan darat, dan pedang Fragarach.
claims.quote: He is said to own a self-navigating boat named Sguaba Tuinne ('Wave-sweeper'), a horse Aonbharr which can course over water as well as land and a deadly strength-sapping sword named Fragarach

claims.statement: In Scottish and Manx legend he is Manannan beg mac y Leir; the Isle of Man (Mannin) is named after him; cognate with the Welsh Manawydan fab Llŷr.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Skotlandia dan Man (Scottish, Manx) ia Manannan beg mac y Leir; Isle of Man (Mannin) dinamai menurutnya; sekerabat dengan Manawydan fab Llŷr (Welsh, Wales).
claims.quote: Manannán appears also in Scottish and Manx legend, where he is known as Manannan beg mac y Leir ('little Manannan, son of the Sea'). The Isle of Man (Mannin ) is generally thought to be named after him, though some have said he is named after the island. He is cognate with the Welsh figure Manawydan fab Llŷr .

claims.statement: His name is Manandán in Old Irish, Manannán in Modern Irish and Mannan in Manx Gaelic.
claims.statement_id: Namanya Manandán (Old Irish, Irlandia Kuno), Manannán (Modern Irish), dan Mannan (Manx Gaelic, bahasa Man).
claims.quote: His name is spelt Manandán in Old Irish, Manannán in Modern Irish, Manannàn in Scottish Gaelic and Mannan in Manx Gaelic.

claims.statement: Manannán is seen as the guardian of the Otherworld (penjaga dunia lain) who frees souls into the afterlife (alam baka).
claims.statement_id: Manannán dipandang sebagai penjaga dunia lain (guardian of the Otherworld) dan pembebas jiwa ke alam baka.
claims.quote: Ia dipandang sebagai 'the guardian of the Otherworld (penjaga dunia lain) dan salah satu yang membebaskan jiwa-jiwa ke alam baka.

claims.statement: Manannán is also known as Oirbsiu or Oirbsen, from whom Lough Corrib takes its name.
claims.statement_id: Manannán juga dikenal sebagai Oirbsiu atau Oirbsen, asal nama Lough Corrib.
claims.quote: Manannán juga dikenal sebagai Oirbsiu atau Oirbsen, asal Lough Corrib mengambil namanya.

claims.statement: Manannán is identified with the trickster (sosok penipu) in Bodach an Chóta Lachtna.
claims.statement_id: Manannán diidentifikasikan dengan sosok penipu dalam Bodach an Chóta Lachtna.
claims.quote: Manannán selanjutnya diidentifikasikan dengan sosok penipu dalam Bodach an Chóta Lachtna

claims.statement: After the coming of humans (Milesians) Manannán is over-king of the surviving Tuatha Dé and uses the féth fíada mist to hide his home.
claims.statement_id: Setelah kedatangan manusia (Milesians, Milesia), Manannán raja atas Tuatha Dé yang tersisa dan memakai kabut gaib (féth fíada) untuk menyembunyikan kediamannya.
claims.quote: He is described as over-king of the surviving Tuatha Dé after the advent of humans (Milesians) and uses the mist of invisibility (féth fíada ) to cloak the whereabouts of his home as well as the sidhe dwellings of the others.

claims.statement: The Welsh Dragon (y Ddraig Goch, the red dragon) is a heraldic symbol of Wales on its national flag.
claims.statement_id: Naga Wales (Welsh Dragon; y Ddraig Goch, naga merah) adalah simbol heraldik Wales yang tampil pada bendera nasional Wales.
claims.quote: The Welsh Dragon (Welsh: y Ddraig Goch , meaning 'the red dragon', pronounced [ə ˈðraiɡ ˈɡoːχ] ) is a heraldic symbol that represents Wales and appears on the national flag of Wales.

claims.statement: The red dragon appears in the Mabinogion tale of Lludd and Llefelys, confined and fighting a white dragon at Dinas Emrys.
claims.statement_id: Naga merah muncul dalam kisah Mabinogion Lludd dan Llefelys (Lludd and Llefelys), terkurung dan bertarung dengan naga putih di Dinas Emrys.
claims.quote: The red dragon appears in the ancient Mabinogion story of Lludd and Llefelys where it is confined, battling with an invading white dragon, at Dinas Emrys.

claims.statement: In the Historia Brittonum (c. 829 AD), Gwrtheyrn, King of the Britons, is told by the boy Emrys to dig up two dragons; the Anglo-Saxon white dragon will be beaten by the red dragon of Wales.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Historia Brittonum (sekitar 829 M), Gwrtheyrn, raja Briton (King of the Britons), diberi tahu anak bernama Emrys untuk menggali dua naga; naga putih Anglo-Saxon akan dikalahkan naga merah Wales.
claims.quote: The story continues in the Historia Brittonum , written around AD 829, where Gwrtheyrn, King of the Britons is frustrated in attempts to build a fort at Dinas Emrys. He is told by a boy, Emrys, to dig up two dragons fighting beneath the castle. He discovers the white dragon representing the Anglo-Saxons, which is soon to be defeated by the red dragon of Wales.

claims.statement: Celtic Briton leaders personified as dragons include Maelgwn Gwynedd, Mynyddog Mwynfawr and Urien Rheged; later Owain Gwynedd, Llywelyn ap Gruffydd and Owain Glyndŵr.
claims.statement_id: Pemimpin Briton Kelt (Celtic Britons) yang dipersonifikasikan sebagai naga: Maelgwn Gwynedd, Mynyddog Mwynfawr, Urien Rheged; kemudian Owain Gwynedd, Llywelyn ap Gruffydd, Owain Glyndŵr.
claims.quote: Ancient leaders of the Celtic Britons that are personified as dragons include Maelgwn Gwynedd, Mynyddog Mwynfawr and Urien Rheged. Later Welsh "dragons" include Owain Gwynedd, Llywelyn ap Gruffydd and Owain Glyndŵr.

claims.statement: The red dragon now symbolises Wales, on the national flag official since 1959.
claims.statement_id: Naga merah kini melambangkan Wales dan ada di bendera nasional yang resmi sejak 1959.
claims.quote: The red dragon is now seen as symbolising Wales, present on the current national flag of Wales, which became an official flag in 1959.

claims.statement: The oldest recorded use of the dragon for Wales is in the Historia Brittonum (c. 829 AD), but it is popularly seen as the battle standard of King Arthur (Raja Arthur) and ancient Celtic leaders.
claims.statement_id: Penggunaan tertua naga untuk Wales ada dalam Historia Brittonum (sekitar 829 M), tetapi naga populer dianggap standar pertempuran Raja Arthur dan pemimpin Celtic kuno.
claims.quote: Penggunaan naga tertua yang tercatat untuk melambangkan Wales adalah dalam Historia Brittonum, yang ditulis sekitar tahun 829 M, tetapi secara populer dianggap sebagai standar pertempuran Raja Arthur dan para pemimpin Celtic kuno lainnya.

claims.statement: Under the Tudor kings the red dragon supported the arms of the Kingdom of England (Kerajaan Inggris); today the Welsh Government (Pemerintah Welsh), the Senedd and others use it.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa raja Tudor, naga merah menjadi pendukung lambang Kerajaan Inggris; kini dipakai Pemerintah Welsh (Wales), Senedd, dan lainnya.
claims.quote: Selama pemerintahan raja Tudor (mereka sendiri berasal dari Welsh), naga merah digunakan sebagai pendukung dalam lambang Kerajaan Inggris. Naga merah sering dianggap melambangkan segala hal Welsh, dan digunakan oleh banyak institusi publik dan swasta. Ini termasuk Pemerintah Welsh, Senedd, Visit Wales

claims.statement: Military use of the term dragon (Latin draco) dates back to the Roman period.
claims.statement_id: Penggunaan militer istilah naga (draco, Latin) berasal dari zaman Romawi (Roman).
claims.quote: The military use of the term "dragon" (in Latin, "draco") dates back to the Roman period

claims.statement: In Lludd and Llevelys the second plague is a shriek that comes every May-eve over every hearth in the Island of Britain: men lose their hue and strength, women lose their children, young men and maidens lose their senses, and all animals, trees, earth and waters are left barren.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Lludd and Llevelys, wabah kedua adalah jeritan yang datang setiap malam Mei di atas setiap perapian di Pulau Britania: para pria kehilangan rona dan kekuatan, para wanita kehilangan anak, para pemuda dan gadis kehilangan akal, dan semua hewan, pohon, tanah, dan air menjadi mandul.
claims.quote: The second plague was a shriek which came on every May-eve, over every hearth in the Island of Britain. And this went through people’s hearts, and so scared them, that the men lost their hue and their strength, and the women their children, and the young men and the maidens lost their senses, and all the animals and trees and the earth and the waters, were left barren.

claims.statement: Llevelys tells Lludd that the second plague in his dominion is a dragon, that another dragon of a foreign race is fighting it and striving to overcome it, and that therefore Lludd's dragon makes a fearful outcry.
claims.statement_id: Llevelys menjelaskan kepada Lludd bahwa wabah kedua di wilayahnya adalah seekor naga, sementara naga lain dari ras asing bertarung dengannya dan berusaha menaklukkannya, sehingga naga Lludd mengeluarkan jeritan yang mengerikan.
claims.quote: “And the second plague,” said he, “that is in thy dominion, behold it is a dragon. And another dragon of a foreign race is fighting with it, and striving to overcome it. And therefore does your dragon make a fearful outcry.

claims.statement: Llevelys advises that the two dragons will drink up all the mead in the cauldron and then sleep, and that Lludd must immediately fold the covering around them, bury them in a kistvaen in the strongest place in his dominions, and hide them in the earth.
claims.statement_id: Llevelys menasihati bahwa kedua naga akan meminum seluruh hidromel di dalam kuali lalu tertidur, dan Lludd harus segera melipat penutupnya, menguburkan mereka di dalam kistvaen di tempat terkuat di wilayahnya, dan menyembunyikannya di dalam bumi.
claims.quote: And they will drink up the whole of the mead; and after that they will sleep. Thereupon do thou immediately fold the covering around them, and bury them in a kistvaen, in the strongest place thou hast in thy dominions, and hide them in the earth.

claims.statement: Lludd folded the covering around the sleeping dragons and hid them in a kistvaen in the securest place he had in Snowdon; the spot was afterwards called Dinas Emreis, before that Dinas Ffaraon, and the fierce outcry ceased in his dominions.
claims.statement_id: Lludd melipat penutup di sekeliling kedua naga yang tertidur dan menyembunyikan mereka di dalam kistvaen di tempat teraman di Snowdon; tempat itu kemudian disebut Dinas Emreis, sebelumnya Dinas Ffaraon, dan jeritan dahsyat itu berhenti di wilayahnya.
claims.quote: And in their sleep, Lludd folded the covering around them, and in the securest place he had in Snowdon, he hid them in a kistvaen. Now after that this spot was called Dinas Emreis, but before that, Dinas Ffaraon. And thus the fierce outcry ceased in his dominions.

claims.statement: Llevelys foretells that as long as the dragons stay in that strong place no plague shall come to the Island of Britain from elsewhere.
claims.statement_id: Llevelys meramalkan bahwa selama kedua naga itu berdiam di tempat yang kuat itu, tidak ada wabah dari tempat lain yang akan menimpa Pulau Britania.
claims.quote: And as long as they shall bide in that strong place no plague shall come to the Island of Britain from elsewhere.

claims.statement: In Nennius's History of the Britons the boy explains that the two serpents are two dragons: the red serpent is the king's dragon, the white serpent the dragon of the people who occupy several provinces and districts of Britain; at length our people shall rise and drive away the Saxon race from beyond the sea.
claims.statement_id: Dalam History of the Britons karya Nennius, sang anak menjelaskan bahwa kedua ular itu adalah dua naga: ular merah adalah naga Vortigern, ular putih adalah naga bangsa yang menduduki banyak provinsi dan distrik Britania; pada akhirnya bangsa kita akan bangkit dan mengusir bangsa Saxon dari seberang laut.
claims.quote: the two serpents are two dragons; the red serpent is your dragon, but the white serpent is the dragon of the people who occupy several provinces and districts of Britain, even almost from sea to sea: at length, however, our people shall rise and drive away the Saxon race from beyond the sea, whence they originally came

claims.statement: In Nennius the two serpents struggle: the white one raises himself and throws the other into the middle of the tent, sometimes driving him to its edge, thrice repeated; at length the red one, apparently the weaker, recovers his strength and expels the white one from the tent.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Nennius, kedua ular bergumul: yang putih bangkit dan melempar yang lain ke tengah tenda, kadang mendorongnya ke tepi, dan itu terulang tiga kali; akhirnya yang merah, yang tampak lebih lemah, memulihkan kekuatannya dan mengusir yang putih dari tenda.
claims.quote: The serpents began to struggle with each other; and the white one, raising himself up, threw down the other into the middle of the tent, and sometimes drove him to the edge of it; and this was repeated thrice. At length the red one, apparently the weaker of the two, recovering his strength, expelled the white one from the tent

claims.statement: In Geoffrey of Monmouth the two dragons, one white and one red, come forth and fight terribly, casting forth fire with their breath; the white dragon has the advantage and makes the other fly to the end of the lake.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Geoffrey of Monmouth, dua naga, satu putih dan satu merah, keluar dan bertarung dengan dahsyat sambil menyemburkan api dari napas mereka; naga putih unggul dan membuat yang lain lari ke ujung danau.
claims.quote: the two dragons, one of which ... was white, the other red, came forth, and, approaching one another, began a terrible fight, and cast forth fire with their breath. But the white dragon had the advantage, and made the other fly to the end of the lake.

claims.statement: In Merlin's prophecy as Geoffrey gives it, woe to the red dragon, for his banishment hastens on: his lurking holes shall be seized by the white dragon, which signifies the Saxons, while the red denotes the British nation, which shall be oppressed; its mountains shall be levelled as the valleys and the rivers of the valleys shall run with blood.
claims.statement_id: Dalam nubuat Merlin menurut Geoffrey, celakalah naga merah karena pengasingannya segera tiba: liangnya akan direbut naga putih yang berarti bangsa Saxon, sedangkan yang merah melambangkan bangsa Britania yang akan tertindas; gunung-gunungnya akan diratakan seperti lembah dan sungai-sungai lembah akan mengalirkan darah.
claims.quote: Woe to the red dragon, for his banishment hasteneth on. His lurking holes shall be seized by the white dragon, which signifies the Saxons whom you invited over; but the red denotes the British nation, which shall be oppressed by the white. Therefore shall its mountains be levelled as the valleys, and the rivers of the valleys shall run with blood.

claims.statement: The prophecy continues: at last the oppressed shall prevail and oppose the cruelty of foreigners; a boar of Cornwall shall give his assistance and trample their necks under his feet.
claims.statement_id: Nubuat itu berlanjut: pada akhirnya yang tertindas akan menang dan melawan kekejaman orang asing; seekor babi hutan dari Cornwall akan membantu dan menginjak leher mereka.
claims.quote: At last the oppressed shall prevail, and oppose the cruelty of foreigners. For a boar of Cornwall shall give his assistance, and trample their necks under his feet.

claims.statement: Merlin's prophecy says the seed of the white dragon shall be swept out of our gardens and the remainder of his generation shall be decimated.
claims.statement_id: Nubuat Merlin menyatakan benih naga putih akan disapu dari kebun-kebun kita, dan sisa keturunannya akan dibantai sepersepuluh.
claims.quote: The seed of the white dragon shall be swept out of our gardens, and the remainder of his generation shall be decimated.

claims.statement: An imp is a European mythological being like a fairy or demon in folklore and superstition; the word may come from ympe.
claims.statement_id: Imp adalah makhluk mitologi Eropa (European) mirip peri atau iblis, dalam cerita rakyat dan takhayul; katanya mungkin dari ympe.
claims.quote: An imp is a European mythological being similar to a fairy or demon, frequently described in folklore and superstition. The word may perhaps derive from the term ympe, used to denote a young grafted tree.

claims.statement: Imps are mischievous rather than dangerous, lesser beings, sometimes the devil's attendants, lively and small.
claims.statement_id: Imp usil, bukan ancaman serius, makhluk rendahan, kadang pengiring Iblis, lincah dan kecil.
claims.quote: Imps are often described as troublesome and mischievous more than seriously threatening or dangerous, and as lesser beings rather than more important supernatural beings. The attendants of the devil are sometimes described as imps. They are usually described as lively and having small stature.

claims.statement: Old English impa meant a young shoot, then a noble scion or child; from the 16th century "imp of hell", and by the 17th a small demon, a witch's familiar.
claims.statement_id: Impa (Old English, Inggris Kuno) berarti tunas muda, lalu keturunan bangsawan atau anak; sejak abad ke-16 "imp of hell", dan pada abad ke-17 iblis kecil, familiar penyihir.
claims.quote: The Old English noun impa meant a young shoot or scion of a plant or tree, and later came to mean the scion of a noble house, or a child in general. Starting in the 16th century, it was often used in expressions like "imps of serpents", "imp of hell", "imp of the devil", and so on; and by the 17th century, it came to mean a small demon, a familiar of a witch.

claims.statement: Unlike Christian folklore, Germanic demons were not always evil; imps were mischievous, and in some religions attendants of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari cerita rakyat Kristen (Christian), iblis dalam legenda Jermanik (Germanic) tak selalu jahat; imp lebih usil, dan dalam sebagian agama pelayan para dewa.
claims.quote: Unlike the Christian folklore, demons in Germanic legends were not necessarily always evil. Imps were often mischievous rather than evil or harmful. In some religions, they were attendants of the gods.

claims.statement: A 14th-century Lincolnshire legend: the devil came with two imps who wrecked the cathedral; an angel ordered them to stop, and the imp that threw a rock was petrified.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Lincolnshire abad ke-14: Iblis datang dengan dua imp yang merusak katedral; seorang malaikat menyuruh berhenti, dan imp yang melempar batu membatu.
claims.quote: A legend in Lincolnshire dating to the 14th-century recounts that the devil, being annoyed with the completion of the cathedral, paid a visit, accompanied by two imps who proceeded to wreak havoc in the building. An angel appeared and ordered them to stop. One turned to throw a rock at the angel and was instantly petrified.

claims.statement: The Lincoln Imp statue in Lincoln Cathedral, England, is now a symbol of the city.
claims.statement_id: Patung Lincoln Imp di Lincoln Cathedral (Lincoln, England) kini menjadi simbol kota.
claims.quote: A statue of the Lincoln Imp inside the medieval Lincoln Cathedral in Lincoln, England. It has now become a symbol of the city.

claims.statement: The Imp is a European (Eropa) mythological being like a fairy (peri) or demon in folklore and superstition (takhayul).
claims.statement_id: Imp adalah makhluk mitologi Eropa yang mirip peri atau demon dalam cerita rakyat dan takhayul.
claims.quote: Imp adalah makhluk mitologi Eropa yang mirip dengan peri atau demon, yang sering digambarkan dalam cerita rakyat dan takhayul.

claims.statement: The servants of the Devil (Sang Iblis) are sometimes depicted as imps, lively and small (bertubuh kecil).
claims.statement_id: Para pelayan Sang Iblis kadang digambarkan sebagai imp yang lincah dan bertubuh kecil.
claims.quote: Para pelayan Sang Iblis terkadang digambarkan sebagai sosok imp. Mereka biasanya digambarkan sebagai sosok yang lincah dan bertubuh kecil.

claims.statement: The brownie (broonie; brùnaidh, gruagach) is a household spirit or hobgoblin of Scottish folklore working at night, given a bowl of milk or cream by the hearth.
claims.statement_id: Brownie (broonie, Scots; brùnaidh, gruagach, Scottish Gaelic) adalah roh rumah atau hobgoblin cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore) yang bekerja malam hari, diberi semangkuk susu atau krim di dekat perapian.
claims.quote: A brownie or broonie (Scots), also known as a brùnaidh or gruagach (Scottish Gaelic), is a household spirit or hobgoblin from Scottish folklore that is said to come out at night while the owners of the house are asleep and perform various chores and farming tasks. The human owners of the house must leave a bowl of milk or cream or some other offering for the brownie, usually by the hearth.

claims.statement: Brownies are easily offended, leave forever if insulted, are mischievous and punish lazy servants.
claims.statement_id: Brownie mudah tersinggung, pergi selamanya bila dihina, usil, dan menghukum pelayan malas.
claims.quote: Brownies are described as easily offended and will leave their homes forever if they feel they have been insulted or in any way taken advantage of. Brownies are characteristically mischievous and are often said to punish or pull pranks on lazy servants.

claims.statement: Brownies began as domestic tutelary spirits, like the Lares of ancient Roman tradition.
claims.statement_id: Brownie berasal dari roh pelindung rumah, mirip Lares tradisi Romawi (Roman) kuno.
claims.quote: Brownies originated as domestic tutelary spirits, very similar to the Lares of ancient Roman tradition.

claims.statement: Brownies are ugly, brown-skinned, hairy; once human-sized, now small; can turn invisible and take animal shapes; leave if given clothes or baptized.
claims.statement_id: Brownie jelek, berkulit cokelat, berbulu; dulu berukuran manusia, kini kecil; dapat tak kasatmata dan berwujud hewan; pergi bila diberi pakaian atau dibaptis.
claims.quote: they are usually described as ugly, brown-skinned, and covered in hair. In the oldest stories, they are usually human-sized or larger. In more recent times, they have come to be seen as small and wizened. They are often capable of turning invisible, and they sometimes appear in the shapes of animals.

claims.statement: Variants in England and Scotland include hobs and ùruisgs; outside them the Welsh Bwbach and Manx Fenodyree.
claims.statement_id: Varian di Inggris dan Skotlandia (England, Scotland): hob dan ùruisg; di luar itu Bwbach (Welsh, Wales) dan Fenodyree (Manx, Man).
claims.quote: Regional variants in England and Scotland include hobs, and ùruisgs. Variants outside England and Scotland are the Welsh Bwbach and the Manx Fenodyree.

claims.statement: The Brownie is a small hard-working fairy or hobgoblin in a house or barn, seldom seen, heard working at night, expecting porridge and honey (bubur, madu).
claims.statement_id: Brownie peri atau hobgoblin kecil yang rajin di rumah atau lumbung, jarang terlihat, terdengar bekerja malam hari, dan mengharapkan bubur dan madu.
claims.quote: Brownie merupakan sejenis peri atau hobgoblin kecil yang rajin, dan dipercayai mendiami suatu rumah atau lumbung. Mereka jarang terlihat, tetapi sering terdengar di malam hari, membersihkan dan melakukan pekerjaan rumah. Sebagai imbalan atas kerja kerasnya, Brownie mengharapkan hadiah makanan, seperti bubur dan madu.

claims.statement: The Brownie is a mythological being popular in Scottish and English (Skotlandia, Inggris) folklore.
claims.statement_id: Brownie makhluk mitologi populer dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia dan Inggris.
claims.quote: Brownie adalah makhluk mitologi yang populer dalam cerita rakyat di sekitar Skotlandia dan Inggris.

claims.statement: Brownies appear in John Milton's L'Allegro; the Brownies of the Girl Guides are named after a story by Juliana Horatia Ewing.
claims.statement_id: Brownie muncul dalam puisi L'Allegro karya John Milton; Brownies dalam Girl Guides dinamai menurut cerita Juliana Horatia Ewing.
claims.quote: Brownies have also appeared outside of folklore, including in John Milton's poem L'Allegro. They became popular in works of children's literature in the late nineteenth century and continue to appear in works of modern fantasy. The Brownies in the Girl Guides are named after a short story by Juliana Horatia Ewing based on brownie folklore.

claims.statement: Brownies take the gift not as payment (pembayaran) but as a token of thanks (tanda penghargaan).
claims.statement_id: Brownie tidak menganggap hadiah itu bayaran, hanya tanda penghargaan.
claims.quote: Namun mereka tidak menganggap hadiahnya tersebut sebagai pembayaran, tetapi hanya sebagai tanda penghargaan.

claims.statement: Brownies are always naked or in rags, and leave forever if given clothing or baptized.
claims.statement_id: Brownie selalu telanjang atau compang-camping, dan pergi selamanya bila diberi pakaian atau dibaptis.
claims.quote: They are always either naked or dressed in rags. If a person attempts to present a brownie with clothing or baptize it, it will leave forever.

claims.statement: Selkies shapeshift between seal and human by removing or donning their seal skin; prominent in Celtic and Norse tradition.
claims.statement_id: Selkie makhluk mitologi yang berubah wujud antara anjing laut (seal) dan manusia dengan melepas atau memakai kulitnya; menonjol dalam tradisi Kelt dan Nordik (Celtic, Norse).
claims.quote: Selkies are mythological creatures that can shapeshift between seal and human forms by removing or putting on their seal skin. They feature prominently in the oral traditions and mythology of various cultures, especially those of Celtic and Norse origin.

claims.statement: Selkie comes from the Scots word for seal; also silkies, selchies; called selkie fowk, seal folk.
claims.statement_id: Kata selkie dari kata Skots (Scots) untuk anjing laut; juga silkies, selchies; disebut selkie fowk, bangsa anjing laut.
claims.quote: The term "selkie" derives from the Scots word for "seal", and is also spelled as silkies, sylkies, or selchies. Selkies are sometimes referred to as selkie folk (Scots: selkie fowk ), meaning "seal folk".

claims.statement: Selkies are mainly tied to Scotland's Northern Isles, living as seals and shedding skin to be human on land.
claims.statement_id: Selkie terutama dikaitkan dengan Northern Isles Skotlandia (Scotland), hidup sebagai anjing laut dan melepas kulit menjadi manusia di darat.
claims.quote: Selkies are mainly associated with the Northern Isles of Scotland, where they are said to live as seals in the sea but shed their skin to become human on land.

claims.statement: Selkies are dual-natured, friendly or dangerous and vengeful; seductive in human form, often in love affairs with humans that produce children.
claims.statement_id: Selkie bersifat ganda, ramah atau berbahaya dan pendendam; menarik dalam wujud manusia, sering berhubungan cinta dengan manusia dan beranak.
claims.quote: Selkies have a dual nature: they can be friendly and helpful to humans, but they can also be dangerous and vengeful. Selkies are often depicted as attractive and seductive in human form, and many stories involve selkies having romantic or sexual relationships with humans, sometimes resulting in children.

claims.statement: Selkies can be forced to marry by someone stealing their skin; such marriages are unhappy, and the selkie escapes if it finds its skin.
claims.statement_id: Selkie dapat dipaksa menikah oleh orang yang mencuri kulitnya; pernikahan itu tak bahagia, dan selkie kabur bila menemukan kulitnya.
claims.quote: Selkies can also be coerced or tricked into marrying humans, usually by someone who steals and hides their seal skin, preventing them from returning to the sea. Such marriages are often unhappy, as the selkie always longs for the sea and may eventually escape if they find their skin.

claims.statement: Selkies are mythological beings of Irish, Scottish and Faroese (Irlandia, Skotlandia, Faroe) folklore; similar ones in Icelandic (Islandia) tradition.
claims.statement_id: Selkie makhluk mitologi dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia, Skotlandia, dan Faroe; serupa dalam tradisi Islandia.
claims.quote: adalah makhluk mitologi yang ditemukan di Irlandia, Skotlandia, dan cerita rakyat Faroe. Makhluk serupa juga dijelaskan dalam tradisi Islandia.

claims.statement: Male selkies are very handsome (tampan) and seduce women (perempuan), especially discontented fishermen's wives (nelayan).
claims.statement_id: Selkie laki-laki sangat tampan dan pandai menggoda perempuan, terutama istri nelayan yang tak puas.
claims.quote: Selkies laki-laki digambarkan sebagai sosok yang sangat tampan dalam bentuk manusia, dan memiliki kekuatan besar untuk menggoda manusia perempuan. Mereka biasanya mencari orang-orang yang tidak puas dengan kehidupan mereka, seperti wanita yang sudah menikah dan sedang menunggu suami nelayan mereka.

claims.statement: Selkies have counterparts elsewhere and are sometimes confused with mermaids or the finfolk.
claims.statement_id: Selkie punya padanan di budaya lain dan kadang dirancukan dengan putri duyung (mermaids) atau finfolk.
claims.quote: Selkies have counterparts in other cultures. They are sometimes confused with other seal-like creatures, such as the mermaids or the finfolk.

claims.statement: The legend is most common in the Northern Isles (Kepulauan Northern) of Scotland and very like the swan-maiden (gadis angsa) tale.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini paling umum di Kepulauan Northern Skotlandia dan sangat mirip kisah gadis angsa.
claims.quote: Legenda ini rupanya yang paling umum di Kepulauan Northern dari Skotlandia dan ini sangat mirip dengan kisah gadis angsa.

claims.statement: A pixie (pisky, pixy, piskie or pigsie in Cornwall and Devon) is a mythical creature of British folklore.
claims.statement_id: Pixie (pisky, pixy, pixi, pizkie, piskie, pigsie di Cornwall dan Devon) adalah makhluk mitos cerita rakyat Britania (British folklore).
claims.quote: A pixie (also called pisky, pixy, pixi, pizkie, piskie, or pigsie in parts of Cornwall and Devon) is a mythical creature of British folklore.

claims.statement: Pixies cluster in the moorlands of Cornwall and Devon, suggesting a Celtic origin; the word also appears in Dorset, Somerset and elsewhere.
claims.statement_id: Pixie terutama di dataran tinggi Cornwall dan Devon, mengisyaratkan asal Kelt (Celtic); kata pixie juga ada di Dorset, Somerset, dan lain-lain.
claims.quote: Pixies are speculated to be particularly concentrated in the high moorland areas around Cornwall and Devon, suggesting some Celtic origin for the belief and name. However, the word 'pixie' (under various forms) also appears in Dorset, Somerset and to a lesser extent in Sussex, Wiltshire and Hampshire.

claims.statement: Like the Irish and Scottish Aos Sí, pixies inhabit ancient underground sites such as stone circles, barrows, dolmens, ringforts or menhirs.
claims.statement_id: Seperti Aos Sí Irlandia dan Skotlandia (Irish, Scottish), pixie mendiami situs bawah tanah kuno seperti lingkaran batu, barrow, dolmen, ringfort, menhir.
claims.quote: Similar to the Irish and Scottish Aos Sí (also spelled Aos Sidhe), pixies are believed to inhabit ancient underground sites such as stone circles, barrows, dolmens, ringforts, or menhirs.

claims.statement: Pixies are generally benign, mischievous, short and childlike, dancing and wrestling outdoors through the night.
claims.statement_id: Pixie umumnya tak jahat, usil, pendek, kekanak-kanakan, suka menari dan bergulat sepanjang malam.
claims.quote: In traditional regional lore, pixies are generally benign, mischievous, short of stature, and childlike; they are fond of dancing and wrestling outdoors, which they perform through the night.

claims.statement: The term Pobel Vean (Little People) is used for them collectively.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan Pobel Vean (Little People, orang kecil) dipakai untuk mereka secara bersama.
claims.quote: The term Pobel Vean (Little People) is often used to refer to them collectively.

claims.statement: In west Penwith spriggans are distinguished from pixies by their malevolence.
claims.statement_id: Di Penwith barat (west Penwith), spriggan dibedakan dari pixie karena jahat.
claims.quote: In west Penwith, the area of late survival of the Cornish language, spriggans are distinguished from pixies by their malevolent nature

claims.statement: Pixies are small fabulous beings (kleine Fabelwesen) of English folklore (englischen Folklore) like kobolds (Kobolden) and fairies (Feen), in Devon and Cornwall.
claims.statement_id: Pixies makhluk dongeng kecil (kleine Fabelwesen) cerita rakyat Inggris (englischen Folklore) mirip kobold (Kobolden) dan peri (Feen), di Devon dan Cornwall.
claims.quote: Pixies sind kleine Fabelwesen aus der englischen Folklore, deren Charakteristika denen von Kobolden und Feen ähneln. Geschichten über diese Wesen sind im Südwesten Englands, in den Regionen Devon und Cornwall, verbreitet.

claims.statement: Pixies were beings not good enough for paradise (Paradies) nor bad enough for hell (Hölle), or druids (Druiden) who did not convert to Christianity (Christentum).
claims.statement_id: Pixies makhluk yang tak cukup baik untuk surga (Paradies) dan tak cukup jahat untuk neraka (Hölle), atau druid (Druiden) yang tak masuk Kristen (Christentum). Dikecilkan oleh Tuhan (Gott) sebagai hukuman.
claims.quote: So sollen die pixies Wesen sein, die nicht gut genug für das Paradies und nicht schlecht genug für die Hölle waren und daher für ewig auf der Erde bleiben mussten. Nach einer anderen Geschichte sind die pixies Druiden, die nicht zum Christentum konvertierten und zur Strafe von Gott so lange geschrumpft wurden, bis sie sich zum Christentum bekannten.

claims.statement: The origin of pixie is uncertain; perhaps Swedish dialect pyske, 'small fairy'.
claims.statement_id: Asal kata pixie tidak pasti; mungkin dari pyske dialek Swedia (Swedish), "peri kecil".
claims.quote: The origin of the word pixie is uncertain. It could have come from the Swedish dialectal pyske, meaning 'small fairy'.

claims.statement: According to the Devon peasant, as Keightley reports from Mrs. Bray, the Pixies are the souls of infants who died before they were baptised.
claims.statement_id: Menurut petani Devon, seperti dikutip Keightley dari Mrs. Bray, para Pixie adalah jiwa bayi yang meninggal sebelum dibaptis.
claims.quote: According to the Devon peasant, the Pixies are the souls of infants who died before they were baptised.

claims.statement: Some Pixies are sent to the mines, where they kindly lead the miner to the richest lode or maliciously, by noises imitating hammer strokes and false fires, draw him to the worst ore and laugh at his disappointment.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa Pixie dikirim ke tambang, tempat mereka dengan baik hati menuntun penambang ke urat bijih terkaya, atau dengan jahat, lewat bunyi yang meniru ketukan palu dan api palsu, memancingnya ke bijih terburuk lalu menertawakan kekecewaannya.
claims.quote: Some are sent to the mines, where they will kindly lead the miner to the richest lode, or maliciously, by noises imitating the stroke of the hammer, and by false fires, draw him on to where the worst ore in the mine lies, and then laugh at his disappointment.

claims.statement: The office of some Pixies is to steal children; of others, to lead travellers astray like Will-o'-the-wisps, or to Pixy-lead them, as it is termed.
claims.statement_id: Tugas sebagian Pixie adalah mencuri anak-anak; tugas yang lain menyesatkan pengembara seperti api-api rawa, atau "memandu-Pixie" mereka (Pixy-lead), sebagaimana istilahnya.
claims.quote: The office of some is to steal children; of others, to lead travellers astray, as Will-o'-the-wisps, or to Pixy-lead them, as it is termed.

claims.statement: Being Pixy-led is very apt to befall worthy yeomen returning at night from fair or market, especially if they sat long at the market-table.
claims.statement_id: Disesatkan Pixie (Pixy-led) mudah menimpa petani terhormat yang pulang malam dari pasar atau pekan raya, terutama bila mereka lama duduk di meja pasar.
claims.quote: The being Pixy-led is a thing very apt to befall worthy yeomen returning at night from fair or market, especially if they sat long at the market-table

claims.statement: Mrs. Bray has been assured that mothers used frequently to pin their children to their sides to prevent their being stolen by the Pixies.
claims.statement_id: Mrs. Bray diberi tahu bahwa para ibu dahulu sering menyematkan anak mereka ke sisi tubuhnya agar tidak dicuri para Pixie.
claims.quote: Mrs. Bray has been assured that mothers used frequently to pin their children to their sides, to prevent their being stolen by the Pixies

claims.statement: Turning the coat, or some other article of dress, is found to be the surest remedy against Pixy-illusion.
claims.statement_id: Membalik mantel, atau pakaian lainnya, didapati sebagai obat paling pasti melawan tipuan Pixie (Pixy-illusion).
claims.quote: This turning of the coat, or some other article of dress, is found to be the surest remedy against Pixy-illusion.

claims.statement: The good dames in that part of the world are very particular about sweeping their houses before bed and often place a basin of water beside the chimney-nook to accommodate the Pixies, who are great lovers of water.
claims.statement_id: Para ibu rumah tangga di daerah itu sangat memperhatikan menyapu rumah sebelum tidur dan sering meletakkan baskom air di sudut cerobong untuk menyenangkan para Pixie, yang sangat menyukai air.
claims.quote: the good dames in this part of the world are very particular in sweeping their houses before they go to bed; and they will frequently place a basin of water beside the chimney-nook, to accommodate the Pixies, who are great lovers of water

claims.statement: Other Pixies make noises in walls to frighten people; in short, everything done elsewhere by fairies, boggarts or like beings is done in Devon by the Pixies.
claims.statement_id: Pixie lain membuat bunyi-bunyi di dinding untuk menakuti orang; singkatnya, segala yang dilakukan di tempat lain oleh peri, boggart, atau makhluk serupa dilakukan di Devon oleh para Pixie.
claims.quote: Others will make noises in walls, to frighten people. In short, everything that is done elsewhere by fairies, boggarts, or other like beings, is done in Devon by the Pixies.

claims.statement: In the tale Pixy-Vengeance, the Pixies, offended at a forgotten bucket of water, agree to punish a serving-girl with a lame leg for seven years, to be cured then by an herb growing on Dartmoor.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Pixy-Vengeance, para Pixie yang marah karena ember air mereka terlupa memutuskan menghukum seorang pelayan dengan kaki pincang selama tujuh tahun, yang baru sembuh dengan sejenis herba yang tumbuh di Dartmoor.
claims.quote: Once it was forgotten, and the Pixies forthwith came up to the girls' room, and loudly complained of the neglect. ... Various modes were proposed and rejected; at last it was agreed to give her a lame leg for a term of seven years, then to be cured by an herb growing on Dartmoor

claims.statement: In the tale The Pixy-Labour, the being cries out about the ointment, strikes the midwife's eye for "meddling with what did not belong to" her, and from that hour till her death she was blind of that eye.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah The Pixy-Labour, makhluk itu berseru tentang salep, memukul mata bidan karena "mencampuri apa yang bukan miliknya", dan sejak saat itu hingga ajalnya mata bidan itu buta.
claims.quote: "The ointment! the ointment!" cried he. "Take that, for meddling with what did not belong to you; you shall see me no more." He struck her eye as he spoke, and from that hour till the day of her death she was blind of that eye.

claims.statement: In the tale Pixy-Gratitude, by their magic power the Pixies made the tulips more beautiful and more permanent than any other tulips and made them emit a fragrance equal to that of the rose.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Pixy-Gratitude, dengan kuasa sihir mereka para Pixie membuat tulip lebih indah dan lebih awet daripada tulip lain, dan membuatnya menebarkan harum seperti mawar.
claims.quote: By their magic power they made the tulips more beautiful and more permanent than any other tulips, and they caused them to emit a fragrance equal to that of the rose.

claims.statement: When the tulips were taken up and the place made a parsley-bed, the power of the Pixies was shown again: the parsley withered and nothing would grow even in the other beds of the garden.
claims.statement_id: Ketika tulip dicabut dan tempatnya dijadikan petak peterseli, kuasa para Pixie kembali tampak: peterseli layu dan tidak ada yang tumbuh bahkan di petak-petak lain di kebun itu.
claims.quote: Again, however, the power of the Pixies was shown; the parsley withered, and nothing would grow even in the other beds of the garden.

claims.statement: A wight is a being or thing in Germanic languages; in Old English anything, more specific in Middle English; in modern fantasy often undead.
claims.statement_id: Wight berarti makhluk atau benda dalam bahasa Jermanik (Germanic); dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno (Old English) apa saja, lebih khusus dalam bahasa Inggris Pertengahan (Middle English).
claims.quote: A wight is a being or thing. This general meaning of the term is shared by its cognates in other Germanic languages, but their usages vary greatly over time and between regions. In Old English, it could refer to anything in existence, with more specificity arising in Middle English

claims.statement: Wight is cognate with German Wicht, Old Norse vættr, Swedish vätte and Danish vætte.
claims.statement_id: Wight sekerabat dengan Wicht (German, Jerman), vættr (Old Norse, Nordik Kuno), vätte (Swedish, Swedia), vætte (Danish, Denmark).
claims.quote: "Wight" is further cognate with Scots: wicht , German: Wicht , Dutch: Wicht , Gothic: 𐍅𐌰𐌹𐌷𐍄𐍃 and Old Norse: vættr , the ancestor of Swedish: vätte , Danish: vætte and Icelandic: vættur .

claims.statement: The eoten Grendel is called in Beowulf wiht unhaélo, that damned creature.
claims.statement_id: Eoten Grendel disebut dalam Beowulf wiht unhaélo, makhluk terkutuk (damned creature).
claims.quote: The eoten Grendel, who is described in Beowulf as wiht unhaélo ("that damned creature")

claims.statement: The term is used for the dwarf of the XCIIIB charm and the eoten Grendel and the dragon in Beowulf.
claims.statement_id: Istilah ini dipakai untuk kurcaci dalam mantra XCIIIB serta Grendel dan naga dalam Beowulf.
claims.quote: The term is also used to refer to beings such as the dwarf which is the focus of the XCIIIB charm, and the eoten Grendel and the dragon in Beowulf.

claims.statement: The word began to mean supernatural or unearthly beings, as in the 8th-century Lindisfarne Gospels.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini mulai bermakna makhluk gaib atau tak duniawi, seperti dalam Lindisfarne Gospels abad ke-8.
claims.quote: The word began to acquire the sense of supernatural or unearthly beings, included in the 8th century Lindisfarne Gospels.

claims.statement: Wichtel in tales (Märchen) and legends (Sagen) look human (menschenähnlich) but small, living in groups underground (unterirdisch), in caves (Höhlen) or corners of houses (Häusern).
claims.statement_id: Wichtel dalam dongeng (Märchen) dan legenda (Sagen) mirip manusia (menschenähnlich) tetapi kecil, hidup berkelompok di bawah tanah (unterirdisch), gua (Höhlen), atau sudut rumah (Häusern).
claims.quote: Als Wichtel werden in Märchen, Sagen und Erzählungen Wesen bezeichnet, die von der Gestalt und Art her menschenähnlich sind, aber deutlich kleiner und in eigenen Gemeinschaften lebend. Sie tauchen meist in Gruppen auf, leben unterirdisch, in Höhlen oder in versteckten Ecken in den Häusern der Menschen.

claims.statement: Wichtel is a diminutive (Diminutiv) of Wicht, which in old German (Altdeutschen) meant a living being (lebendes Wesen, Geschöpf).
claims.statement_id: Wichtel adalah bentuk kecil (Diminutiv) dari Wicht, yang dalam bahasa Jerman lama (Altdeutschen) berarti makhluk hidup (lebendes Wesen, Geschöpf).
claims.quote: Wichtel oder Wichtelmännchen ist ein Diminutiv von Wicht, einem Begriff, der im Altdeutschen allgemein für lebendes Wesen, Geschöpf stand.

claims.statement: Wichtel are friendly (freundlich), help with daily work (täglichen Arbeit), and sometimes swap a human child (menschliches Kind).
claims.statement_id: Wichtel ramah (freundlich), membantu pekerjaan sehari-hari (täglichen Arbeit), dan kadang menukar anak manusia (menschliches Kind).
claims.quote: Im Allgemeinen sind sie den Menschen gegenüber freundlich und helfen ihnen, meist unaufgefordert, bei der täglichen Arbeit. Bisweilen bitten sie ihrerseits die Menschen um Hilfe, manchmal tauschen sie ein menschliches Kind gegen ein eigenes aus.

claims.statement: In modern fantasy, wights are often specifically undead.
claims.statement_id: Dalam fantasi modern (modern fantasy), wight sering berarti mayat hidup (undead).
claims.quote: In modern fantasy, wights are often specifically undead.

claims.statement: In English-speaking cultures Christmas elves live with Santa Claus at the North Pole as helpers, clad in green or red, with pointy ears and hats.
claims.statement_id: Dalam budaya berbahasa Inggris (English-speaking), Christmas elves tinggal bersama Santa Claus di North Pole dan membantunya; berbaju hijau atau merah, bertelinga dan bertopi runcing.
claims.quote: In English-speaking cultures, Christmas elves are diminutive elves that live with Santa Claus at the North Pole and act as his helpers. Christmas elves are usually depicted as green- or red-clad, with large, pointy ears and wearing pointy hats.

claims.statement: They are humanoid or sometimes furry mammals; Santa's elves make toys in Santa's workshop and tend his reindeer.
claims.statement_id: Mereka humanoid atau kadang mamalia berbulu; elf Santa membuat mainan di bengkel Santa dan merawat rusa kutubnya.
claims.quote: They are most often depicted as humanoids, but sometimes as furry mammals with tails. Santa's elves are often said to make the toys in Santa's workshop and take care of his reindeer, among other tasks.

claims.statement: The link of Christmas presents with elves has precedents in the Scandinavian nisse or tomte in the 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Kaitan hadiah Natal dengan elf berakar pada nisse atau tomte Skandinavia (Scandinavian) abad ke-19.
claims.quote: The association of Christmas presents with elves has precedents in the first half of the 19th century with the Scandinavian nisse or tomte

claims.statement: In the 1823 poem A Visit from St. Nicholas, often attributed to Clement Clarke Moore, Santa Claus is called "a right jolly old elf".
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi A Visit from St. Nicholas (1823), sering dikaitkan dengan Clement Clarke Moore, Santa Claus disebut "a right jolly old elf".
claims.quote: In the 1823 poem A Visit from St. Nicholas (commonly known as 'Twas the Night Before Christmas), often attributed to Clement Clarke Moore, Santa Claus himself is described in line 45: "He was chubby and plump, a right jolly old elf".

claims.statement: The image of elves in the workshop was popularized by Godey's Lady's Book on its 1873 Christmas cover.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran elf di bengkel dipopulerkan Godey's Lady's Book lewat sampul edisi Natal (Christmas) 1873.
claims.quote: The image of elves in the workshop was popularized by Godey's Lady's Book, with a front cover illustration for its 1873 Christmas issue showing Santa surrounded by toys and elves

claims.statement: By 1891 the saint had merged with Tomten, a farm guardian; through Jenny Nyström the figure became Jultomten.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1891 sang santo menyatu dengan Tomten, penjaga pertanian; lewat karya Jenny Nyström menjadi Jultomten. Ini terjadi di Swedia (Sweden).
claims.quote: Prior to the influence of Saint Nicholas in Sweden, the job of giving out gifts was done by the Yule goat. By 1891, the saint had merged with Tomten, which was previously an elfish / dwarfish farm guardian. Following the work of Jenny Nyström, this hybrid figure became known as Jultomten.

claims.statement: In American, Canadian, Irish and British (Amerika, Kanada, Irlandia, Inggris) culture, Christmas elves live with Santa (Sinterklas) at the North Pole (Kutub Utara) as helpers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam budaya Amerika, Kanada, Irlandia, dan Inggris, kurcaci Natal tinggal dengan Sinterklas di Kutub Utara sebagai pembantunya.
claims.quote: Dalam budaya Amerika, Kanada, Irlandia, dan Inggris, kurcaci Natal adalah kurcaci yang tinggal dengan Sinterklas di Kutub Utara dan bertindak sebagai pembantunya.

claims.statement: Europe had elf-like beings such as kobolds from Germany and brownies in Scotland.
claims.statement_id: Di Eropa (Europe) ada makhluk serupa elf, seperti kobold dari Jerman (Germany) dan brownie di Skotlandia (Scotland).
claims.quote: In various regions of Europe there were similar supernatural beings that can be connected to elves, such as kobolds from Germany and house spirits named brownies in Scotland.

claims.statement: The 2003 Christmas film Elf.
claims.statement_id: Film Natal Elf (2003).
claims.quote: Sailors aboard USS Harry S. Truman watch a screening of the 2003 Christmas film Elf

claims.statement: According to Mental Floss, the 1857 poem "The Wonders of Santa Claus" in Harper's Weekly tells of a team of elves "all working with all their might" to make a million pretty things (cakes, sugar-plums and toys) to fill the stockings hung up by the little girls and boys.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mental Floss, puisi "The Wonders of Santa Claus" di Harper's Weekly tahun 1857 menceritakan sekelompok elf yang "semuanya bekerja dengan sekuat tenaga" membuat sejuta barang kecil yang cantik, yaitu kue, gula-gula, dan mainan, untuk mengisi kaus kaki yang digantung anak perempuan dan laki-laki.
claims.quote: A 1857 poem published in Harper’s Weekly likely did more to solidify the image of Christmas elves in pop culture. Titled “The Wonders of Santa Claus,” it tells of a team of elves “all working with all their might/To make a million of pretty things/Cakes, sugar-plums, and toys/To fill the stockings, hung up you know/By the little girls and boys.”

claims.statement: According to Mental Floss, in the Brothers Grimm fairytale "The Elves and the Shoemaker" (1812), the business of a poor cobbler struggling to finish his work before Christmas is saved by altruistic elves who visit his shop at night and make his shoes while he sleeps.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mental Floss, dalam dongeng "The Elves and the Shoemaker" (1812) karya Brothers Grimm, usaha seorang tukang sepatu miskin yang berjuang menyelesaikan pekerjaan sebelum Natal diselamatkan oleh elf yang baik hati, yang datang ke tokonya pada malam hari dan membuatkan sepatu sementara ia tidur.
claims.quote: In “The Elves and the Shoemaker,” the Brothers Grimm paint these stereotypically mischievous creatures in a positive light. The fairytale from 1812 follows a poor cobbler struggling to finish his work before Christmas. His business is saved by altruistic elves who visit his shop at night and make his shoes for him while he sleeps.

claims.statement: According to Mental Floss, Santa's helpers now star in hit movies, decorate holiday sweaters, and "spy" on people from their shelves.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mental Floss, para pembantu Santa kini membintangi film laris, menghiasi sweter liburan, dan "mengawasi" orang dari rak-rak mereka.
claims.quote: Santa’s helpers now star in hit movies, decorate our ugly holiday sweaters, and spy on us from our shelves.

claims.statement: In recent films (e.g. The Santa Clause series and The Christmas Chronicles), the elves' jobs also include operating the police and air forces that protect the North Pole, helping Santa outside the Pole when he is captured by the real-world police, and serving as Santa's secret-service-like bodyguards (Fred Claus).
claims.statement_id: Dalam film-film baru (misalnya seri The Santa Clause dan The Christmas Chronicles), tugas para elf juga mencakup menjalankan polisi dan angkatan udara yang melindungi Kutub Utara, membantu Santa di luar Kutub Utara ketika ia ditangkap polisi dunia nyata, dan menjadi pengawal mirip dinas rahasia bagi Santa (Fred Claus).
claims.quote: In recent films (e.g. The Santa Clause series and The Christmas Chronicles), the elves' jobs also include operating police and air forces protecting the North Pole, helping Santa outside the Pole when he is captured by the real-world police, and as Santa's secret-service-like bodyguards (Fred Claus).

claims.statement: The elves are generally said to live for hundreds, or even thousands, of years, although in some cases they appear eternally youthful like children.
claims.statement_id: Para elf umumnya dikatakan hidup ratusan bahkan ribuan tahun, meskipun dalam beberapa kasus mereka tampak awet muda seperti anak-anak.
claims.quote: The elves are generally said to live for hundreds, or even thousands, of years, despite the fact that in some cases they appear eternally youthful as children.

claims.statement: In the 2020 sequel The Christmas Chronicles 2, the elves are divided into two camps, and one faction of "naughty elves" led by Belsnickel plots to overthrow Santa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sekuel The Christmas Chronicles 2 (2020), para elf terbagi menjadi dua kubu, dan satu faksi "elf nakal" yang dipimpin Belsnickel merencanakan penggulingan Santa.
claims.quote: In the 2020 sequel The Christmas Chronicles 2, they are divided into two camps, with one faction of "naughty elves" led by Belsnickel, who plots to overthrow Santa.

claims.statement: A gremlin is a mischievous fictional creature invented in the early 20th century to explain aircraft and later machine malfunctions; depictions vary.
claims.statement_id: Gremlin adalah makhluk usil rekaan dari awal abad ke-20 untuk menjelaskan kerusakan pesawat, lalu mesin lain; gambarannya beragam.
claims.quote: A gremlin is a mischievous fictional creature invented at the beginning of the 20th century originally to explain malfunctions in aircraft, and later in other machinery, processes and their operators. Depictions of these creatures vary widely.
