claims.statement: The term for an aircraft saboteur arose in Royal Air Force (RAF) slang among British pilots in Malta, the Middle East and India in the 1920s; earliest print a poem in Aeroplane in Malta, 10 April 1929.
claims.statement_id: Kata gremlin untuk penyabotase pesawat muncul dalam slang Royal Air Force (RAF) di kalangan pilot Britania (British) di Malta, Middle East (Timur Tengah), dan India pada 1920-an; catatan tertua puisi di Aeroplane in Malta, 10 April 1929.
claims.quote: Use of the term in the sense of a mischievous creature that sabotages aircraft first arose in Royal Air Force (RAF) slang among British pilots stationed in Malta, the Middle East and India in the 1920s, with the earliest printed record in a poem published in the journal Aeroplane in Malta on 10 April 1929.

claims.statement: Folklorist John W. Hazen: some derive the name from Old English gremian, to vex; Carol Rose links it to Grimm's Fairy Tales and Fremlin beer.
claims.statement_id: Folklorist John W. Hazen: sebagian menurunkan namanya dari gremian (Old English, Inggris Kuno) "menjengkelkan"; Carol Rose mengaitkannya dengan Grimm's Fairy Tales dan bir Fremlin.
claims.quote: the folklorist John W. Hazen states that some people derive the name from the Old English word gremian, "to vex", while Carol Rose, in her book Spirits, Fairies, Leprechauns, and Goblins: An Encyclopedia, attributes the name to a portmanteau of Grimm's Fairy Tales and Fremlin Beer.

claims.statement: Flight crews blamed gremlins for inexplicable accidents; enemy aircraft turned out to have the same problems.
claims.statement_id: Awak pesawat menyalahkan gremlin atas kecelakaan tak terjelaskan; pesawat musuh ternyata mengalami masalah serupa.
claims.quote: The flight crews blamed gremlins for otherwise inexplicable accidents which sometimes occurred during their flights. Gremlins were also thought at one point to have enemy sympathies, but investigations revealed that enemy aircraft had similar and equally inexplicable mechanical problems.

claims.statement: According to Paul Quinion, the term may blend goblin with Fremlin, the commonest beer in the RAF in the 1920s.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Paul Quinion, kata ini mungkin gabungan goblin dengan Fremlin, bir paling umum di RAF pada 1920-an.
claims.quote: According to Paul Quinion, it is plausible that the term is a blend of the word "goblin" with the name of the manufacturer of the most common beer available in the RAF in the 1920s, Fremlin.

claims.statement: The British writer (britische Schriftsteller) Roald Dahl, who served in the Royal Air Force, published The Gremlins in 1943.
claims.statement_id: Penulis Britania (britische Schriftsteller) Roald Dahl, mantan anggota Royal Air Force, menerbitkan The Gremlins pada 1943.
claims.quote: Der britische Schriftsteller Roald Dahl, der auch in der Royal Air Force gedient hatte, veröffentlichte 1943 „The Gremlins“.

claims.statement: The Gremlin, like other kinds of kobold (Koboldarten), loves mischief (Schabernack), above all with machines (maschinellen) and technology (technischen).
claims.statement_id: Gremlin, seperti jenis kobold (Koboldarten) lain, gemar berbuat usil (Schabernack), terutama di bidang mesin (maschinellen) dan teknik (technischen).
claims.quote: Der Gremlin hat, wie viele andere Koboldarten auch, Spaß am Schabernack, vor allem im maschinellen und technischen Bereich.

claims.statement: The gremlin concept was popularized in World War II among Royal Air Force airmen.
claims.statement_id: Konsep gremlin dipopulerkan pada Perang Dunia II (World War II) di kalangan penerbang Royal Air Force.
claims.quote: This concept of gremlins was popularized during World War II among airmen of the Royal Air Force (RAF) units

claims.statement: Lir or Ler (Old Irish 'Sea') is a sea god of Irish mythology, a personification of the sea, called Allód in early genealogies, matching Llŷr of Welsh mythology.
claims.statement_id: Lir atau Ler (Sea, laut, dalam Old Irish) adalah dewa laut mitologi Irlandia (Irish mythology), personifikasi laut, bernama Allód dalam silsilah awal, sepadan dengan Llŷr mitologi Wales (Welsh).
claims.quote: Lir or Ler (meaning "Sea" in Old Irish; Ler and Lir are the nominative and genitive forms, respectively) is a sea god in Irish mythology. His name suggests that he is a personification of the sea, rather than a distinct deity. He is named Allód in early genealogies, and corresponds to the Llŷr of Welsh mythology.

claims.statement: Lir is chiefly an ancestor, father of the god Manannán mac Lir of medieval Irish literature.
claims.statement_id: Lir tokoh leluhur, ayah dewa Manannán mac Lir dalam sastra Irlandia (Irish) abad pertengahan.
claims.quote: Lir is chiefly an ancestor figure, and is the father of the god Manannán mac Lir, who appears frequently in medieval Irish literature.

claims.statement: Lir, like the Welsh Llŷr, is a sea god; in Gaelic myth his son Manannán mac Lir takes over his place.
claims.statement_id: Lir, seperti Llŷr (Welsh), dewa laut; dalam mitos Gaelik (Gaelic) putranya Manannán mac Lir mengambil alih kedudukannya.
claims.quote: Lir, like his Welsh counterpart Llŷr, is a god of the sea, though in the case of the Gaelic myths his son Manannán mac Lir seems to take over his position and so features more prominently.

claims.statement: Lir is key in The Children of Lir, perhaps not Manannán's father; he was Bodb Dearg's rival for the kingship of the Tuatha Dé Danann.
claims.statement_id: Lir tokoh utama The Children of Lir, tak pasti sama dengan ayah Manannán; ia saingan Bodb Dearg memperebutkan takhta Tuatha Dé Danann.
claims.quote: Lir is a key character in the mythological story The Children of Lir; however, it is not definitely established whether this is the same person as Manannán's father or a different Lir. The Lir in this story was the rival of Bodb Dearg for the kingship of the Tuatha Dé Danann after their retreat into the fairy mounds.

claims.statement: Bodb gave Lir his daughter Aeb; they had Fionnuala, Aed, Fiachra and Conn.
claims.statement_id: Bodb menikahkan Lir dengan putrinya Aeb; mereka beranak Fionnuala, Aed, Fiachra, dan Conn.
claims.quote: In order to appease Lir, Bodb gave one of his daughters to marry him, Aeb. The couple had four children, one girl, Fionnuala, and three sons, Aed and twins, Fiachra and Conn.

claims.statement: Lir married Aobh's sister (Schwester) Aoife, who from jealousy (Eifersucht) turned the children (Kinder) into swans (Schwäne); they wandered for 900 years (Jahre).
claims.statement_id: Lir menikahi Aoife, saudari (Schwester) Aobh, yang karena cemburu (Eifersucht) mengubah anak-anak (Kinder) menjadi angsa (Schwäne); mereka mengembara 900 tahun (Jahre).
claims.quote: Lir heiratete daraufhin Aobhs Schwester Aoife, die jedoch kinderlos bleibt und aus Eifersucht und Neid versucht, die Kinder ihrer Schwester zu töten. Als sie dies doch nicht übers Herz bringt, verwandelt sie die Kinder stattdessen in Schwäne. Die vier Kinder müssen 900 Jahre lang umherirren

claims.statement: Ler ('Sea' in old Irish; Lir the genitive) is a sea god of Irish (Irlandia) mythology, a personification of the sea (laut).
claims.statement_id: Ler (Laut dalam bahasa Irlandia kuno; Lir bentuk genitif) dewa laut mitologi Irlandia, personifikasi laut.
claims.quote: Ler (berarti "Laut" dalam bahasa Irlandia kuno; Lir adalah bentuk genitif) adalah dewa laut dalam mitologi Irlandia. Nama-nya menunjukkan bahwa ia adalah personifikasi dari laut, bukan dewa yang berbeda.

claims.statement: Nibelung (German) or Niflungr (Old Norse) is a personal or clan name of Germanic legend, tied to Nebel ('mist'), naming the Middle High German Nibelungenlied.
claims.statement_id: Nibelung (German) atau Niflungr (Old Norse) adalah nama pribadi atau klan dalam legenda Jermanik (Germanic), dikaitkan dengan Nebel (kabut, mist), dan memberi nama Nibelungenlied (Middle High German).
claims.quote: The term Nibelung (German) or Niflungr (Old Norse) is a personal or clan name with several competing and contradictory uses in Germanic heroic legend. It has an unclear etymology, but is often connected to the root of German Nebel , meaning 'mist'. The term in its various meanings gives its name to the Middle High German heroic epic the Nibelungenlied .

claims.statement: Nibelung mostly names the Burgundian royal house, Gibichungen or Gjúkingar, led by Gunther or Gunnar, who killed Siegfried or Sigurd and were destroyed at Attila the Hun's court.
claims.statement_id: Nibelung terutama keluarga kerajaan Burgundia (Burgundian), Gibichungen atau Gjúkingar, dipimpin Gunther atau Gunnar, penyebab kematian Siegfried atau Sigurd, dihancurkan di istana Attila the Hun.
claims.quote: The most widespread use of the term Nibelung denotes the Burgundian royal house, also known as the Gibichungen (German) or Gjúkingar (Old Norse). A group of royal brothers led by king Gunther or Gunnar, the Gibichungs are responsible for the death of the hero Siegfried or Sigurd and are later destroyed at the court of Attila the Hun

claims.statement: Nibelung also names the king and people of a mythical land of dwarfs and giants in the Nibelungenlied, origin of the hoard of the Nibelungs.
claims.statement_id: Nibelung juga raja dan penghuni negeri mitos kurcaci dan raksasa dalam Nibelungenlied, asal nama harta Nibelung (hoard of the Nibelungs).
claims.quote: it refers to the king and inhabitants of a mythical land inhabited by dwarfs and giants in the first half of the Nibelungenlied, as well as to the father and one of two brothers fighting over a divided inheritance. This land and its inhabitants give their name to the "hoard of the Nibelungs"

claims.statement: Medieval German documents other uses of Nibelung besides the Gibichungs.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Jerman (German) abad pertengahan ada pemakaian Nibelung lain selain Gibichung.
claims.quote: In medieval German, several other uses of the term Nibelung are documented besides the reference to the Gibichungs

claims.statement: The nibelungos are a mythical people (pueblo mitológico) of Germanic (germanas) legend ruled by prince (príncipe) Nibelung, dark dwarfs (enanos oscuros) deep in the earth (tierra) mining gold (oro).
claims.statement_id: Nibelungo (nibelungos) bangsa mitos (pueblo mitológico) legenda Jermanik (germanas) dipimpin pangeran (príncipe) Nibelung, kurcaci gelap (enanos oscuros) di dalam bumi (tierra) yang menambang emas (oro).
claims.quote: Los nibelungos (en alemán Nibelung, en nórdico antiguo Niflungr) son un pueblo mitológico de las leyendas germanas gobernado por el príncipe «Nibelung». Eran enanos oscuros que vivían en las profundidades de la tierra y se dedicaban a la extracción de metales preciosos, particularmente oro.

claims.statement: They held a treasure (tesoro) at the bottom of the Rin (Rhine) stolen from the nymphs (ninfas); their king owned a cursed magic ring (anillo); Sigfrido killed Nibelung and Schilbung over sharing the hoard.
claims.statement_id: Mereka memiliki harta (tesoro) di dasar sungai Rin (Rhein) yang dicuri dari peri air (ninfas); raja mereka punya cincin (anillo) sakti pembawa sial; Sigfrido membunuh Nibelung dan Schilbung soal pembagian harta.
claims.quote: Poseían un enorme tesoro que se encontraba en el fondo del río Rin y que habían robado a las ninfas que lo custodiaban. El rey de los nibelungos poseía un anillo que tenía poderosas propiedades mágicas y atraía la desgracia a su portador. El caballero Sigfrido mató a los príncipes nibelungos Nibelung y Schilbung tras discutir con ellos sobre la forma de repartir el tesoro.

claims.statement: The composer (compositor) Richard Wagner wrote a cycle of four operas (óperas), El anillo del nibelungo, based on these legends.
claims.statement_id: Komponis (compositor) Richard Wagner menggubah siklus empat opera (óperas) El anillo del nibelungo berdasarkan legenda ini.
claims.quote: Posteriormente, el compositor Richard Wagner, basándose en estas leyendas mitológicas, compuso un ciclo de cuatro óperas titulado El anillo del nibelungo

claims.statement: In Needler's introduction the hoard belongs to Siegfried (Sigurd), who has slain its previous owners, Schilbung and Nibelung, and wrested it from its guardian, the dwarf Alberich (Andvari).
claims.statement_id: Dalam pengantar terjemahan Needler, harta itu menjadi milik Siegfried (Sigurd), yang telah membunuh pemilik sebelumnya, Schilbung dan Nibelung, dan merebutnya dari penjaganya, kurcaci Alberich (Andvari).
claims.quote: to Siegfried (Sigurd), who has slain the previous owners of it, Schilbung and Nibelung, and wrested it from its guardian the dwarf Alberich (Andvari).

claims.statement: In Needler's translation, twelve of their followers are keen warriors as strong as giants; Siegfried slew them in anger and felled seven hundred warriors in Nibelungenland.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Needler, dua belas pengikut mereka adalah prajurit tangkas yang sekuat raksasa; Siegfried membunuh mereka dalam amarah, dan menumbangkan tujuh ratus prajurit di Nibelungenland.
claims.quote: They had there of their followers / twelve warriors keen, And strong they were as giants: / what booted giants e'en? Them slew straightway in anger / Siegfried's mighty hand, And warriors seven hundred / he felled in Nibelungenland

claims.statement: In Needler's translation, Siegfried saw such a store of gems that they could not be loaded on a full five score of wagons, and more still of shining gold from Nibelungenland.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Needler, Siegfried melihat permata begitu banyak sehingga tidak dapat dimuat di seratus gerobak, dan emas berkilau yang lebih banyak lagi dari Nibelungenland.
claims.quote: he saw of gems such store That they might not be laden / on wagons full five score; More still of gold all shining / from Nibelungenland.

claims.statement: In Needler's translation, Siegfried slew the two mighty kings as well, but fell into gravest danger through Alberich, who thought to wreak vengeance at once for his slain masters, until Siegfried stayed his wrath with his strong arm.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Needler, Siegfried membunuh kedua raja yang perkasa itu pula, tetapi ia jatuh ke dalam bahaya besar karena Alberich, yang hendak segera membalas dendam atas tuan-tuannya yang terbunuh, sampai Siegfried menahan amarahnya dengan lengan yang kuat.
claims.quote: Thereto the kings so mighty, / them slew he both as well. But into gravest danger / through Alberich he fell, Who thought for his slain masters / vengeance to wreak straightway, Until the mighty Siegfried / his wrath with strong arm did stay.

claims.statement: In Needler's translation, the Dwarf could not prevail against Siegfried however he tried; they coursed the mountainside like two wild lions.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Needler, sang Kurcaci tidak dapat mengalahkan Siegfried sekeras apa pun ia mencoba; keduanya berkejaran di lereng gunung seperti dua singa liar.
claims.quote: Nor could prevail against him / the Dwarf, howe'er he tried. E'en as two wild lions / they coursed the mountainside

claims.statement: Needler's footnote says the sightless mantle Siegfried won from Alberich is the tarnkappe, a cloak that made the wearer invisible and also gave him the strength of twelve men.
claims.statement_id: Catatan kaki Needler menyatakan jubah tak terlihat yang direbut Siegfried dari Alberich adalah tarnkappe, jubah yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat dan juga memberinya kekuatan dua belas orang.
claims.quote: This is the tarnkappe, a cloak that made the wearer invisible, and also gave him the strength of twelve men.

claims.statement: In Needler's translation, Siegfried orders Alberich to bring him knights, the best they have to show, a thousand Nibelungen, to stand before their lord.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Needler, Siegfried memerintahkan Alberich membawa kepadanya ksatria terbaik, seribu orang Nibelungen, untuk berdiri di hadapan tuan mereka.
claims.quote: bring me knights hither, / the best we have to show, A thousand Nibelungen, / to stand before their lord.

claims.statement: In Needler's translation, Hagen took all that treasure and sank it in the Rhine where Loch is by the river; he thought to profit by it, yet that could never be.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Needler, Hagen mengambil seluruh harta itu dan menenggelamkannya di Sungai Rhine, di tempat bernama Loch; ia mengira akan beruntung karenanya, tetapi hal itu tidak pernah terjadi.
claims.quote: In that while had Hagen / all that treasure ta'en. Where Loch is by the river / all in the Rhine sank he. He weened thereof to profit, / yet such thing might never be.

claims.statement: In the Volsunga saga, after Loki takes his gold, the dwarf Andvari goes into a hollow of the rocks and cries out that the gold ring, and all the gold with it, shall be the bane of every man who owns it thereafter.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Volsunga saga, setelah Loki merampas emasnya, kurcaci Andvari masuk ke celah batu dan berseru bahwa cincin emas itu, dan seluruh emasnya, akan menjadi bencana bagi setiap orang yang memilikinya sesudahnya.
claims.quote: then the dwarf went into a hollow of the rocks, and cried out, that that gold-ring, yea and all the gold withal, should be the bane of every man who should own it thereafter.

claims.statement: In the Volsunga saga, the dwarf Andvari always abode in the force called Andvari's force, in the likeness of a pike, and got meat for himself there.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Volsunga saga, kurcaci Andvari selalu tinggal di air terjun yang disebut air terjun Andvari, dalam rupa ikan tombak, dan mencari makan di sana.
claims.quote: there was a dwarf called Andvari, who ever abode in that force, (1) which was called Andvari's force, in the likeness of a pike, and got meat for himself

claims.statement: Borvo (Bormo) was a Celtic god of thermal and healing springs in Roman Gaul and the Iberian Peninsula; equated with Apollo, at Aix-en-Provence with Hercules; his partner was Damona.
claims.statement_id: Borvo (Bormo) dewa Kelt (Celtic) mata air panas dan penyembuh, dipuja di Galia Romawi (Roman Gaul) hingga Semenanjung Iberia (Iberian Peninsula); disamakan dengan Apollo, di Aix-en-Provence dengan Hercules; pasangannya Damona.
claims.quote: Borvo, also Bormo, was an ancient Celtic god of thermal and healing springs. His cult is attested across a wide area of Roman Gaul and reached the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula. Under the interpretatio romana he was usually identified with Apollo, and at Aix-en-Provence instead with Hercules. His most frequent divine partner was the goddess Damona.

claims.statement: The Gaulish name Boruō means 'hot spring', from Proto-Celtic berw-, 'boil'.
claims.statement_id: Nama Galia (Gaulish) Boruō berarti mata air panas, dari akar Proto-Kelt (Proto-Celtic) berw-, mendidih.
claims.quote: The Gaulish theonym Boruō means 'hot spring', 'warm source'. It stems from the Proto-Celtic verbal root berw- ('boil, brew'

claims.statement: Borvo is god of warm curative spring waters; evidence is almost all votive inscriptions at Gallo-Roman spas.
claims.statement_id: Borvo dewa air hangat mata air panas yang berkhasiat; buktinya hampir seluruhnya prasasti persembahan di pemandian Galia-Romawi (Gallo-Roman).
claims.quote: Borvo is generally interpreted as a god of the warm, welling waters of thermal springs, which were held to be curative. The evidence for his worship is almost entirely epigraphic, in the form of votive dedications set up at Gallo-Roman spa sites.

claims.statement: A relief from Entrains shows him with goblet, money bag and fruit; one from Vichy shows him naked on a rock with a bubbling cup.
claims.statement_id: Relief dari Entrains menampilkannya dengan piala, kantong uang, dan buah; relief dari Vichy menampilkannya telanjang di batu memegang cawan berbuih.
claims.quote: A relief from Entrains shows him with a goblet, a money bag and a plate of fruit, features that have been taken to mark a god of plenty and wealth. A relief from Vichy shows him seated naked on a rock, holding a cup from which liquid bubbles over.

claims.statement: Many spring-town names derive from Borvo, including Bourbon, Bourbonne and La Bourboule.
claims.statement_id: Banyak nama tempat dekat mata air berasal dari Borvo, termasuk Bourbon, Bourbonne, dan La Bourboule.
claims.quote: Numerous toponyms of settlements linked to springs are derived from Borvo or Bormo, including Bourbon, Bourbonne, Boulbon, Bormes, Bourbriac, La Bourboule and Worms.

claims.statement: Bormo (Borvo, Bormanus, deus Bormanicus in Portugal) is a Celtic healing god (keltischen Heil-Gottes).
claims.statement_id: Bormo (Borvo, Bormanus, deus Bormanicus di Portugal) adalah dewa penyembuh Kelt (keltischen Heil-Gottes).
claims.quote: Bormo, auch Borvo, Bormanus oder deus Bormanicus (im heutigen Portugal), ist der Name eines keltischen Heil-Gottes.

claims.statement: Borvo/Bormo survives in the French place names (französischen Ortsnamen) Bourbonne-les-Bains and Bourbon-Lancy.
claims.statement_id: Borvo atau Bormo masih ada dalam nama tempat Prancis (französischen Ortsnamen) Bourbonne-les-Bains dan Bourbon-Lancy.
claims.quote: Borvo/Bormo ist noch heute in den französischen Ortsnamen Bourbonne-les-Bains (Département Haute-Marne) und Bourbon-Lancy (Département Saône-et-Loire) zu finden.

claims.statement: The name Borvo derives from the Celtic word for boil (kochen), linked to his role as local god of hot springs (heißen Quellen).
claims.statement_id: Nama Borvo dari kata Kelt untuk mendidih (kochen), terkait perannya sebagai dewa lokal mata air panas (heißen Quellen).
claims.quote: Der Name Borvo wird vom keltischen Wort für „kochen“ hergeleitet, er hängt mit seiner Funktion als Lokalgottheit bei heißen Quellen zusammen („der Kochende/Sprudelnde“).

claims.statement: The nuckelavee is a horse-like demon of Orcadian folklore, seeming a horseman but a fleshless one-eyed finned horse with a fleshless human torso on its back.
claims.statement_id: Nuckelavee iblis serupa kuda cerita rakyat Orkney (Orcadian folklore), tampak seperti penunggang kuda, tetapi kuda tanpa kulit bermata satu bersirip dengan tubuh manusia tanpa kulit di punggungnya.
claims.quote: is a horse-like demon from Orcadian folklore that combines equine and human elements. If one was looking casually, or under the cover of shadow in the night, it was thought to have the silhouette of a normal horseman. However, upon further inspection, it resembles a fleshless horse which sports one eye and fins on its legs

claims.statement: British folklorist Katharine Briggs called it the nastiest of the demons of Scotland's Northern Isles.
claims.statement_id: Folklorist Britania (British) Katharine Briggs menyebutnya yang paling keji di antara iblis Northern Isles Skotlandia (Scotland).
claims.quote: British folklorist Katharine Briggs called it "the nastiest" of all the demons of Scotland's Northern Isles.

claims.statement: The nuckelavee's breath wilts crops and sickens livestock; it was blamed for droughts and epidemics though it lives in the sea.
claims.statement_id: Napas nuckelavee melayukan tanaman, menyakiti ternak, dan ia disalahkan atas kekeringan dan wabah meski hidup di laut.
claims.quote: The nuckelavee's breath was thought to wilt crops and sicken livestock and the creature was held responsible for droughts and epidemics on land despite being predominantly a sea-dweller.

claims.statement: Like other sea monsters it cannot tolerate fresh water; those it chases need only cross a stream.
claims.statement_id: Seperti monster laut lain, ia tak tahan air tawar; orang yang dikejarnya cukup menyeberangi sungai.
claims.quote: In common with many other sea monsters, it is unable to tolerate fresh water. Therefore, those it is pursuing have only to cross a river or stream to be rid of it.

claims.statement: The nuckelavee is confined in summer by the Mither o' the Sea, an ancient Orcadian spirit who controls it.
claims.statement_id: Nuckelavee dikurung pada musim panas oleh Mither o' the Sea, roh Orkney (Orcadian) kuno yang dapat mengendalikannya.
claims.quote: The nuckelavee is kept in confinement during the summer months by the Mither o' the Sea, an ancient Orcadian spirit, and the only one able to control it.

claims.statement: Nuckelavee comes from Orcadian knoggelvi, per Walter Traill Dennison of Orkney 'Devil of the Sea'; in Shetland it is mukkelevi.
claims.statement_id: Nuckelavee dari knoggelvi (Orcadian), menurut Walter Traill Dennison dari Orkney berarti Iblis Laut (Devil of the Sea); di Shetland disebut mukkelevi.
claims.quote: The term nuckelavee derives from Orcadian knoggelvi, and according to Orkney resident and 19th-century folklorist Walter Traill Dennison means "Devil of the Sea". The same demon is called a mukkelevi in Shetland

claims.statement: Orcadian folklore had strong Scandinavian influence; the nuckelavee may blend a Celtic water horse with a creature of the Norsemen; like the kelpie it explained puzzling events.
claims.statement_id: Cerita rakyat Orkney dipengaruhi Skandinavia (Scandinavian); nuckelavee mungkin gabungan kuda air Kelt (Celtic) dan makhluk bangsa Nordik (Norsemen); seperti kelpie, ia menjelaskan kejadian yang tak dipahami.
claims.quote: Orcadian folklore had a strong Scandinavian influence, and it may be that the nuckelavee is a composite of a water horse from Celtic mythology and a creature imported by the Norsemen. As with similar malevolent entities such as the kelpie, it possibly offered an explanation for incidents that islanders in ancient times could not otherwise understand.

claims.statement: The nuckelavee is a horse-like evil spirit (roh jahat) of Orkney folklore (cerita rakyat Orkney) combining horse and human.
claims.statement_id: Nuckelavee adalah roh jahat serupa kuda dari cerita rakyat Orkney yang menggabungkan kuda dan manusia.
claims.quote: Nuckelavee (pengucapan: /nʌklɑːˈviː/) atau nuckalavee adalah roh jahat serupa kuda dari cerita rakyat Orkney yang menggabungkan elemen kuda dan manusia.

claims.statement: In Northern English folklore the Barghest (Barguest) is a monstrous black dog with large teeth and claws, or a ghost or household elf in Northumberland and Durham, like the Cauld Lad of Hylton.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris Utara (Northern English folklore), Barghest (Barguest) anjing hitam mengerikan bergigi dan bercakar besar, atau hantu atau elf rumah di Northumberland dan Durham, seperti Cauld Lad of Hylton.
claims.quote: In Northern English folklore, the Barghest or Barguest is a mythical monstrous black dog with large teeth and claws; however, in other cases, the name can refer to a ghost or household elf, especially in Northumberland and Durham, such as the Cauld Lad of Hylton.

claims.statement: Ghost was pronounced guest in Northern England, so the name may be burh-ghest; or from German Berg-geist, Bär-geist or Bahr-Geist.
claims.statement_id: Ghost di Inggris Utara (Northern England) diucapkan guest, sehingga namanya mungkin burh-ghest; atau dari Berg-geist, Bär-geist, Bahr-Geist (German, Jerman).
claims.quote: "Ghost" in Northern England was pronounced "guest", and the origin is thought to be of the combination burh-ghest, "town-ghost". Others explain it as cognate to German Berg-geist, "mountain ghost" or Bär-geist, "bear-ghost". Another mooted derivation is Bahr-Geist, German for the "spirit of the funeral bier".

claims.statement: In Yorkshire, England, a Barghest haunts the gorge of Troller's Gill in the Yorkshire Dales; the ballad The Legend of the Troller's Gill is in William Hone's Everyday Book (1830).
claims.statement_id: Di Yorkshire (England), Barghest menghantui ngarai Troller's Gill di Yorkshire Dales; balada The Legend of the Troller's Gill ada dalam Everyday Book karya William Hone (1830).
claims.quote: In Yorkshire, England, one notable case is said to frequent a remote gorge named Troller's Gill in the Yorkshire Dales. A ballad entitled "The Legend of the Troller's Gill" can be found in William Hone's Everyday Book (1830).

claims.statement: In 1870s Durham a shapeshifting Barghest near Darlington took the form of a headless man or lady, a white cat, rabbit or black dog.
claims.statement_id: Di Durham pada 1870-an Barghest yang berubah wujud tinggal dekat Darlington, menjelma lelaki atau perempuan tanpa kepala, kucing putih, kelinci, atau anjing hitam.
claims.quote: In Durham, during the 1870s a shapeshifting Barghest was said to live near Darlington and was said to take the form of a headless man (who would vanish in flames), a headless lady, a white cat, a rabbit, a dog, or a black dog.

claims.statement: The Barghest is an omen of death; at a notable death it appears followed by the local dogs in a funeral procession.
claims.statement_id: Barghest pertanda kematian; saat tokoh meninggal ia muncul diikuti anjing-anjing setempat dalam semacam iring-iringan jenazah.
claims.quote: The Barghest often allegedly serves as an omen of death. At the passing of a notable person the Barghest may appear, followed by all the other dogs of the local area in a kind of funeral procession, heralding the person's death with howling and barking.

claims.statement: Besides a fiery-eyed black dog it can go invisible with rattling chains, foretell death lying across a threshold, and like the vampire cannot cross rivers.
claims.statement_id: Selain anjing hitam bermata api, ia dapat tak terlihat dengan bunyi rantai, meramalkan kematian dengan berbaring di ambang pintu, dan seperti vampir tak dapat menyeberangi sungai.
claims.quote: Besides taking the form of a large black dog with fiery eyes, it may also become invisible and walk about with the sound of rattling chains. It may also foretell the death of an individual by lying across the threshold of his or her house, and like the vampire the Barghest is unable to cross rivers.

claims.statement: The Barghest (Bargtjest, Bo-guest, Bargest) is a mythical black dog (mythischer Schwarzer Hund) believed in northern England (Norden Englands), especially Yorkshire.
claims.statement_id: Barghest (Bargtjest, Bo-guest, Bargest) adalah anjing hitam mitos (mythischer Schwarzer Hund) yang dipercaya di utara Inggris (Norden Englands), terutama Yorkshire.
claims.quote: Der Barghest (auch „Bargtjest“, „Bo-guest“ oder „Bargest“) ist ein mythischer Schwarzer Hund, an den man im Norden Englands, insbesondere in Yorkshire, glaubte.

claims.statement: A tale says it sometimes enters the city (Stadt) of York to stalk lone travellers (einsamen Reisenden) in narrow streets.
claims.statement_id: Ada cerita ia kadang memasuki kota (Stadt) York dan mengintai pelancong sendirian (einsamen Reisenden) di jalan sempit.
claims.quote: Es gibt eine Geschichte, wonach er gelegentlich in die Stadt York eindringt und dann einsamen Reisenden auf den engen Straßen der Stadt auflauert.

claims.statement: Some say it is not a ghost (Geist) but a kobold (Kobold) able to turn into a dog (Hundeform).
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian sumber ia bukan hantu (Geist), melainkan kobold (Kobold) yang dapat berubah menjadi anjing (Hundeform).
claims.quote: Er soll kein Geist sein, sondern eher ein Kobold, der sich unter anderem in eine Hundeform verwandeln kann.

claims.statement: The Dullahan (Dubhlachan, dúlachán) is a legendary creature of Irish folklore, a headless rider on a black horse or coachman carrying his own head.
claims.statement_id: Dullahan (Dubhlachan, dúlachán) adalah makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore), penunggang kuda hitam tanpa kepala atau kusir yang membawa kepalanya sendiri.
claims.quote: The Dullahan (Irish: Dubhlachan; dúlachán, /ˈduːləˌhɑːn/) is a type of legendary creature in Irish folklore. He is depicted as a headless rider on a black horse, or as a coachman, who carries his own head.

claims.statement: Per the lexicographer Edward O'Reilly, Dullahan (Dulachan), meaning a hobgoblin, signifies a dark, sullen person.
claims.statement_id: Menurut leksikografer Edward O'Reilly, Dullahan (Dulachan) yang mengacu pada hobgoblin berarti orang gelap dan murung.
claims.quote: Dullahan or Dulachan (Irish: Dubhlachan [Duḃlaċan]) referring to "hobgoblin" (generic term; cf. Dullahan described as "unseelie (wicked) fairy"), literally "signifies dark, sullen person", according to the lexicographer Edward O'Reilly.

claims.statement: The Dullahan is also called Colainn Gan Cheann, 'without a head' in Irish.
claims.statement_id: Dullahan juga disebut Colainn Gan Cheann, tanpa kepala (without a head) dalam bahasa Irlandia (Irish).
claims.quote: The Dullahan is also called Colainn Gan Cheann, meaning "without a head" in Irish.

claims.statement: The Dullahan's vehicle is the Cóiste Gan Cheann (Headless Coach) or cóiste bodhar (Soundless Coach), in Hiberno-English coach-a-bower.
claims.statement_id: Kendaraan Dullahan disebut Cóiste Gan Cheann (Headless Coach) atau cóiste bodhar (Soundless Coach), dalam Hiberno-English coach-a-bower.
claims.quote: "Headless Coach" (Irish: Cóiste Gan Cheann ) or the "Soundless Coach" (literally "deaf coach", Irish: cóiste bodhar ; Hiberno-English: Coshta Bower, corrupted to "coach-a-bower") is the name given to the vehicle driven by the Dullahan.

claims.statement: In Croker's tale the head looks like a large cream cheese hung with black puddings, ashen pale, with two fiery eyes flashing like meteors.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Croker, kepalanya seperti keju krim besar dikelilingi puding hitam, pucat abu, dengan dua mata berapi (fiery eyes) yang berkilat seperti meteor.
claims.quote: It looked like a large cream cheese hung round with black puddings: no speck of colour enlivened the ashy paleness of the depressed features; the skin lay stretched over the unearthly surface almost like the parchment head of a drum. Two fiery eyes of prodigious circumference, with a strange and irregular motion, flashed like meteors.

claims.statement: The Dullahan (Gan Ceann, kopflos) of Irish mythology (irischen Mythologie) is an evil being (böses Wesen), a headless rider or knight (kopfloser Reiter, Ritter), usually fallen soldiers (Soldaten) and heroes (Helden).
claims.statement_id: Dullahan (Gan Ceann, kopflos) dari mitologi Irlandia (irischen Mythologie) adalah makhluk jahat (böses Wesen), penunggang atau kesatria tanpa kepala (kopfloser Reiter, Ritter), biasanya arwah prajurit (Soldaten) dan pahlawan (Helden) yang gugur.
claims.quote: Der Begriff Dullahan (im Irischen auch Gan Ceann, zu deutsch „kopflos“) stammt aus der irischen Mythologie und bezeichnet eine Art böses Wesen, welches als kopfloser Reiter oder auch kopfloser Ritter in Erscheinung tritt. Es handelt sich meist um gefallene Soldaten und Helden, die als Geistererscheinung in Form eines kopflosen Reiters weiterleben.

claims.statement: Armed with armour (Rüstung), shield (Schild) and sword (Schwert), the Dullahan is read as a death omen (Todesomen); usually male (männliche), sometimes female (weiblich).
claims.statement_id: Bersenjata baju zirah (Rüstung), perisai (Schild), dan pedang (Schwert), Dullahan ditafsirkan sebagai pertanda kematian (Todesomen); biasanya laki-laki (männliche), bisa perempuan (weiblich).
claims.quote: Mit Rüstung, Schild und Schwert bewaffnet ist der Dullahan in den meisten mythologischen Sagen als Todesomen zu deuten. Dullahan werden meist als männliche Wesen dargestellt, können jedoch auch weiblich sein.

claims.statement: In English folklore Herne the Hunter is a ghost of Windsor Forest and Great Park in Berkshire, antlered, horse-riding, tormenting cattle and rattling chains.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), Herne the Hunter adalah hantu Windsor Forest dan Great Park di Berkshire, bertanduk rusa, menunggang kuda, menyiksa ternak, dan menggemerincingkan rantai.
claims.quote: In English folklore, Herne the Hunter is a ghost associated with Windsor Forest and Great Park in the English county of Berkshire. He is said to have antlers growing from his head, ride a horse, torment cattle, and rattle chains.

claims.statement: Herne is first mentioned in William Shakespeare's 1597 play The Merry Wives of Windsor; how far it used a real local legend is unknown.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan tertua Herne dari lakon William Shakespeare The Merry Wives of Windsor (1597); tak diketahui seberapa jauh ia memakai legenda setempat.
claims.quote: The earliest mention of Herne comes from William Shakespeare's 1597 play The Merry Wives of Windsor, and it is impossible to know how accurately or to what degree Shakespeare may have incorporated a real local legend into his work

claims.statement: Shakespeare: all winter at midnight Herne walks round an oak with great ragged horns, blasts the tree, makes milch-kine yield blood and shakes a chain.
claims.statement_id: Shakespeare: sepanjang musim dingin, tengah malam, Herne mengelilingi pohon ek dengan tanduk besar, merusak pohon, membuat sapi perah (milch-kine) mengeluarkan darah, dan menggemerincingkan rantai.
claims.quote: Doth all the winter-time, at still midnight Walk round about an oak, with great ragg'd horns; And there he blasts the tree, and takes the cattle, And makes milch-kine yield blood, and shakes a chain In a most hideous and dreadful manner.

claims.statement: The 1602 first quarto says the ghost, Horne, was invented to scare children into obedience, walking the forest as a great stag.
claims.statement_id: Kuarto pertama (1602) menyebut hantu Horne diciptakan untuk menakuti anak-anak agar patuh, berwujud rusa jantan besar.
claims.quote: The first quarto of the play from 1602 includes a different version of this text, which states that the ghost (spelled "Horne" in this version) was invented to scare children into obedience, and that mothers tell their children the tale of a ghost who walks the forest in the form of a great stag.

claims.statement: Official versions call Herne the ghost of a former Windsor Forest keeper haunting an oak at midnight in winter.
claims.statement_id: Versi resmi lakon menyebut Herne arwah bekas penjaga Windsor Forest yang menghantui pohon ek pada tengah malam di musim dingin.
claims.quote: Officially published versions of the play refer only to the tale of Herne as the ghost of a former Windsor Forest keeper who haunts a particular oak tree at midnight in the winter time.

claims.statement: Herne is read as a god of the hunt (Gott der Jagd) and lord of game (Herr des Wildes), perhaps a local Anglo-Saxon (Angelsachsen) god of Windsor Forest; some equate him with Cernunnos.
claims.statement_id: Herne ditafsirkan sebagai dewa perburuan (Gott der Jagd) dan penguasa satwa (Herr des Wildes), mungkin dewa lokal Anglo-Saxon (Angelsachsen) di Windsor Forest; ada yang menyamakannya dengan Cernunnos.
claims.quote: Herne wird als Gott der Jagd und Herr des Wildes gedeutet. Vermutungen zufolge war Herne eine Lokalgottheit der Angelsachsen im Windsor Forest, einem Wald, der sich über die heutigen Grafschaften Berkshire, Buckinghamshire und Hampshire erstreckte. Man nimmt an, Herne sei identisch mit Cernunnos

claims.statement: Others see Herne as a form of the Germanic god (germanischen Gottes) Odin in the Wild Hunt (Wilden Jagd).
claims.statement_id: Sebaliknya, ada yang melihat Herne sebagai wujud dewa Jermanik (germanischen Gottes) Odin dalam Perburuan Liar (Wilden Jagd).
claims.quote: Konträr dazu sieht man in Herne eine Erscheinungsform des germanischen Gottes Odin bei der Wilden Jagd.

claims.statement: Nodens (from dative Nodenti or Nodonti) is a Celtic healing god of Ancient Britain; plaques at Lydney Park (Gloucestershire) link him with dogs.
claims.statement_id: Nodens (dari datif Nodenti atau Nodonti) dewa penyembuh Kelt (Celtic) Britania kuno (Ancient Britain); plakat di Lydney Park (Gloucestershire) mengaitkannya dengan anjing.
claims.quote: (reconstructed from the dative Nodenti or Nodonti) is a Celtic healing god worshipped in Ancient Britain. Although no physical depiction of him has survived, votive plaques found in a shrine at Lydney Park (Gloucestershire) indicate his connection with dogs, a beast associated with healing symbolism in antiquity.

claims.statement: The deity is known at only one other place, Cockersand Moss (Lancashire).
claims.statement_id: Dewa ini hanya dikenal di satu tempat lain, Cockersand Moss (Lancashire).
claims.quote: The deity is known in only one other location, in Cockersand Moss (Lancashire).

claims.statement: He was equated with the Roman Mars as healer; his name is cognate with the Irish Nuada and Welsh Nudd.
claims.statement_id: Ia disamakan dengan Mars (Roman) sebagai penyembuh; namanya sekerabat dengan Nuada (Irish, Irlandia) dan Nudd (Welsh, Wales).
claims.quote: He was equated on most inscriptions with the Roman god Mars (as a healer rather than as a warrior) and associated in a curse with Silvanus (a hunting-god). His name is cognate with that of later Celtic mythological figures, such as the Irish Nuada and the Welsh Nudd.

claims.statement: J. R. R. Tolkien investigated the Latin inscription; it may have shaped Middle-earth and Celebrimbor, whose name like Airgetlám means Silver-hand.
claims.statement_id: J. R. R. Tolkien menyelidiki prasasti Latin (Latin) itu; mungkin memengaruhi Middle-earth dan Celebrimbor, yang namanya seperti Airgetlám berarti Tangan Perak (Silver-hand).
claims.quote: The philologist and author J. R. R. Tolkien was invited to investigate the Latin inscription, and scholars have noted several likely influences on his Middle-earth fantasy writings, including the Elvish smith, maker of Rings of Power, Celebrimbor, whose name, like that of Nuada's epithet Airgetlám, means 'Silver-hand'.

claims.statement: Nodens appears in Arthur Machen's works and H. P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos.
claims.statement_id: Nodens muncul dalam karya Arthur Machen dan Cthulhu Mythos H. P. Lovecraft.
claims.quote: Nodens appears, too, in the works of Arthur Machen, as well as H. P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos.

claims.statement: Nodons (Nodens) is an old Celtic god (altkeltischer Gott) of Britain (Britannien), god of healing (Heilung), water (Wassers) and dogs (Hunde).
claims.statement_id: Nodons (Nodens) dewa Kelt kuno (altkeltischer Gott) di Britania (Britannien), dewa penyembuhan (Heilung), air (Wassers), dan anjing (Hunde).
claims.quote: Nodons, auch Nodens, ist ein in Britannien verehrter altkeltischer Gott. Er wird als Gott der Heilung, des Wassers und der Hunde beschrieben.

claims.statement: At Lydney Park were found offerings naming Nodons, a bronze (Bronzestatue) of a four-horse (vier Pferden) chariot, and a monument of a man killing a fish (Fisch).
claims.statement_id: Di Lydney Park ditemukan persembahan bernama Nodons, patung perunggu (Bronzestatue) kereta empat kuda (vier Pferden), dan monumen lelaki membunuh ikan (Fisch).
claims.quote: Neben Votivgaben, die den Namen Nodons tragen, wurde eine Bronzestatue gefunden, die einen von vier Pferden gezogenen Wagen darstellt, auf dem ein Mann mit einer Keule steht, sowie ein Monument, auf dem ein Mann einen Fisch tötet.

claims.statement: Sulis was the deity of Bath's thermal spring, worshipped by the Romano-British as Sulis Minerva, a life-giving mother goddess and agent of curses.
claims.statement_id: Sulis dewi mata air panas Bath, dipuja orang Romawi-Britania (Romano-British) sebagai Sulis Minerva, dewi ibu pemberi hidup dan pelaksana kutukan; Kelt (Celtic) di Britania Raya (Great Britain).
claims.quote: Sulis was a deity worshipped at the thermal spring of Bath. She was worshipped by the Romano-British as Sulis Minerva, whose votive objects and inscribed lead tablets suggest that she was conceived of both as a nourishing, life-giving mother goddess and as an effective agent of curses invoked by her votaries.

claims.statement: Linguists increasingly see the name as cognate with Old Irish súil, eye.
claims.statement_id: Banyak ahli bahasa menganggap nama itu sekerabat dengan Irlandia Kuno (Old Irish) súil, mata.
claims.quote: an emerging consensus among linguists regards the name as cognate with Old Irish súil ("eye, sight").

claims.statement: Sul was standard until a 1979 curse tablet from Aquae Sulis read dea Sulis, the only nominative instance.
claims.statement_id: Sul bacaan baku sampai ditemukan lempeng kutukan 1979 di Aquae Sulis berisi dea Sulis, satu-satunya bentuk nominatif.
claims.quote: Sul was the standard rendering until the 1979 discovery of a lead curse tablet from the sacred spring at Aquae Sulis which contained the phrase "dea Sulis," which is the first and only example preserving the deity's name in the nominative case.

claims.statement: The Romans called Bath Aquae Sulis, the waters of Sulis; she was likely a healing goddess.
claims.statement_id: Orang Romawi (Romans) menamai Bath Aquae Sulis, perairan Sulis; ia kemungkinan dewi penyembuh.
claims.quote: Sulis was the local goddess of the thermal springs that still feed the spa baths at Bath, which the Romans called Aquae Sulis ("the waters of Sulis"). Sulis was likely venerated as a healing divinity, whose sacred hot springs could cure physical or spiritual suffering and illness.

claims.statement: According to Miranda Green the cult of Sulis at Bath lasted to the mid-fourth century CE.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Miranda Green, pemujaan Sulis di Bath aktif hingga pertengahan abad keempat Masehi (CE).
claims.quote: According to scholar Miranda Green, the cult of Sulis at Bath was active until the mid-fourth century CE.

claims.statement: Sulis is a sun and healing goddess of the British Celts, equated with Minerva under the Interpretatio Romana.
claims.statement_id: Sulis dewi matahari dan penyembuhan (Sonnen- und Heil-Gottheit) Kelt Britania (britannischen Kelten), disamakan dengan Minerva menurut Interpretatio Romana.
claims.quote: Sulis ist eine Sonnen- und Heil-Gottheit der britannischen Kelten. Nach der Interpretatio Romana wurde sie der Göttin Minerva gleichgesetzt.

claims.statement: Over 12,500 Roman and 18 Celtic coins were found in the reservoir.
claims.statement_id: Di kolam ditemukan lebih dari 12.500 koin Romawi (Roman) dan 18 koin Kelt (Celtic); juga sekitar 130 lempeng kutukan.
claims.quote: with over 12,500 Roman coins and 18 Celtic coins having been found in the reservoir.

claims.statement: About 130 curse tablets, mostly to Sulis, were found in the sacred spring at Bath's Roman baths.
claims.statement_id: Sekitar 130 lempeng kutukan, kebanyakan untuk Sulis, ditemukan di mata air suci pemandian Romawi (Roman) di Bath.
claims.quote: About 130 curse tablets, mostly addressed to Sulis, have been found in the sacred spring at the Roman baths in Bath.

claims.statement: Boann (Boand) is the Irish goddess of the River Boyne (Bóinn) in Meath; per the Lebor Gabála Érenn and Táin Bó Fraích, sister of Befind, daughter of Delbáeth son of Elada of the Tuatha Dé Danann; husband Nechtan or Elcmar; mother of Aengus by the Dagda.
claims.statement_id: Boann (Boand) dewi Irlandia (Irish) Sungai Boyne (River Boyne, Bóinn) di Meath; menurut Lebor Gabála Érenn dan Táin Bó Fraích saudari Befind, putri Delbáeth putra Elada dari Tuatha Dé Danann; suaminya Nechtan atau Elcmar; ibu Aengus dengan Dagda (the Dagda); di Irlandia (Ireland).
claims.quote: Boann or Boand is the Irish goddess of the River Boyne (Bóinn), an important river in Ireland's historical province of Meath. According to the Lebor Gabála Érenn and Táin Bó Fraích she was the sister of Befind and daughter of Delbáeth, son of Elada, of the Tuatha Dé Danann. Her husband is variously Nechtan or Elcmar.

claims.statement: In the dinsenchas her name is read as white cow.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dinsenchas namanya ditafsirkan sebagai sapi putih (white cow).
claims.quote: Her name is interpreted as "white cow" (Irish: bó fhionn ; Old Irish: bó find ) in the dinsenchas, where she is also called "White Boand".

claims.statement: The Dagda made the sun stand still so Elcmar would not notice; nine months passed and Boann bore Aengus, at Brú na Bóinne.
claims.statement_id: Dagda membuat matahari berhenti agar Elcmar tak sadar; sembilan bulan berlalu dan Boann melahirkan Aengus, di Brú na Bóinne.
claims.quote: To hide the pregnancy from Elcmar, the Dagda casts a spell on him, making "the sun stand still" so he will not notice the passing of time. Meanwhile, nine months pass and Boann gives birth to Aengus.

claims.statement: Per the Dindsenchas, though Nechtan forbade it, Boann approached the Well of Segais (Connla's Well), ringed by nine magic hazels.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Dindsenchas, meski dilarang Nechtan, Boann mendatangi Well of Segais (Connla's Well) yang dikelilingi sembilan pohon hazel ajaib.
claims.quote: Though forbidden to by her husband, Nechtan, Boann approached the magical Well of Segais (also known as the Connla's Well), which was surrounded, according to the legend, by nine magic hazel-trees.

claims.statement: Boann circled the well tuathal; the waters surged to the sea creating the Boyne, and she lost an arm, leg, eye and then her life.
claims.statement_id: Boann mengitari sumur itu tuathal; air meluap ke laut menciptakan Boyne, dan ia kehilangan lengan, kaki, mata, lalu nyawanya.
claims.quote: Boann challenged the power of the well by walking around it tuathal; this caused the waters to surge up violently and rush down to the sea, creating the Boyne. In this catastrophe, she was swept along in the rushing waters, and lost an arm, leg and eye, and ultimately her life, in the flood.

claims.statement: Bóann is a figure of Irish Celtic myth, river goddess (Flussgöttin) of the Boyne; she profaned Nechtan's secret spring in the Síd by walking against the sun (tuaithbel), drowned, and the Boyne arose.
claims.statement_id: Bóann tokoh mitologi Kelt Irlandia (Irlands), dewi sungai (Flussgöttin) Boyne; ia menodai mata air rahasia Nechtan di Síd dengan berjalan melawan matahari (tuaithbel), tenggelam, dan Boyne pun tercipta.
claims.quote: ist eine Figur der keltischen Mythologie Irlands und dort die Flussgöttin des Boyne. Die Mythologie erzählt, sie habe die geheime Quelle ihres Gatten Nechtan im Síd durch Herumgehen gegen den Sonnenlauf (tuaithbel) entweiht, worauf sie darin ertrunken sei und der Boyne entstand.

claims.statement: The land around the pre-Celtic mounds of Newgrange in the Boyne valley (Boyne-Tal) is called Brug na Boinne after her.
claims.statement_id: Daerah sekitar makam prasejarah (vorkeltischen Grabhügel) Newgrange di lembah Boyne (Boyne-Tal) dinamai Brug na Boinne menurut dia.
claims.quote: Die Gegend um die vorkeltischen Grabhügel bei Newgrange im Boyne-Tal wird nach ihr Brug na Boinne genannt.

claims.statement: A hobgoblin is a household spirit of English folklore, once helpful, since Christianity seen as mischievous; Shakespeare calls Puck in A Midsummer Night's Dream a hobgoblin.
claims.statement_id: Hobgoblin roh rumah tangga cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), dulu penolong, sejak Kristen (Christianity) dianggap jahil; Shakespeare menyebut Puck dalam A Midsummer Night's Dream hobgoblin; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: A hobgoblin is a household spirit, appearing in English folklore, once considered helpful, but which since the spread of Christianity has often been considered mischievous. Shakespeare identifies the character of Puck in his A Midsummer Night's Dream as a hobgoblin.

claims.statement: The term hobgoblin comes from hob; recorded about 1530.
claims.statement_id: Istilah hobgoblin berasal dari hob; tercatat sekitar 1530.
claims.quote: The term "hobgoblin" comes from "hob". The earliest known use of the word can be traced to about 1530, although it was likely in use for some time prior to that.

claims.statement: Hobgoblins are small hairy men, kin of brownies, doing house chores while the family sleeps.
claims.statement_id: Hobgoblin lelaki kecil berbulu, kerabat brownie, mengerjakan tugas rumah saat keluarga tidur.
claims.quote: Hobgoblins seem to be small, hairy little men who, like their close relatives the brownies, are often found within human dwellings, doing odd jobs around the house while the family is asleep. Such chores are typically small tasks like dusting and ironing.

claims.statement: Hobgoblins like pranks more than brownies and seem able to shapeshift, as in a monologue by Puck.
claims.statement_id: Hobgoblin lebih gemar bercanda daripada brownie dan tampaknya bisa berubah wujud, seperti monolog Puck.
claims.quote: While brownies are more peaceful creatures, hobgoblins are more fond of practical jokes. They also seem to be able to shapeshift, as seen in one of Puck's monologues in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

claims.statement: Hobgoblins are easily annoyed and can be dangerous; giving them clothing often banishes them forever.
claims.statement_id: Hobgoblin mudah tersinggung, bisa jahil, menakutkan, berbahaya; diberi pakaian membuat mereka pergi selamanya.
claims.quote: Like other fairy folk, hobgoblins are easily annoyed. They can be mischievous, frightening, and even dangerous. Attempts to give them clothing will often banish them forever

claims.statement: According to Elizabeth Mary Wright, dobby is another term for hobgoblin in Lancashire and Yorkshire.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Elizabeth Mary Wright, dobby sebutan lain hobgoblin di Lancashire dan Yorkshire.
claims.quote: Dobby is another term for hobgoblin in Lancashire and Yorkshire according to the folklorist Elizabeth Mary Wright, especially one that is a relentless prankster.

claims.statement: The hobgoblin is a legendary British (britannique) creature, friendly, living in country homes; later sometimes an evil spirit confused with the goblin (gobelin).
claims.statement_id: Hobgoblin makhluk legenda Britania (britannique), ramah, tinggal di rumah pedesaan; kemudian kadang dianggap roh jahat dan dicampur dengan goblin (gobelin).
claims.quote: Le hobgoblin est une créature légendaire du folklore britannique. Il est décrit comme amical et parfois serviable, vivant dans les habitations des campagnes. Dans le folklore anglais plus tardif, il est parfois décrit comme un esprit diabolique et confondu avec le gobelin.

claims.statement: Hob may come from Welsh (gallois) hob to hop, or English (anglais) hob hearth.
claims.statement_id: Hob mungkin dari kata Wales (gallois) hob melompat, atau kata Inggris (anglais) hob perapian.
claims.quote: Une hypothèse dérive hobgoblin du gallois hob, « sautiller », et coblyn « gobelin » ; ce « gobelin sautillant » pouvant être rattaché au personnage légendaire de Puck. Ou bien Hob dérive de l'anglais hob, « foyer »

claims.statement: Hob is a diminutive of Robert/Robin, perhaps linking the hobgoblin to Robin Goodfellow (Puck).
claims.statement_id: Hob nama kecil Robert/Robin, mungkin mengaitkan hobgoblin dengan Robin Goodfellow (Puck).
claims.quote: De même Hob est le diminutif de Robert/Robin, rattachant peut-être le hobgoblin au Robin Goodfellow (Puck).

claims.statement: Each-uisge (Scottish Gaelic) means water horse; an Irish and Scottish water spirit, each-uisce/aughisky/ech-ushkya in Ireland, cabbyl-ushtey on the Isle of Man; horse-shaped, like the kelpie but more vicious.
claims.statement_id: Each-uisge (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic) berarti kuda air; roh air Irlandia (Irish) dan Skotlandia (Scottish), each-uisce/aughisky/ech-ushkya di Irlandia (Ireland), cabbyl-ushtey di Isle of Man; berwujud kuda, mirip kelpie tetapi lebih ganas.
claims.quote: literally "water horse") is a water spirit in Irish and Scottish folklore, spelled as the each-uisce (anglicized as aughisky or ech-ushkya) in Ireland and cabbyl-ushtey on the Isle of Man. It usually takes the form of a horse, and is similar to the kelpie but far more vicious.

claims.statement: Katharine Briggs called it perhaps the fiercest and most dangerous water-horse.
claims.statement_id: Katharine Briggs menyebutnya mungkin kuda air paling ganas dan berbahaya.
claims.quote: has been described as "perhaps the fiercest and most dangerous of all the water-horses" by the folklorist Katharine Briggs.

claims.statement: The each-uisge lives in the sea and lochs of the Scottish Highlands and shapeshifts into a horse, pony, handsome man or giant bird.
claims.statement_id: Each-uisge tinggal di laut dan loch air asin dan tawar di Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highlands), dan berubah wujud jadi kuda, poni, lelaki tampan, atau burung raksasa.
claims.quote: the each-uisge lives in the sea, sea lochs, and fresh water lochs. The each-uisge is a shape-shifter, disguising itself as a fine horse, pony, a handsome man or an enormous bird such as a boobrie.

claims.statement: Its skin turns adhesive; it drags the victim to the deepest loch and eats all but the liver.
claims.statement_id: Kulitnya jadi lengket, membawa korban ke bagian loch terdalam, memakan semuanya kecuali hati.
claims.quote: the each-uisge's skin becomes adhesive and the creature immediately goes to the deepest part of the loch with its victim. After the victim has drowned, the each-uisge tears them apart and devours the entire body except for the liver, which floats to the surface.

claims.statement: In human form it is known by water weeds or sand and mud in its hair.
claims.statement_id: Dalam wujud manusia dikenali dari rumput air atau pasir dan lumpur di rambutnya.
claims.quote: In its human form it is said to appear as a handsome man, and can be recognised as a mythological creature only by the water weeds or profuse sand and mud in its hair.

claims.statement: Each Uisge is a shapeshifting creature of the fairy realm (Feenreiches) or Otherworld (Anderswelt), living in the lochs (Lochs) and coasts of Scotland (Schottlands), one of the most dangerous water monsters of the Scottish-Celtic legend world (schottisch-keltischen Sagenwelt).
claims.statement_id: Each Uisge makhluk pengubah wujud dari dunia peri (Feenreiches) atau Dunia Lain (Anderswelt), menghuni loch (Lochs) dan perairan pantai Skotlandia (Schottlands), salah satu monster air paling berbahaya di dunia legenda Kelt Skotlandia (schottisch-keltischen Sagenwelt).
claims.quote: ist im schottischen Volksglauben eine gestaltwandelnde Kreatur des Feenreiches oder der Anderswelt, die der Sage nach die Lochs und Küstengewässer Schottlands bewohnen soll und als eines der gefährlichsten Wassermonster der schottisch-keltischen Sagenwelt gilt.

claims.statement: Each Uisge is easily confused with the Irish (irischen, Irlands) Aughisky, with the same powers but living in still waters.
claims.statement_id: Each Uisge mudah tertukar dengan Aughisky Irlandia (irischen, Irlands) yang berkemampuan sama tetapi menghuni perairan tergenang.
claims.quote: Das Each Uisge kann leicht mit dem irischen Aughisky verwechselt werden, dem die Erzählungen dieselben Fähigkeiten und eine ähnliche Verhaltensweise zusprechen, das aber die stehenden Gewässer Irlands bewohnt haben soll.

claims.statement: A blacksmith from Raasay took revenge with large red-hot hooks and a roasted sheep as bait.
claims.statement_id: Pandai besi dari Raasay membalas dendam dengan kait besar membara dan umpan domba panggang.
claims.quote: In revenge the blacksmith and his son made a set of large hooks, in a forge they set up by the loch side. They then roasted a sheep and heated the hooks until they were red hot.

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Bukan makhluk: Enfield poltergeist adalah klaim aktivitas supranatural di rumah 284 Green Street, Enfield, London pada 1977–1979 yang berpusat pada dua kakak beradik Hodgson; sebagian penyelidik menemukan bukti kejadiannya dipalsukan. Artikelnya membahas peristiwa modern dan perdebatannya, bukan sosok makhluk cerita rakyat. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enfield_poltergeist).

claims.statement: In Nordic folklore, including the Northern Isles, hidden-folk: Faroese and Icelandic huldufólk, Norwegian huldrefolk; covering elves, wights, brownies (nisse), trolls.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Nordik (Nordic folklore), termasuk Northern Isles, hidden-folk: Faroe dan Islandia (Faroese and Icelandic) huldufólk, Norwegia (Norwegian) huldrefolk; mencakup elf, wight, brownie (nisse), troll; di Islandia dan Kepulauan Faroe.
claims.quote: In Nordic folklore, including the Northern Isles, hidden-folk (Faroese and Icelandic: huldufólk ; Norwegian: huldrefolk ),

claims.statement: Supernatural beings of nature, humanlike, in a parallel world, visible at will.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk gaib di alam, mirip manusia, hidup di dunia sejajar, bisa menampakkan diri sesuka hati.
claims.quote: They are supernatural beings that live in nature. They look and behave similarly to humans, but live in a parallel world. They can make themselves visible at will.

claims.statement: Konrad von Maurer cites a 19th-century Icelandic source: their philtrum is convex.
claims.statement_id: Konrad von Maurer mengutip sumber Islandia (Icelandic) abad ke-19: beda satu-satunya philtrum mereka cembung.
claims.quote: Konrad von Maurer cites a 19th-century Icelandic source claiming that the only visible difference between normal people and outwardly human-appearing huldufólk is, the latter have a convex rather than concave philtrum

claims.statement: In Faroese tales they dwell in mounds (also called Elves); Icelandic tales warn against throwing stones.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng Faroe (Faroese) mereka tinggal di gundukan (disebut juga Elves); dongeng Islandia (Icelandic) melarang melempar batu.
claims.quote: Their dwellings are in mounds, and they are also called Elves." Some Icelandic folk tales caution against throwing stones, as it may hit the hidden people.

claims.statement: Huldufólk was a synonym of álfar in the 19th century; Jón Árnason found álfar pejorative.
claims.statement_id: Huldufólk sinonim álfar (elf) pada abad ke-19; menurut Jón Árnason álfar merendahkan.
claims.quote: The term huldufólk was taken as a synonym of álfar (elves) in 19th-century Icelandic folklore. Jón Árnason found that the terms are synonymous, except álfar is a pejorative term.

claims.statement: Huldufólk means hidden people (peuple caché), beings of Icelandic (islandais) folklore: elves, trolls and invisible people in mountains and rocks, their towns the Álagablettur.
claims.statement_id: Huldufólk berarti orang tersembunyi (peuple caché), makhluk folklore Islandia (islandais): elf, troll, orang tak kasat mata di gunung dan batu, kota mereka Álagablettur; juga di Kepulauan Faroe.
claims.quote: terme islandais signifiant littéralement en français « peuple caché », est composé des créatures des légendes et croyances du folklore islandais. Il s'agit d'elfes, de trolls et de personnes invisibles qui vivent préférentiellement dans les montagnes et les rochers où ils construisent leurs villes, les Álagablettur.

claims.statement: A road at Kópavogur was reportedly planned to avoid destroying their home.
claims.statement_id: Jalan di Kópavogur konon dirancang agar tidak merusak tempat tinggal mereka.
claims.quote: citant notamment l'exemple d'un tracé de route qui aurait été étudié pour éviter de détruire leur lieu de vie à Kópavogur.

claims.statement: The Salmon of Knowledge (Irish An Bradán Feasa) is a creature of the Fenian Cycle, sometimes identified with Fintan mac Bóchra the Wise.
claims.statement_id: Salmon of Knowledge (Irlandia, Irish: An Bradán Feasa), makhluk Siklus Fenian (Fenian Cycle), kadang disamakan dengan Fintan mac Bóchra Sang Bijak (The Wise); di Irlandia.
claims.quote: The Salmon of Knowledge (Irish: An Bradán Feasa ) is a creature in the Fenian Cycle of Irish mythology, sometimes identified with the mythical seer Fintan mac Bóchra who was known as "The Wise" and was once transformed into a salmon.

claims.statement: In The Boyhood Deeds of Fionn, a salmon ate nine hazelnuts fallen into the Well of Wisdom and gained all the world's knowledge.
claims.statement_id: Dalam The Boyhood Deeds of Fionn, salmon biasa memakan sembilan buah hazel yang jatuh ke Well of Wisdom dan memperoleh seluruh pengetahuan dunia.
claims.quote: In the story, an ordinary salmon ate nine hazelnuts that fell into the Well of Wisdom (an Tobar Segais) from nine hazel trees that surrounded the well. By this act, the salmon gained all the world's knowledge. The first person to eat of its flesh would in turn gain this knowledge.

claims.statement: Finn Eces (Finegas) fished seven years and gave the fish to Fionn son of Cumhall to cook but not eat. Fionn mac Cumhaill.
claims.statement_id: Finn Eces (Finegas) memancing tujuh tahun, lalu memberi ikan kepada Fionn putra Cumhall untuk dimasak tanpa dimakan. Fionn mac Cumhaill.
claims.quote: The poet Finn Eces (or Finegas) spent seven years fishing for this salmon. Finally Finn caught the salmon and gave the fish to Fionn, his servant and son of Cumhall, with instructions to cook it but on no account eat any of it.

claims.statement: Fionn gained all knowledge, drew on it by biting his thumb, and became leader of the Fianna.
claims.statement_id: Fionn memperoleh seluruh pengetahuan, memanggilnya dengan menggigit ibu jari, dan menjadi pemimpin Fianna.
claims.quote: Fionn ate the salmon and in so doing gained all the knowledge of the world. For the rest of his life, Fionn could draw upon this knowledge merely by biting his thumb. The deep knowledge and wisdom gained from the Salmon of Knowledge allowed Fionn to become the leader of the Fianna

claims.statement: The Welsh Hanes Taliesin has a similar story about Taliesin.
claims.statement_id: Hanes Taliesin dari Wales (Welsh) memuat kisah serupa tentang Taliesin.
claims.quote: The Welsh Hanes Taliesin (16th c.) has a similar story of how the poet Taliesin received his wisdom, that also involves shape-shifting into the form of a fish.

claims.statement: The Saumon de la sagesse ate nine hazelnuts fallen into the Boyne or Shannon, grew enormous and knew everything.
claims.statement_id: Saumon de la sagesse memakan sembilan buah hazel yang jatuh ke Sungai Boyne atau Shannon, menjadi sangat besar dan tahu segalanya.
claims.quote: est à l'origine un saumon ordinaire, qui mange les neuf noisettes tombés de l'arbre du savoir dans le fleuve Boyne — ou parfois le Shannon. Ce faisant, le saumon devient énorme et acquiert tout le savoir du monde, devenant plus sage que les hommes.

claims.statement: Sirona was an ancient Celtic healing goddess of curative springs in eastern Gaul, the Germanies and the Danube provinces; consort of Apollo Grannus.
claims.statement_id: Sirona (Đirona/Dirona) dewi penyembuhan Kelt (Celtic) kuno, mata air penyembuh, dipuja di Galia (Gaul) timur, Germania (Germanies), provinsi Danube; pasangan Apollo Grannus; di Prancis dan Jerman.
claims.quote: was an ancient Celtic goddess of healing, associated with curative and thermal springs, worshipped in eastern Gaul, the Germanies and the Danube provinces. She is attested chiefly as the consort of Apollo under his healing surname Grannus

claims.statement: Her emblems are a snake and a bowl of eggs; no classical author names her.
claims.statement_id: Lambangnya ular dan semangkuk telur; tak ada pengarang klasik yang menyebutnya.
claims.quote: Her most distinctive attributes are the snake and a bowl of eggs, taken as emblems of healing and renewal. No classical author names her, the evidence being epigraphic and iconographic.

claims.statement: The name derives from the Proto-Indo-European word for star.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari kata Proto-Indo-Eropa (Proto-Indo-European) untuk bintang (star).
claims.quote: Most scholars derive its first element from the Proto-Indo-European word for 'star', *h₂ster, which gives Proto-Celtic *sterā-, so that the name means something like 'star (goddess)'.

claims.statement: Cult in the Germanies and eastern Gaul, upper Moselle (Treveri), Mainz; also Raetia, Noricum, Pannonia, Dacia and Rome.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan di Germania dan Galia timur, lembah Moselle hulu (Treveri), Mainz; juga Raetia, Noricum, Pannonia, Dacia, Roma (Rome).
claims.quote: Her cult was concentrated in the Germanies and eastern Gaul, above all in the valley of the upper Moselle, among the Treveri, and in the Mainz area. Dedications also come from the territories of the Aedui and the Leuci, and from further afield: the Danube provinces of Raetia, Noricum and Pannonia, the province of Dacia, and the city of Rome.

claims.statement: At Corseul in Brittany she is named Tsirona.
claims.statement_id: Di Corseul (Brittany) ia disebut Tsirona.
claims.quote: At Corseul in Brittany she is named Tsirona and is invoked together with the numen of the emperor, a pairing that points to her high standing.

claims.statement: Sirona (Đirona) was a Celtic goddess of healing (keltische Göttin der Heilung), equated with the Greek (griechischen) Hygieia, cult partner of Apollo Grannus.
claims.statement_id: Sirona (Đirona) dewi penyembuhan Kelt (keltische Göttin der Heilung), disamakan dengan dewi Yunani (griechischen) Hygieia, rekan pemujaan Apollo Grannus.
claims.quote: Sirona, auch Đirona, war eine keltische Göttin der Heilung. Sie wurde ikonographisch der griechischen Heilgöttin Hygieia gleichgesetzt. Sie ist häufig Kultgenossin des Apollo Grannus.

claims.statement: Sirona is known only from ancient votive inscriptions; no mythology survives.
claims.statement_id: Sirona hanya dikenal dari prasasti persembahan kuno; tak ada mitologi yang diwariskan.
claims.quote: Sirona ist ausschließlich aus antiken Weiheinschriften bekannt, eine Mythologie ist nicht überliefert.

claims.statement: A 2nd-century AD shrine of Apollo and Sirona was excavated at Hochscheid (Hunsrück).
claims.statement_id: Tempat suci Apollo dan Sirona abad ke-2 Masehi digali di Hochscheid (Hunsrück).
claims.quote: Ein Heiligtum des Apollo und der Sirona des 2. Jahrhunderts n. Chr. wurde in Hochscheid (Hunsrück) ausgegraben.

claims.statement: Brân the Blessed (Welsh Bendigeidfran/Brân Fendigaidd, Blessed Crow) is a giant king of Britain in the Welsh Triads and the Second Branch of the Mabinogi, Branwen ferch Llŷr; son of Llŷr and Penarddun, brother of Brânwen, Manawydan, Nisien, Efnysien.
claims.statement_id: Brân the Blessed (Wales, Welsh: Bendigeidfran/Brân Fendigaidd, Gagak yang Diberkati) raksasa dan raja Britania (Britain), dalam Welsh Triads dan Cabang Kedua (Second Branch) Mabinogi, Branwen ferch Llŷr; putra Llŷr dan Penarddun, saudara Brânwen (Branwen), Manawydan, Nisien, Efnysien.
claims.quote: Brân the Blessed (Welsh: Bendigeidfran or Brân Fendigaidd, literally "Blessed Crow") is a giant and king of Britain in Welsh mythology. He appears in several of the Welsh Triads, but his most significant role is in the Second Branch of the Mabinogi, Branwen ferch Llŷr. He is a son of Llŷr and Penarddun, and the brother of Brânwen, Manawydan, Nisien and Efnysien.

claims.statement: Brân means crow or raven; he is considered a sea god and god of poetry and bards.
claims.statement_id: Brân berarti gagak; ia dianggap dewa laut serta dewa puisi dan bard.
claims.quote: The name "Brân" in Welsh is usually translated as crow or raven. He is considered a sea-god as well as a god of poetry and bards.

claims.statement: In the Mabinogion, Brân gives Matholwch a magic cauldron that revives the dead after Efnysien's insult.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mabinogion, Brân memberi Matholwch kuali ajaib penghidup orang mati; penghinaan oleh Efnysien; Irlandia (Irish).
claims.quote: Matholwch is deeply offended until Brân offers him compensation in the form of a magic cauldron that can restore the dead to life.

claims.statement: Brân wades across the Irish Sea to rescue Branwen. (Ireland)
claims.statement_id: Brân mengarungi Laut Irlandia (Irish Sea) untuk menyelamatkan Branwen. (Ireland)
claims.quote: Brân wades across the Irish Sea to rescue her with his brother Manawydan and a huge host of warriors

claims.statement: Brân has his head cut off and taken to Britain; it speaks for seven years at Harlech.
claims.statement_id: Brân menyuruh memenggal kepalanya dan membawanya ke Britania; kepala itu berbicara selama tujuh tahun di Harlech.
claims.quote: The survivors are told by a mortally wounded Brân to cut off his head and to return it to Britain. For seven years the seven survivors stay in Harlech, where they are entertained by Brân's head, which continues to speak.

claims.statement: The head is buried at the Gwynfryn, the White Hill (perhaps the Tower of London), facing France.
claims.statement_id: Kepala dikubur di Gwynfryn, Bukit Putih (White Hill, diduga Tower of London), menghadap Prancis (France).
claims.quote: they take the now silent head to the Gwynfryn, the "White Hill" (thought to be the location where the Tower of London now stands), where they bury it facing France so as to ward off invasion.

claims.statement: Bran der Gesegnete is a giant (Riese) of Welsh legend (walisischen Sagen); Bran means crow (Krähe) or raven (Rabe).
claims.statement_id: Bran der Gesegnete raksasa (Riese) dari legenda Wales (walisischen Sagen); Bran berarti gagak (Krähe) atau raven (Rabe).
claims.quote: ist ein Riese aus den walisischen Sagen. Aus dem Walisischen übersetzt bedeutet Bran „Krähe“, oft wird er jedoch auch „Rabe“ genannt.

claims.statement: Crow and raven are often synonyms for warrior (Krieger).
claims.statement_id: Gagak dan raven sering menjadi sinonim untuk pejuang (Krieger).
claims.quote: Beides ist häufig ein Synonym für „Krieger“.

claims.statement: The cat-sìth (Scottish Gaelic; Irish cat sí) is a fairy of Celtic myth, a large black cat with a white spot walking on its hind legs, in the Scottish Highlands. More common in Scotland than Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Cat-sìth (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic; Irlandia, Irish cat sí) peri mitologi Kelt (Celtic), kucing hitam besar berbercak putih, berjalan dengan kaki belakang, di Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highlands); di Inggris Raya dan Irlandia. Lebih umum di Skotlandia (Scotland) daripada Irlandia (Ireland).
claims.quote: is a fairy creature from Celtic mythology, said to resemble a large black cat with a white spot on its chest that walks on its hind legs. Legend has it that the spectral cat haunts the Scottish Highlands. The legends surrounding this creature are more common in Scottish folklore, but a few occur in Irish.

claims.statement: Some held it a witch able to become a cat nine times.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian menganggapnya penyihir yang bisa menjadi kucing sembilan kali.
claims.quote: Some common folklore suggested that the cat-sìth was not a fairy, but a witch that could transform into a cat nine times.

claims.statement: As large as a dog, back arched and bristles erect.
claims.statement_id: Sebesar anjing, punggung melengkung dan bulu tegak; mungkin terinspirasi kucing Kellas.
claims.quote: It is described as being as large as a dog and chooses to display itself with its back arched and bristles erect.

claims.statement: The cat-sìth was believed to steal souls of the newly dead by crossing over the body; guarded in the Late Wake (Fèill Fhadalach).
claims.statement_id: Cat-sìth diyakini mencuri jiwa orang baru meninggal dengan melangkahi jenazah; dijaga dalam Late Wake (Fèill Fhadalach).
claims.quote: The cat-sìth were believed to steal the souls of the recently deceased that hadn't gone to the land of the dead. This would happen by a cat-sìth crossing over a new dead body.

claims.statement: At Samhain milk was left out for luck; otherwise it dried up the cows' milk.
claims.statement_id: Saat Samhain diberi susu untuk keberuntungan; jika tidak, susu sapi dikeringkan; di Skotlandia.
claims.quote: Around Samhain, it was custom to leave out a saucer of milk for them. If you did, your household would receive good luck for the year. If you didn't, the cat-sìth would return the favor and dry up the milk of the house's cows.

claims.statement: People kept a vigil called the Late Wake or Fèill Fhadalach (Irish Gaelic).
claims.statement_id: Orang berjaga dalam vigili Late Wake atau Fèill Fhadalach (Irish Gaelic).
claims.quote: To avoid the soul being taken during this period, people would stay to watch the body in a vigil called the Late Wake or Fèill Fhadalach in Irish Gaelic.

claims.statement: Cait Sith is a figure of Celtic myth (keltischen Mythologie), a large black cat in the Highlands; linked to the Cu Sith (Cù-sìth).
claims.statement_id: Cait Sith tokoh mitologi Kelt (keltischen Mythologie), kucing hitam besar di Highlands; terkait Cu Sith (Cù-sìth).
claims.quote: ist eine Sagengestalt der keltischen Mythologie. Es handelt sich um eine große schwarze Katze, die in den Highlands leben soll.

claims.statement: Cait Sith usually means no harm but can turn wild if surprised or threatened; name means fairy cat (Feenkatze).
claims.statement_id: Cait Sith biasanya tidak mencelakai, tetapi bisa buas bila dikejutkan atau diancam; nama berarti kucing peri (Feenkatze).
claims.quote: Die Cait Sith ist üblicherweise nicht darauf aus, dem Menschen zu schaden. Jedoch, sollte man sie alleine in abgelegenen Orten überraschen oder sie bedrohen, dann kann sie sehr wild und gefährlich werden.

claims.statement: The legend is thought to come from sightings of the Kellas cat (Kellas-Katze).
claims.statement_id: Sagenya diduga dari pengamatan kucing Kellas (Kellas-Katze, Kellas cat).
claims.quote: Es wird vermutet, dass die Sage von Beobachtungen der Kellas-Katze herrührt.

claims.statement: In Irish mythology Clíodhna (Clídna, Clíodna, Clíona, Cleena) is a Queen of the Banshees of the Tuatha Dé Danann; Clíodna of Carrigcleena rules the sióga of South Munster (Desmond).
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Irlandia (Irish), Clíodhna (Clídna, Clíodna, Clíona, Cleena) Ratu Banshee (Queen of the Banshees) Tuatha Dé Danann; Clíodna dari Carrigcleena memerintah sióga di South Munster (Desmond); di Irlandia.
claims.quote: In Irish mythology, Clíodhna (Clídna, Clíodna, Clíona, sometimes anglicised to Cleena) is a Queen of the Banshees of the Tuatha Dé Danann. Clíodna of Carrigcleena is the potent banshee that rules as queen over the sióga (fairies) of South Munster, or Desmond.

claims.statement: In some myths she is a goddess of love and beauty, patron of County Cork, with three birds whose song heals.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian mitos ia dewi cinta dan kecantikan, pelindung County Cork, dengan tiga burung yang nyanyiannya menyembuhkan.
claims.quote: In some Irish myths, Clíodhna is a goddess of love and beauty, and the patron of County Cork. She is said to have three brightly coloured birds who eat apples from an otherworldly tree and whose sweet song heals sickness.

claims.statement: Her palace was in rocks near Mallow, Carrig-Cleena; Munster peasants saw her as benefactor.
claims.statement_id: Istananya di tumpukan batu dekat Mallow, Carrig-Cleena; petani Munster menganggapnya pelindung.
claims.quote: She had her palace in the heart of a pile of rocks, 5 mi (8.0 km) from Mallow, which is still commonly known by the name of Carrig-Cleena, and numerous legends about her are told among the Munster peasantry who considered her their benefactor.

claims.statement: The legend of Cleena's Wave is in the Acallam na Senórach; Ciabham was son of the King of Ulster.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Cleena's Wave tercatat dalam Acallam na Senórach; Ciabham putra raja Ulster (King of Ulster).
claims.quote: This legend is recorded in Acallam na Senórach ("Colloquy of the Ancients"), longest-surviving work of medieval Irish literature. During the time of the Fianna lived Ciabham of the Curling Hair, son of the King of Ulster.

claims.statement: They reached Tír Tairngire, Manannan's land; the druid Gebann's daughter was Cleena.
claims.statement_id: Mereka tiba di Tír Tairngire, negeri Manannan; putri druid Gebann bernama Cleena.
