claims.quote: They then reached Tír Tairngire ("the land of promise"), an otherworldly land ruled by Manannan their king. Ciabham is entertained at a feast within Manannan's city. The chief druid Gebann had a daughter named Cleena of the Fair Hair.

claims.statement: Music lulled Cleena asleep and a great wave swept her away; the spot is Tonn Chlíodhna, Clíodhna's Wave, near Glandore.
claims.statement_id: Musik membuat Cleena tertidur, ombak besar menyapunya; tempat itu Tonn Chlíodhna, Ombak Clíodhna (Clíodhna's Wave), dekat Glandore; di pantai Irlandia (Irish).
claims.quote: One of them treacherously played music which caused Cleena to fall asleep. Then a great wave came and swept her away. The place was then called Tonn Chlíodhna, "Clíodhna's Wave", which is near Glandore harbour.

claims.statement: Cliodhna is seen as a Banshee, one of the Túatha Dé Danann, and a figure of the Celtic Otherworld (Keltischen Anderswelt).
claims.statement_id: Cliodhna dipandang sebagai Banshee, Túatha Dé Danann, dan sosok Dunia Lain Kelt (Keltischen Anderswelt).
claims.quote: Cliodhna wird als Banshee, als Túatha Dé Danann und als Gestalt aus der Keltischen Anderswelt gesehen.

claims.statement: Cormac Laidir Mac Carthy, builder of Blarney Castle, asked the goddess (Göttin) for help and was told to kiss the first stone he saw.
claims.statement_id: Cormac Laidir Mac Carthy, pembangun Blarney Castle, meminta bantuan dewi (Göttin) itu dan disuruh mencium batu pertama yang dilihatnya.
claims.quote: Einer anderen Legende nach rief Cormac Laidir Mac Carthy, der Erbauer des Blarney Castle, die Göttin um Hilfe bei einem Rechtsstreit an. Die wies ihn an, den ersten Stein, den er morgens sah, zu küssen.

claims.statement: Coventina was a Romano-British goddess of wells and springs, known from inscriptions in Northumberland, England, near Carrawburgh on Hadrian's Wall; perhaps also Hispania and Narbonensis.
claims.statement_id: Coventina dewi Romawi-Britania (Romano-British) sumur dan mata air, dari prasasti di Northumberland, Inggris (England), dekat Carrawburgh di Tembok Hadrianus (Hadrian's Wall); mungkin juga di Hispania dan Narbonensis.
claims.quote: Coventina was a Romano-British goddess of wells and springs. She is known from multiple inscriptions at one site in Northumberland, England, an area surrounding a wellspring near Carrawburgh on Hadrian's Wall. It is possible that other inscriptions, two from Hispania and one from Narbonensis, refer to Coventina, but this is disputed.

claims.statement: In 1879 dedications were found in a walled area around the spring called Coventina's Well.
claims.statement_id: Tahun 1879 persembahan ditemukan di area berdinding mata air Coventina's Well.
claims.quote: In 1879, dedications to Coventina and votive deposits were found in a walled area which had been built to contain the outflow from a spring now called "Coventina's Well".

claims.statement: The well held 13,487 coins from Mark Anthony to Gratian, a relief of three nymphs, ten altars to Coventina and Minerva.
claims.statement_id: Isi sumur: 13.487 koin dari Mark Anthony hingga Gratian, relief tiga nimfa, sepuluh altar untuk Coventina dan Minerva.
claims.quote: The contents of the well included 13,487 coins from Mark Anthony to Gratian, a relief of three water nymphs, the head of a male statue, two dedication slabs to the goddess Coventina, ten altars to Coventina and Minerva, two clay incense burners, and a wide range of votive objects.

claims.statement: Worship ended abruptly around 388, perhaps due to Theodosius I's anti-pagan edicts.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan berakhir mendadak sekitar 388, mungkin karena dekret anti-pagan Theodosius I.
claims.quote: Evidence from coin hoards and stones which covered them and those also blocking the well suggest a fairly abrupt end around 388, perhaps due to events linked to anti-pagan edicts of Theodosius I.

claims.statement: Altars show Coventina as a Roman nymph; one in triple form or with two attendants.
claims.statement_id: Altar menggambarkan Coventina sebagai nimfa Romawi (Roman); satu dalam wujud tiga atau dengan dua pendamping.
claims.quote: Excavation of the site revealed several inscribed altars, some with depictions of Coventina in typical Roman nymph form: reclining, partially clothed and associated with water. On one, Coventina is either depicted in triple form or with two attendants.

claims.statement: Coventina was a healing and spring goddess (Heil- und Quellgöttin) of British myth, worshipped at Hadrian's Wall (Hadrianswall).
claims.statement_id: Coventina dewi penyembuhan dan mata air (Heil- und Quellgöttin) mitologi Britania (britannischen), dipuja di Tembok Hadrianus (Hadrianswall); Kelt.
claims.quote: Coventina war in der britannischen Mythologie eine Heil- und Quellgöttin, die am Hadrianswall verehrt wurde.

claims.statement: Legionaries (Legionäre) on Hadrian's Wall built Coventina a shrine near the fort of Brocolitia (Carrawburgh).
claims.statement_id: Para legiuner (Legionäre) di Tembok Hadrianus membangun tempat suci untuk Coventina dekat benteng Brocolitia (Carrawburgh).
claims.quote: Für Coventina errichteten die am Hadrianswall stationierten Legionäre ein Heiligtum beim Kastell Brocolitia (Carrawburgh, Northumberland).
